Topics.TitleEn: Data Seeding, Database First (Scaffold-DbContext) & Raw SQL / Stored Procs
Topics.TitleAr: زراعة البيانات Seeding والـ Database First واستدعاء Raw SQL و Stored Procedures
Topics.SummaryAr:
• **Data Seeding**: (1) `HasData(...)` داخل Migrations (مناسب للبيانات الثابتة ولازم تحط الـ PK بإيدك!) (2) Custom Startup Seeder / JSON File (للباسووردات المشفرة والبيانات الديناميكية).
• **Database First**: `Scaffold-DbContext "Server=..." Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer -OutputDir Models` أو بـ **EF Core Power Tools**؛ ولو عملت `-Force` هيمسح تعديلاتك على الملفات المولدة إلا لو كانت في ملفات `partial`!
• **Raw SQL**: `.FromSql($"SELECT ... WHERE Id = {id}")` (آمن من SQL Injection لأنه Parameterized تلقائيا!)، و `ExecuteSqlAsync` للأوامر اللي مبترجعش صفوف.
Topics.SummaryEn:
• Seeding: `HasData()` (requires explicit PK values, tracked in migrations) vs Startup/JSON Seeding.
• Database First: `Scaffold-DbContext` or EF Core Power Tools generates `partial` classes so custom additions belong in separate partial files (surviving `-Force`).
• Raw SQL: `FromSql` / `FromSqlInterpolated` (safe FormattableString parameterization) vs `FromSqlRaw` + `SqlParameter`; `Database.ExecuteSqlAsync` for DML/SPs.
Topics.CommonMistakes:
• Passing concatenated strings `$"SELECT ... {x}"` into `FromSqlRaw(...)` instead of `FromSql(...)` -> SQL Injection vulnerability!
• Omitting primary keys inside `HasData(new Category { Name = "Books" })` (EF Core throws error during `Add-Migration`!).
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• Compare `HasData()` vs Startup Code Seeding.
• What happens if you run `Scaffold-DbContext ... -Force` after editing a generated class?
• Compare `FromSql` vs `FromSqlRaw` for SQL Injection safety.

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: Every entity seeded with HasData() MUST explicitly provide its Primary Key value (even Identity PKs).

Modules.TitleAr: ما قبل الـ ASP.NET: بروتوكول HTTP و Kestrel و Reverse Proxy
Modules.Description: World Wide Web stack (HTML/CSS/JS), HTTP vs HTTPS (TLS), Raw Request/Response format, HTTP Verbs & Idempotency, Status Codes (2xx-5xx), ASP.NET Core Project Templates, Kestrel Edge vs Reverse Proxy.

Topics.TitleEn: HTTP/HTTPS (TLS), Verbs, Idempotency & Status Codes
Topics.TitleAr: بروتوكول HTTP vs HTTPS والـ Methods والـ Idempotency والـ Status Codes
Topics.SummaryAr:
• **HTTP vs HTTPS**: الـ HTTPS هو HTTP جوه نفق مشفر بالـ **TLS** (بورت 443 بدل 80)، بيضمن التشفير وهوية السيرفر وسلامة البيانات.
• **HTTP Verbs**: `GET` (قراءة)، `POST` (إنشاء جديد - مش Idempotent)، `PUT` (استبدال كامل - Idempotent)، `PATCH` (تعديل جزئي)، `DELETE` (حذف - Idempotent).
• **Status Codes المهمة**: `200 OK`, `201 Created`, `204 NoContent`, `400 BadRequest`, `401 Unauthorized` (مش مسجل دخول - Unauthenticated!), `403 Forbidden` (مسجل بس معندوش صلاحية!), `404 NotFound`, `500 InternalServerError`.
Topics.SummaryEn:
• HTTP Request = Request Line + Headers + Body; Response = Status Line + Headers + Body.
• HTTPS = HTTP + TLS encryption & server certificate verification (port 443).
• Idempotency: repeating `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE` leaves server state same as calling once; `POST` creates duplicates.
• Critical status codes: `401 Unauthorized` (who are you?) vs `403 Forbidden` (I know you, no permission!).
Topics.CommonMistakes:
• Returning `401 Unauthorized` when an already authenticated normal user opens an Admin-only route (should be `403 Forbidden`!).
• Thinking `DELETE` isn't idempotent because the 2nd response code changes (`200` -> `404`): Idempotency is about **server state**, NOT the status code!
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• Difference between `401 Unauthorized` and `403 Forbidden`?
• Compare `PUT` vs `PATCH` vs `POST` and which HTTP methods are Safe / Idempotent.
• List the 5 HTTP status code classes (`1xx`–`5xx`).

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: 401 = Unauthenticated (not logged in / bad token); 403 = Authenticated but lacks required Role/Permission.
GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE leave server state identical if repeated; POST is NOT idempotent.
PUT replaces the entire resource representation; PATCH applies partial updates.

Questions.Prompt: You call `DELETE /api/orders/5` twice: the 1st call returns 200 OK, the 2nd returns 404 NotFound. Is DELETE idempotent?
Options: Yes — server state after N calls equals 1 call
Questions.CorrectAnswer: Yes — server state after N calls equals 1 call
Questions.Explanation: Idempotency applies to the side effect on server state (order 5 remains deleted), not necessarily receiving identical HTTP status codes.

Questions.Prompt: An already logged-in regular user tries to access `/Admin/Dashboard` without the Admin role. Which HTTP status code should the server return?
Questions.Explanation: 401 means not authenticated (who are you?); 403 means authenticated but forbidden from this resource.

Topics.TitleEn: ASP.NET Core Templates, Kestrel Server & Reverse Proxy
Topics.TitleAr: أنواع مشاريع ASP.NET Core وسيرفر Kestrel و الـ Reverse Proxy
Topics.SummaryAr:
• قوالب **ASP.NET Core**: `MVC` (صفحات HTML + Pattern الـ M-V-C)، `Razor Pages` (Page-focused)، `Web API / Minimal API` (ترجع JSON)، `Blazor` (تفاعل بالـ C# بدل JS)، `gRPC`.
• **Kestrel**: الـ Web Server المدمج السريع والـ Cross-platform اللي بيشتغل **جوه نفس Process الأبلكيشن**.
• في الـ Production بنحط قدامه **Reverse Proxy** زي IIS أو Nginx أو YARP ليه؟ لـ TLS termination، و Load Balancing، والـ Rate Limiting، وعزل Kestrel عن الإنترنت المباشر.
Topics.SummaryEn:
• Templates: `dotnet new mvc` (Model-View-Controller HTML), `dotnet new webapi` (Minimal APIs default in .NET 8+ or Controllers, returns JSON), `razor`, `blazor`, `grpc`.
• **Kestrel**: built-in cross-platform managed web server running **in-process** inside the app.
• **Reverse Proxy** (Nginx, IIS, Caddy): terminates public HTTPS, handles static caching, compression, load balancing, and shields Kestrel.
Topics.CommonMistakes:
• Thinking Kestrel runs as a separate external Windows service you install manually (it is an in-process NuGet/framework server!).
• Exposing raw Kestrel directly on complex multi-app hosts without forwarded headers / reverse proxy configuration.
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• What is Kestrel and where does it run?
• Why put a Reverse Proxy (Nginx / IIS) in front of Kestrel in production?
• Compare ASP.NET Core MVC vs Razor Pages vs Web API vs Blazor.

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: Built-in cross-platform web server running inside your .NET app process (not an external daemon).
TLS termination, Load Balancing, security shielding, and caching in front of Kestrel.

Modules.Description: MVC Separation of Concerns, Project Conventions, Actions & IActionResult, Request Pipeline Middleware (Use/Run/Map & order), Routing (Conventional, Attribute, Constraints), Model Binding & Validation, DI with DbContext, Razor Views (_Layout/_ViewStart/_ViewImports), and IEnumerable vs IQueryable.

Topics.TitleEn: MVC Pattern, Project Conventions, Controllers & IActionResult
Topics.TitleAr: نمط MVC وهيكلة المشروع و الـ Actions و IActionResult
Topics.SummaryAr:
• نمط **MVC** بيقسم التطبيق لـ 3 أجزاء (**Separation of Concerns**): **Model** (الداتا والقواعد)، **View** (الواجهة `.cshtml` بدون Business Logic)، **Controller** (الـ Coordinator اللي بيستلم الـ Request ويرجع Response).
• Conventions مهمة جدا: اسم الكنترولر لازم ينتهي بـ `Controller` (مثل `PlanController`)، والمجلد جوه `Views/` يكون بنفس الاسم بدون `Controller` (`Views/Plan/Index.cshtml`) — ولو مالقاهش يدور في `Views/Shared/` ولو مالقاهش يضرب `InvalidOperationException`.
• الـ Action ميثود `public` بترجع `IActionResult` (`View()`, `PartialView()`, `RedirectToAction()`, `Json()`, `Content()`, `NotFound()`, `BadRequest()`).
Topics.SummaryEn:
• MVC splits Model (state/rules), View (presentation `.cshtml`), Controller (coordinator).
• Naming conventions: `<Name>Controller` -> `Views/<Name>/<Action>.cshtml` -> fallback `Views/Shared/<Action>.cshtml` -> else `InvalidOperationException`.
• Return `IActionResult` so a single action can return HTML `View()`, `RedirectToAction()`, `NotFound()`, `Json()`, or `File()`.
Topics.CommonMistakes:
• Putting business/DB logic directly inside `.cshtml` Razor Views.
• Creating a Controller class without inheriting `Controller` (misses `View()`, `ModelState`, `RedirectToAction()`) or omitting the `Controller` suffix.
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• Explain the 3 components of MVC and how a request flows through them.
• What is the view discovery search path order when calling `return View();`?
• Why return `IActionResult` instead of strictly `ViewResult`?

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: 1. Views/<Controller>/<Action>.cshtml -> 2. Views/Shared/<Action>.cshtml -> 3. InvalidOperationException.
Controllers MUST end with 'Controller' (e.g. PlanController maps to route segment 'Plan').
Common return contract for View(), PartialView(), Json(), RedirectToAction(), NotFound(), BadRequest().

Topics.TitleEn: Middleware Request Pipeline: Use, Run, Map & Exact Registration Order
Topics.TitleAr: خط طلبات الـ Middleware و Use / Run / Map وأهمية الترتيب
Topics.SummaryAr:
• الـ **Middleware** عبارة عن طبقات بتعدي عليها كل Request بالترتيب وترجع من خلالها بالـ Reverse Order (زي البصلة / Russian dolls).
• 3 دوال بناء: **`app.Use`** (بينفذ قبل وبعد وبيستدعي `await next()` للطبقة التالية)، **`app.Run`** (Terminal Middleware بيقفل الـ Pipeline وما يكملش بعدها!)، **`app.Map`** (بيعمل Branching لمسار URL معين).
• **الترتيب في `Program.cs` حياة أو موت!** لازم: `UseExceptionHandler` -> `UseHttpsRedirection` -> `UseStaticFiles` -> `UseRouting` -> `UseAuthentication` -> `UseAuthorization` -> `MapControllerRoute`.
Topics.SummaryEn:
• Request pipeline runs middlewares in exact registration order on entry, and reverse order on exit.
• `app.Use`: executes before/after `await next(context)`.
• `app.Run`: terminal (short-circuits, never calls next!).
• `app.Map`: branches pipeline by URL prefix.
• Order: ExceptionHandler -> HTTPS -> StaticFiles -> Routing -> CORS -> Authentication -> Authorization -> Endpoints.
Topics.CommonMistakes:
• Putting `app.UseAuthorization()` BEFORE `app.UseRouting()` or BEFORE `app.UseAuthentication()` (auth breaks completely!).
• Putting `app.Run(...)` before `MapControllerRoute(...)` (short-circuits every MVC route!).
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• Explain the difference between `app.Use`, `app.Run`, and `app.Map`.
• What happens if you put `UseStaticFiles()` AFTER `UseAuthorization()` or `UseAuthorization()` BEFORE `UseAuthentication()`?
• How do you write a Custom Timing/Logging Middleware class?

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: app.Use chains via await next(); app.Run terminates pipeline; app.Map branches on path prefix.
ExceptionHandler -> StaticFiles -> Routing -> Authentication -> Authorization -> MapControllerRoute.

Topics.TitleEn: Routing: Conventional Routes, Attribute Routing & Route Constraints
Topics.TitleAr: التوجيه Routing: الـ Conventional و Attribute Routing والـ Constraints
Topics.SummaryAr:
• الـ **Conventional Routing** في `Program.cs`: `pattern: "{controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}"` (العلامة `=` بتدي القيمة الافتراضية و `?` بتخلي `id` اختياري).
• الـ **Attribute Routing**: `[Route("results")]` فوق الكنترولر و `[HttpGet("json/{id:int}")]` فوق الـ Action.
• **Route Constraints** بتقيد شكل الـ URL: `{id:int}`، `{id:min(1)}`، `{name:alpha}`، `{name:length(3,20)}` — لو النوع مش مطابق يرجع `404` قبل ما يدخل الـ Action!
Topics.SummaryEn:
• Conventional default template: `{controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}`.
• Attribute routing puts explicit `[Route(...)]` / `[HttpGet(...)]` on controllers & actions.
• Constraints (`:int`, `:min(1)`, `:alpha`, `:length(3,20)`, `:guid`) filter URL matching at routing stage before action execution.
Topics.CommonMistakes:
• Expecting `/Products/Details/abc` to enter `Details(int id)` cleanly when route constraint `{id:int}` is active (constraint yields 404; without `:int`, `id` defaults to 0 with ModelState error!).
• Combining `[Route]` without checking how it overrides conventional routing for that action.
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• Conventional Routing vs Attribute Routing — when to use each?
• What do `=Home` and `?` mean in `{controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}`?
• Give examples of Route Constraints (`:int`, `:alpha`, `:min`, `:guid`).

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: '{controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}' defaults Controller=Home, Action=Index, optional id.
Colon rules like {id:int} or {name:alpha} restrict URL matching directly in the router.

Topics.TitleEn: Model Binding Sources & Validation (Data Annotations + ModelState)
Topics.TitleAr: ربط البيانات Model Binding ومصادرها والتحقق Validation
Topics.SummaryAr:
• الـ **Model Binding** بياخد الداتا من الـ HTTP Request ويحطها تلقائيا في بارامترات الـ Action أو الـ Model Class.
• ترتيب الأولوية الافتراضي: Form (`[FromForm]`) -> Route (`[FromRoute]`) -> QueryString (`[FromQuery]`).
• باقي المصادر الصريحة: **`[FromBody]`** (JSON في الـ Body - في APIs)، **`[FromHeader]`**، **`[FromServices]`** (من الـ DI Container!).
• مع الـ Validation: بنحط Attributes زي `[Required]`, `[Range]`, `[EmailAddress]` ونشيك جوه الـ Action بـ **`if (!ModelState.IsValid) return View(model);`**!
Topics.SummaryEn:
• Automatically maps incoming HTTP values to C# action parameters/models.
• Default source lookup order: Form values -> Route values -> Query string.
• Explicit attributes: `[FromRoute]`, `[FromQuery]`, `[FromForm]`, `[FromBody]` (JSON payload), `[FromHeader]`, `[FromServices]`.
• Server validation checks `if (!ModelState.IsValid)` using Data Annotations (`[Required]`, `[StringLength]`, `[Range]`).
Topics.CommonMistakes:
• Skipping `if (!ModelState.IsValid)` on server-side POST actions (relying only on HTML/jQuery validation).
• Using `return View("Index")` directly after successful `POST` instead of `RedirectToAction` (PRG: Post-Redirect-Get pattern prevents duplicate form submit on F5!).
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• List the default Model Binding value provider priority order.
• Explain `[FromRoute]`, `[FromQuery]`, `[FromForm]`, `[FromBody]`, `[FromHeader]`, `[FromServices]`.
• What is `ModelState.IsValid` and the PRG (Post-Redirect-Get) pattern?

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: Default binding order: 1. Form fields -> 2. Route values -> 3. Query string.
[FromRoute], [FromQuery], [FromForm], [FromBody], [FromHeader], [FromServices] override default lookup.
Check ModelState.IsValid; on failure return View(model), on success RedirectToAction (Post-Redirect-Get).

Topics.TitleEn: DI with DbContext, Razor Syntax (.cshtml), _Layout, _ViewStart & _ViewImports
Topics.TitleAr: حقن الاعتمادية DI وواجهة Razor وملفات _Layout و _ViewStart و _ViewImports
Topics.SummaryAr:
• الـ **Controller** مبيعملش `new GymDbContext()` بإيده! بنسجل `AddDbContext<GymDbContext>()` في `Program.cs` والـ DI يحقنه في الـ Constructor (**Scoped Lifetime** افتراضيا!).
• **Razor (`.cshtml`)**: `@model List<Plan>` يحدد نوع الـ Model؛ `@Model` توصل للبيانات؛ `@if`/`@foreach`؛ `@{ C# block }`.
• **ملفات الـ Layout المهمة**:
  - `_Layout.cshtml`: القالب الرئيسي (Navbar + Footer + **`@RenderBody()`** + `@RenderSectionAsync`).
  - `_ViewStart.cshtml`: بيشتغل **قبل** كل View ليحدد `Layout = "_Layout";` بدل تكراره (ويمكن إلغاؤه بـ `Layout = null;`).
  - `_ViewImports.cshtml`: بيشارك `@using` و `@addTagHelper` على مستوى كل الـ Views!
Topics.SummaryEn:
• Register `builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>()` (Scoped per HTTP request) and inject via Controller constructor.
• Razor `.cshtml`: `@model T` declares model type; `@Model` accesses it; `@{ ... }` runs code blocks; Tag Helpers (`asp-controller`, `asp-action`, `asp-route-id`).
• `_Layout.cshtml` (`@RenderBody()`), `_ViewStart.cshtml` (runs before every view to set default `Layout`), `_ViewImports.cshtml` (shared `@using` & Tag Helpers).
Topics.CommonMistakes:
• Confusing `@model` (lowercase: declares the type at top of `.cshtml`) vs `@Model` (PascalCase: accesses the actual runtime object).
• Forgetting `@RenderBody()` inside `_Layout.cshtml` -> throws `InvalidOperationException`.
• Registering `DbContext` or DbContext-dependent repository as `Singleton` instead of `Scoped`!
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• What is the difference between `_Layout.cshtml`, `_ViewStart.cshtml`, and `_ViewImports.cshtml`?
• In what order do `_ViewImports`, `_ViewStart`, `Index.cshtml`, and `_Layout` execute?
• Difference between `@model` and `@Model` in Razor?
• What DI lifetime does `AddDbContext` register?

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: _ViewImports adds shared @using/TagHelpers -> _ViewStart sets default Layout -> View renders inside _Layout's @RenderBody().
@model (lowercase) declares the strongly-typed class/interface; @Model (uppercase) accesses the passed instance.
DbContext is Scoped by default (1 instance per HTTP request); NEVER inject a Scoped DbContext into a Singleton service.

Options: _ViewImports supplies @using/TagHelpers -> _ViewStart assigns Layout -> Index.cshtml executes -> _Layout wraps it via @RenderBody()
Index.cshtml runs alone, then _ViewStart overrides its HTML

Topics.TitleEn: IQueryable vs IEnumerable in Controllers & Avoiding Early ToList()
Topics.TitleAr: الفرق المصيري بين IQueryable و IEnumerable في الـ Actions وتجنب ToList() البدري
Topics.SummaryAr:
• **`IEnumerable<T>`** (`System.Collections.Generic`): الـ Lambda بتنفذ كـ كود C# في **ميموري السيرفر** (`IL` / Delegate) — لو جبت 10,000 صف الأول وعملت `.Where()` بعدها انت حملت الجدول كله في الرام!
• **`IQueryable<T>`** (`System.Linq`): بتبني **Expression Tree** وتترجمها لـ **SQL `WHERE`/`ORDER BY`/`TAKE`** يتنفذ جوه **SQL Server نفسه** وميرجعلكش غير الصفوف المطلوبة!
• غلطة شهيرة: تنادي `.ToList()` بدري قبل `.Where()` و `.Take()`.
Topics.SummaryEn:
• `IEnumerable<T>` executes `Func<T, bool>` delegates in App RAM (loads all rows if pulled from DB first).
• `IQueryable<T>` builds `Expression<Func<T, bool>>` trees translated to native SQL `WHERE`/`TOP`/`OFFSET` inside SQL Server.
• Keep query `IQueryable` while composing filters/sorting/paging, call `.ToListAsync()` ONLY at the end before passing to `View()`!
Topics.CommonMistakes: • Returning `IEnumerable<T>` from a Repository method BEFORE applying `.Where()` and pagination (switches LINQ from `Queryable` to `Enumerable`, forcing full table load into RAM!).
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• Compare `IEnumerable<T>` vs `IQueryable<T>` (namespace, delegate vs Expression Tree, where filtering runs, deferred execution, performance).
• Why should repositories return `IQueryable` or accept filter specifications before `.ToListAsync()`?

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: IEnumerable uses Func<> in App RAM; IQueryable uses Expression<> translated to SQL WHERE/OFFSET inside SQL Server.
Compose all Where/OrderBy/Skip/Take on IQueryable FIRST, then call ToListAsync() once at execution.

Topics.TitleEn: Repository Pattern, Dependency Injection Lifetimes, Edit (GET/POST), ViewModels & TempData
Topics.TitleAr: نمط Repository وحقن الاعتمادية DI Lifetimes و ViewModels و TempData و Overposting
Topics.SummaryAr:
• Repository Pattern (S و D من SOLID): فصل استعلامات EF Core عن الكنترولر خلف Interface (`IPlanRepository`) لسهولة التعديل والـ Unit Testing.
• Dependency Injection Lifetimes: `AddTransient` (نسخة جديدة في كل حقنة)، `AddScoped` (نسخة واحدة لكل HTTP Request — الأفضل مع `DbContext`)، `AddSingleton` (نسخة واحدة طول عمر التطبيق).
• تمرير البيانات: `ViewData` (Dictionary)، `ViewBag` (`dynamic` لنفس الطلب فقط)، `TempData` (تعيش بعد `RedirectToAction`).
• الحماية في Edit POST: استخدم `ViewModel` بدل Entity مباشرة لمنع Overposting Attack، مع `[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]` ضد CSRF ونمط PRG (Post-Redirect-Get).
Topics.SummaryEn:
• Repository + SOLID (Single Responsibility & Dependency Inversion): Controllers depend on `IPlanRepository`.
• DI Container Lifetimes: `Transient` (per injection), `Scoped` (per HTTP Request), `Singleton` (app lifetime).
• `ViewData` / `ViewBag` (single request) vs `TempData` (survives RedirectToAction).
• ViewModels prevent Overposting; `[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]` blocks CSRF; PRG prevents F5 duplicate submits.
Topics.CommonMistakes:
• Injecting a Scoped DbContext/Repository inside a Singleton service (Captive Dependency error!).
• Binding Entity classes directly in [HttpPost] action parameters instead of ViewModels (Overposting risk!).
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• Compare AddTransient vs AddScoped vs AddSingleton (and what is Captive Dependency?).
• Compare ViewData, ViewBag, and TempData.
• What is Overposting and how do ViewModels prevent it?

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: Transient=every resolution; Scoped=once per HTTP request (DbContext); Singleton=shared app-wide.
ViewData (Dictionary) & ViewBag (dynamic) last 1 request; TempData survives a RedirectToAction.
Never bind EF Entity classes directly on POST; use dedicated ViewModels with only allowed fields.
Guards POST/PUT actions against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks.

Topics.TitleEn: City Library OOP & Library Management System (EF Core Capstone)
Topics.TitleAr: مشروع المكتبة بـ OOP وبـ EF Core + مشروع ReadMore Books و National Bank
Topics.SummaryAr:
• مشروع **City Library OOP** بيعلمك تفصل طبقات: Models (`Book`, `Member`, `Loan`)، Design patterns (`Composition`, `Polymorphism`, `file` validators) قبل ما تكتب سطر كود.
• مشروع **Library Management System (Adham Atef EF Core)** بيطبق `BaseEntity`، `LibraryDbContext`، Data Annotations و Relationships (`MemberLoan` many-to-many with payload, Fines, Authors, Categories).
• تطبيقات **ReadMore Books** و **Online Learning Platform** و **National Bank Management System** (Interactive Menu + Seeding + Eager Loading).
Topics.SummaryEn:
• **City Library System** (`OOP_Thinking.html`, `LibrarySystem_Solution`): BaseEntity inheritance, clean folder separation (`Models/`, `Context/`, `Migrations/`), relationship modeling.
• **ReadMore Books / Online Learning Platform / National Bank** EF Core assignments combining M:N payloads, self-referencing hierarchies, seeding, and eager loading.
Topics.CommonMistakes: • Creating bidirectional infinite JSON cycles or forgetting `.HasKey(x => new { x.MemberId, x.BookId })` on explicit join tables without surrogate `Id`.
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• How do you organize Entities, Configurations, and Context in a layered EF Core project?
• Why extract shared audit columns into a `BaseEntity` abstract class?

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: Keep common PK/Audit columns (Id, CreatedAt) in abstract BaseEntity inherited by domain models.
When borrowing/enrollment tracks extra fields (LoanDate, ReturnDate, Fine), model a join class with composite or surrogate PK.

Questions.Prompt: In Library Management System (Adham Atef EF Project), why extract `BaseEntity` and model `MemberLoan` as a dedicated join entity?
Questions.CorrectAnswer: `BaseEntity` centralizes shared keys/audit fields cleanly; `MemberLoan` models M:N with extra attributes (LoanDate, DueDate, ReturnDate, Fine).
Questions.Explanation: Whenever an M:N relationship carries domain payload attributes, an explicit join entity replaces implicit skip navigation.

Topics.TitleEn: Gym Management System (C# & MVC) & University Research SQL Exam
Topics.TitleAr: مشروع الجيم Gym Management وامتحان الجامعة الشامل للـ SQL Server
Topics.SummaryAr:
• **Gym Management System**: بدأ في C# Basics (Input validation + Pricing rules) وكبر لـ ASP.NET Core MVC App بـ `Members`, `Trainers`, `Plans`, `MemberSubscriptions`, `Sessions` + `GymDbContext` + Fluent API + `PlanController`.
• **University Research System Exam**: امتحان عملي شامل 49 سؤال T-SQL على جدول `Researcher`, `ResearchProject`, `WorksOn`, `Grants`, `Publication` يغطي كل حاجة من `LEFT JOIN` لحد `Indexed Views` و `Audit Triggers` و `TRY-CATCH Transactions` و `Index Optimizations`!
Topics.SummaryEn:
• **Gym Management System**: Domain evolution from C# console input validation to full ASP.NET Core MVC + EF Core Fluent API + Razor Views (`PlanController`).
• **University Research DB Exam**: Comprehensive SQL mastery benchmark covering Joins, Paging, Grouping/Having, Inline/Scalar TVFs, Indexed Views (`COUNT_BIG(*)`), `AFTER UPDATE` Triggers with `SYSTEM_USER`, and ACID Transactions.
Topics.CodeSnippet:
-- University Exam Highlight: Researcher + Optional Active Projects + Grant Check
SELECT r.Id, r.FirstName + ' ' + r.LastName AS FullName, p.Title
FROM dbo.Researcher r
LEFT JOIN dbo.WorksOn w ON w.ResearcherId = r.Id
LEFT JOIN dbo.ResearchProject p ON p.Id = w.ProjectId
ORDER BY r.LastName OFFSET 10 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY;
Topics.CommonMistakes: • Filtering optional `LEFT JOIN` project statuses inside `WHERE` (drops researchers who aren't assigned to any project!).
Topics.InterviewQuestions:
• Walk through how `MVC-Session02` builds the Gym Plan Index end-to-end (Route -> Controller -> DbContext -> SQL -> View Model -> `_Layout`).
• In the University Exam, suggest 3 query optimizations for slow multi-join queries (Indexes on FK+WHERE, Covering INCLUDE, Avoid `SELECT *` / non-SARGable WHERE).

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: 1. Index FKs & WHERE filters; 2. Add Covering INCLUDE columns; 3. SARGable predicates; 4. Paginate with OFFSET-FETCH.
Log Old & New values using INSERTED JOIN DELETED + SYSTEM_USER + SYSDATETIME().

Questions.CorrectAnswer: 1. Non-clustered indexes on FK join columns; 2. Filtered/Composite index on (Status, StartDate DESC) with INCLUDE columns; 3. Pagination with OFFSET-FETCH and avoiding SELECT *.
Questions.Explanation: Covers join keys, predicate pushdown/seek, Sort elimination via index order, and covering leaf columns.

Modules.Description: Upcoming Route Academy syllabus phases documented in ASP.NET Student Guide Schema.pdf (Web APIs, Security/JWT, Clean Architecture, Caching/SignalR/Deployment). Note: Video & lab files for these phases are not yet in your local folder.

Topics.TitleEn: RESTful Web APIs, Swagger/OpenAPI, Identity & JWT Authentication
Topics.TitleAr: تطوير الـ Web APIs والـ JWT Token و ASP.NET Identity (قادم في المنهج)
Topics.SummaryAr: • المرحلة القادمة بعد MVC حسب ملف `ASP.NET Student Guide Schema.pdf`: تصميم RESTful APIs بـ `[ApiController]` و Route Conventions، توثيق Swagger/OpenAPI، التوثيق بـ ASP.NET Core Identity + JWT Tokens + Role/Policy Authorization.
Topics.SummaryEn:
• Listed in `ASP.NET Student Guide Schema.pdf` (pages 32–36) after MVC.
• `[ApiController]`, REST resource routes, Swagger/OpenAPI, `ProblemDetails`, ASP.NET Core Identity (`UserManager`, `RoleManager`), JWT Bearer authentication & refresh tokens.
Topics.CommonMistakes: • Confusing Cookie-based auth in MVC with Stateless JWT Bearer auth in APIs.
Topics.InterviewQuestions: • What does `[ApiController]` automatically provide (400 automatic validation, `[FromBody]` inference, ProblemDetails)?

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: Enables automatic ModelState 400 responses, attribute routing enforcement, and binding inference.

Questions.Prompt: What automatic behaviors does `[ApiController]` enable in ASP.NET Core Web APIs?
Questions.CorrectAnswer: 1. Attribute routing requirement; 2. Automatic HTTP 400 validation error responses; 3. Binding source inference ([FromBody] for complex types, [FromRoute]/[FromQuery] for simple); 4. ProblemDetails error formatting.
Questions.Explanation: Standard Web API convention covered in Phase 5 of ASP.NET Student Guide Schema.pdf.

Topics.TitleEn: Clean Architecture, Unit of Work, Caching, SignalR & Deployment
Topics.TitleAr: الـ Clean Architecture و Repository/UoW و Caching و SignalR والنشر
Topics.SummaryAr: • حسب ملف `ASP.NET Student Guide Schema.pdf`: N-Tier vs Clean Architecture / Onion، أنماط Repository + Unit of Work + Specification Pattern + AutoMapper + MediatR/CQRS، الـ Caching (In-Memory & Redis)، Background Jobs (Hangfire)، Real-Time بـ SignalR، و Docker / IIS / Azure Deployment.
Topics.SummaryEn:
• Covered in later phases of `ASP.NET Student Guide Schema.pdf` (pages 35–42).
• Clean Architecture dependency rule (Domain -> Application -> Infrastructure -> Presentation), Repository + Unit of Work, Redis Distributed Cache, Hangfire, SignalR hubs, and CI/CD Deployment.
Topics.CodeSnippet:
// Clean Architecture Dependency Rule:
// Domain (0 dependencies) <- Application (Interfaces) <- Infrastructure (EF Core) + API
Topics.CommonMistakes: • Putting EF Core / Infrastructure references inside the Domain Core project.
Topics.InterviewQuestions: • Explain the Dependency Inversion rule in Clean Architecture.

ConventionKeys.ShortRule: Inner Domain & Application layers must NOT depend on outer EF Core/Web UI Infrastructure layers.

[S01] Session 01 C# - Basics
[S02] Session Agenda | 01 | What is Programming | 02 | Programming Paradigms | 03 | Comments | 05 | Value Types | 06 | Reference Types | 07 | Stack vs Heap | 04 | Variables
[S03] What is Programming & How Does Code Run? | Programming is writing instructions for a computer. Computers only understand 0s and 1s (binary), so we use programming languages like C# as a translator between human ideas and machine instructions. | Communication | Tell the computer exactly what to do, in a language it understands. | Abstraction | Hide complex details behind simple commands. | x | Automation | Make the computer do repetitive work for us. | Problem Solving | Break big problems into small, solvable steps. | Four Things Programming Helps Us Do | How Does Your Code Run ?
[S04] Compiled vs Interpreted | Compiled | Translate the whole program to machine code before running. | C, C++, Rust | ✅ | Fast execution | ❌ | Must recompile for each platform | Interpreted | Translate one line at a time while the program runs. | Python, JavaScript, Ruby | ✅ | Runs anywhere | ❌ | Slower — translating as it goes | Two Approaches
[S05] How C# Runs Your Code | Why JIT is Great | 1. Runs Anywhere             				2. Fast Like Compiled | 3. Catches Errors Early    				4. Runtime Optimizations | C#'s Hybrid — How JIT Works
[S06] Programming Paradigms — Different Ways to Write Code | A | paradigm | is just a style of writing code. Different problems call for different styles. The good news: C# supports all of them, so you can pick the best tool for each job. | The Four Paradigms in C# | Style | Idea | C# Example | Imperative | Step-by-step instructions | for, while, if/else | Procedural | Break code into reusable functions | void CalculateTotal() { } | OOP | Model the world as objects with data + behavior | class Car { } | Functional | Transform data with pure functions | LINQ, Lambda: list.Where(x => x > 5)
[S07] Comments in C# | Comments are notes you write in your code that the computer ignores. They help other developers (and future you!) understand what the code does and why. Good comments make code readable. Bad comments just repeat what the code already says. | /* */ | Multi-lines. | Longer explanations | /* auth logic */ | // | Single-line | Quick notes on one line | // calculate tax | Three Types of Comments | /// | XML Docs | API documentation | /// <summary>...</summary> | Visual Studio Shortcuts | Shortcut | What It Does | Ctrl + K, Ctrl + C | Comment selected lines | Ctrl + K, Ctrl + U | Uncomment selected lines | Ctrl + / | Toggle comment on current line
[S08] Declaring Variables | A variable is a named box that stores data. To create one, you give it a type (what kind of data), a name (how you'll refer to it), and optionally a value (what's inside the box). | The Three Parts of a Variable
[S09] Variable Scope — Where Can You Use It? | Scope is the area of your code where a variable is visible and usable. Think of it like a room — a variable declared inside a room can't be seen from outside. C# has three levels of scope, nested like Russian dolls. | Three Levels of Scope
[S10] Variable Lifetime — How Long Does It Live? | Lifetime is how long a variable stays in memory before being cleaned up. Some variables live for milliseconds, others for the entire life of your app. Understanding this helps you predict memory usage and avoid bugs. | Four Types of Lifetime
[S11] Naming Things in C# | Good names make code readable. Bad names force everyone to guess what a variable or method actually does. C# has simple rules for naming, plus conventions that teams follow to stay consistent. | The Rules — What You Can and Can't Do | Two Naming Styles — When to Use Each
[S12] Value Types — Each Variable Owns Its Data | Value Types store the actual data directly inside the variable. When you assign one variable to another, a copy of the value is created — the two variables are then completely independent of each other. Think of it as: each variable gets its own private box. | Common Value Types
[S13] Reference Types — Two Variables, One Object | Reference Types store a reference (address) to the actual data on the Heap. When you assign one variable to another, only the reference is copied — not the data itself. Both variables end up pointing to the same object, and a change made through one is visible through the other. | Common Reference Types
[S14] Value vs Reference — Side-by-Side Summary | Let's put both kinds of types in one comparison table so the differences are easy to remember. Master this single chart and you'll instantly know what happens to any variable you assign, copy, or pass to a method in C#. | Aspect | Value Type | Reference Type | Storage | Stack (fast, automatic cleanup) | Heap (flexible, garbage collected) | Contains | The actual data | Memory address (pointer) | Assignment | Copies the value | Copies the reference (address) | Default | 0, false, empty | null (points to nothing) | Examples | int, bool, struct, enum | class, array, string, List | Safety | Changes don't leak out | Changes affect everyone sharing | Side-by-Side Comparison
[S15] Memory — Stack vs Heap | When your program runs, it uses two areas of memory: the Stack and the Heap. The Stack is fast and automatic. The Heap is flexible but needs cleanup. Knowing which lives where helps you understand performance and avoid bugs. | Stack | A small, ultra-fast memory region used for tracking method execution and short-lived data, operating on a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) basis. | Heap | A much larger, flexible pool of memory used for dynamic allocations where data lives independently of method scopes and is maintained by the .NET Garbage Collector (GC) | What goes here | Value types (int, bool, double, char, and custom struct declarations) | Automatic Deallocation | As soon as a method finishes executing | What goes here | Reference types (class, interface, delegate, string, and array) | Garbage Collection (GC) | Memory on the heap cannot be dropped instantaneously.

The good news: C# supports all of them, so you can pick the best tool for each job. | The Four Paradigms in C# | Style | Idea | C# Example | Imperative | Step-by-step instructions | for, while, if/else | Procedural | Break code into reusable functions | void CalculateTotal() { } | OOP | Model the world as objects with data + behavior | class Car { } | Functional | Transform data with pure functions | LINQ, Lambda: list.Where(x => x > 5)"}, {"label": "Slide 07", "t": 7, "text": "Comments in C# | Comments are notes you write in your code that the computer ignores. They help other developers (and future you!) understand what the code does and why. Good comments make code readable. Bad comments just repeat what the code already says. | /* */ | Multi-lines. | Longer explanations | /* auth logic */ | // | Single-line | Quick notes on one line | // calculate tax | Three Types of Comments | /// | XML Docs | API documentation | /// <summary>...</summary> | Visual Studio Shortcuts | Shortcut | What It Does | Ctrl + K, Ctrl + C | Comment selected lines | Ctrl + K, Ctrl + U | Uncomment selected lines | Ctrl + / | Toggle comment on current line"}, {"label": "Slide 08", "t": 8, "text": "Declaring Variables | A variable is a named box that stores data. To create one, you give it a type (what kind of data), a name (how you'll refer to it), and optionally a value (what's inside the box). | The Three Parts of a Variable"}, {"label": "Slide 09", "t": 9, "text": "Variable Scope — Where Can You Use It? | Scope is the area of your code where a variable is visible and usable. Think of it like a room — a variable declared inside a room can't be seen from outside. C# has three levels of scope, nested like Russian dolls. | Three Levels of Scope"}, {"label": "Slide 10", "t": 10, "text": "Variable Lifetime — How Long Does It Live? | Lifetime is how long a variable stays in memory before being cleaned up. Some variables live for milliseconds, others for the entire life of your app. Understanding this helps you predict memory usage and avoid bugs. | Four Types of Lifetime"}, {"label": "Slide 11", "t": 11, "text": "Naming Things in C# | Good names make code readable. Bad names force everyone to guess what a variable or method actually does. C# has simple rules for naming, plus conventions that teams follow to stay consistent. | The Rules — What You Can and Can't Do | Two Naming Styles — When to Use Each"}, {"label": "Slide 12", "t": 12, "text": "Value Types — Each Variable Owns Its Data | Value Types store the actual data directly inside the variable. When you assign one variable to another, a copy of the value is created — the two variables are then completely independent of each other. Think of it as: each variable gets its own private box. | Common Value Types"}, {"label": "Slide 13", "t": 13, "text": "Reference Types — Two Variables, One Object | Reference Types store a reference (address) to the actual data on the Heap. When you assign one variable to another, only the reference is copied — not the data itself. Both variables end up pointing to the same object, and a change made through one is visible through the other. | Common Reference Types"}, {"label": "Slide 14", "t": 14, "text": "Value vs Reference — Side-by-Side Summary | Let's put both kinds of types in one comparison table so the differences are easy to remember. Master this single chart and you'll instantly know what happens to any variable you assign, copy, or pass to a method in C#. | Aspect | Value Type | Reference Type | Storage | Stack (fast, automatic cleanup) | Heap (flexible, garbage collected) | Contains | The actual data | Memory address (pointer) | Assignment | Copies the value | Copies the reference (address) | Default | 0, false, empty | null (points to nothing) | Examples | int, bool, struct, enum | class, array, string, List | Safety | Changes don't leak out | Changes affect everyone sharing | Side-by-Side Comparison"}, {"label": "Slide 15", "t": 15, "text": "Memory — Stack vs Heap | When your program runs, it uses two areas of memory: the Stack and the Heap. The Stack is fast and automatic. The Heap is flexible but needs cleanup. Knowing which lives where helps you understand performance and avoid bugs. | Stack | A small, ultra-fast memory region used for tracking method execution and short-lived data, operating on a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) basis. | Heap | A much larger, flexible pool of memory used for dynamic allocations where data lives independently of method scopes and is maintained by the .NET Garbage Collector (GC) | What goes here | Value types (int, bool, double, char, and custom struct declarations) | Automatic Deallocation | As soon as a method finishes executing | What goes here | Reference types (class, interface, delegate, string, and array) | Garbage Collection (GC) | Memory on the heap cannot be dropped instantaneously."}, {"label": "Slide 16", "t": 16, "text": "What Goes Where"}, {"label": "Slide 17", "t": 17, "text": "How a Value Type Stores in Stack"}, {"label": "Slide 18", "t": 18, "text": "How a Reference Type Stores in Stack & Heap"}, {"label": "Slide 19", "t": 19, "text": "Thank You | See You Next Session"}]

[@01:30|t=90] Declaring Variables ROUTE A variable is a named box that stores data. C# Assignment 
All questions use the same theme: a Book with a Title and Pages. Try each one yourself before checking the answer.
Create a Book class with a Title (string) and Pages (int). Create a Book object and store it in a variable of type object. Print it.
Using the Book class above, print the result of calling ToString(), Equals() (compare book with itself), GetHashCode(), and GetType() on book.
Look at the line below. Is it a compile-time error, a runtime error, or a logical error? Fix it.Compile-time error — you can't put text (string) into an int variable.
Write code that divides 10 by 0 inside a try block, catches the exception, prints "Cannot divide by zero", and then prints "Done" in a finally block.
Declare an int pages = 300; then store it in a double variable without using a cast.
Declare a double price = 49.99; then convert it into an int using a cast.
Given string pagesText = "464";, convert it into an int using the Convert class.
Given string yearText = "2023";, convert it using int.Parse(). Then given string badText = "abc";, use int.TryParse() to safely try converting it, and print "Invalid number" if it fails.
Given int pages = 464;, convert it into a string using ToString() and print its type using GetType() to prove it's now a string.
Declare int copies = 100;. Box it into an object variable, then unbox it back into a new int variable, and print both.
Declare an int? year = null;. Print whether it has a value, then assign it 2023 and print its value.
Declare a string? reviewer = null;. Print whether it is null.
Declare a Book? book = null;. Use ?. to safely read book.Title without crashing the program, and print the result.
Using title from the previous question, use ?? to print "Untitled" if title is null. Then use ??= to assign title the value "Untitled" only if it's still null.
Given string? name = "Ahmed"; (you are sure it's not null here), assign it to a non-nullable string confirmedName using the ! operator.

[S01] C# - Basics | Session 02
[S02] Session Agenda | 01 | Object in C# | 02 | Error Types | 03 | Exception Handling | 05 | Boxing & Unboxing | 04 | Type Casting & Conversion
[S03] Object in C# — The Root of Everything | is the parent of all data types in C#. Every type, whether it's a value type (like | int | ) or a reference type (like | string | or a custom class) | Every type | is eventually derived from object. | Key Points | Universal Base Type | Every single type in C# inherits from object, directly or indirectly. Even int is shorthand for : | System.Int32 → System.ValueType → System.Object | Storage Type | An object variable can hold any type of data, whether a value type or a reference type | Methods | Object provides a set of methods that are available on every type in the language. | Single Root Inheritance | Unlike C++ which has no universal base, C#'s single-root design enables unified type checking | and | boxing/unboxing
[S04] The Four Universal Methods | Two Approaches | Since every type inherits from object, all data types automatically get a common set of methods. This means built-in types (like int and string) and custom classes all have the same basic functionality. | Method | What It Does | Default Behaviour | Override Strategy | ToString() | Returns a string representation of the object | Returns the fully qualified type name. Useless for debugging. | Always override for meaningful output. | Equals() | Determines whether two objects are equal | Compares references (memory addresses). Types like | string | and | int | override to compare values. | Override when value equality matters. Must pair with GetHashCode. | GetHashCode() | Returns a hash code (integer) used in hash-based collections | Based on the reference address. Different instances return different values, even if they contain identical data. | Must override if Equals is overridden. Use consistent fields. | GetType() | Returns the type of the current object at runtime | Returns | Namespace.TypeName | . Used for retrieving type information at runtime (reflection). | Cannot override — sealed by the CLR.
[S05] Errors | Syntax Error | Logical Error | Run Time Error | Warning | Error Types — When Things Go Wrong
[S06] Compile-time Errors — Caught by the Compiler | 1. Detected by the Roslyn compiler before the program ever runs | 2. The program will not build until fixed | 3. Includes syntax errors, type mismatches, misspelled identifiers, missing returns | 4. Modern C# adds nullable reference types (C# 8.0+) to catch null issues at compile time | Examples: | Missing semicolon (;). | Using undeclared variables. | Incorrect method signatures. | Mismatched parentheses () or braces {} . | Error Types — When Things Go Wrong
[S07] Runtime Errors (Exceptions) — Crash the Program | Common types of runtime errors: | NullReferenceException: Occurs when you try to use an object that is null. | IndexOutOfRangeException: Happens when you access an array or collection with an invalid index. | DivideByZeroException: Triggered when you attempt to divide a number by zero. | FileNotFoundException: Raised when a file is not found during an I/O operation. | 1. Happen while the program is running | 2. Crash the program if not handled with | try-catch | 3. Most common cause of production bugs and user-facing failures | 4. NullReferenceException is the #1 exception in .NET applications worldwide | Error Types — When Things Go Wrong
[S08] Logical Errors — Silent and Dangerous | Examples: | Incorrect formula or calculation. | Wrong comparison in a conditional statement. | Using the wrong data types for variables. | 1. No compiler error, no exception thrown | 2. Program runs but produces the wrong result | 3. Hardest to detect and fix — only careful testing, code review, and static analysis reveals them | 4. Often caused by off-by-one errors, incorrect operators, or floating-point precision issues | Error Types — When Things Go Wrong
[S09] Exception Handling | An exception is an object that represents an error that happens while the program is running. Exception handling lets the program catch the error, display a helpful message, and continue running instead of crashing. | Prevent application crashes | keep the program alive and responsive | Why Handle Exceptions? The Four Pillars | Show user-friendly messages | not ugly stack traces or yellow screens of death | Log details for debugging | capture what went wrong, when, where, and for which user | Guarantee cleanup | close files, release DB connections, free resources with finally or using | Exception Properties
[S10] try contains risky code, catch handles exceptions, and finally runs always — whether the try succeeded or failed. Together they form the complete exception-handling structure in C#. | The Three Parts | try { } | Code that might fail | Required — stops at first error, subsequent lines skipped | catch { } | Handle the error				Optional — can have multiple, ordered most-specific first | finally { } | Cleanup code				Optional — always executes, even if try has a return | Execution Scenarios | Scenario | try | catch | finally | No exception | Runs fully | Skipped | Runs | Exception caught | Stops at error | Runs | Runs | Exception not caught | Stops at error | No match | Runs, then crash | try-catch-finally
[S11] .NET provides many built-in exception types for different kinds of errors. Using the correct exception helps you handle errors properly and prevent your program from crashing. | The Eight Most Common Exceptions | Exception | What Causes It | Example | NullReferenceException | Using a member on a | null | object | string s = null; s.Length; | FormatException | Invalid string format when parsing | int.Parse("abc"); | DivideByZeroException | Dividing an integer by zero | int x = 10 / 0; | IndexOutOfRangeException | Accessing an invalid array index | int[] a = {1}; a[5]; | ArgumentNullException | null | passed to a method parameter that doesn't allow it | File.Open(null, ...); | ArgumentException | Invalid argument value (other than null) | File.Open("", ...); | FileNotFoundException | File does not exist at the given path | File.ReadAllText("x.txt"); | InvalidOperationException | Operation not valid in the object's current state | emptyList.First(); | Common Built-in Exceptions
[S12] Type Casting & Conversion | Type Conversion is the process of converting a value from one data type to another. In C#, conversions can be done automatically (implicit) or manually (explicit). | Implicit Casting | Explicit Casting | Implicit casting happens automatically when a smaller type is assigned to a larger type, and there is no risk of data loss. | Explicit casting (manual casting) is needed when converting from a larger type to a smaller type, or from an incompatible type . This can result a data loss or errors.
[S13] Type Casting & Conversion | Why Do We Need Type Conversion? | Methods expect specific types | Some methods need | double | , others need | int | — we convert to match what they expect | User input is always text | Console.ReadLine() | returns a | string | , but math needs numbers → we convert | To avoid bugs & be clear | Casting shows "I know what I'm doing" — explicit code communicates intent to other developers
[S14] Implicit Conversions — The Safe Path | Implicit casting is an automatic conversion from a smaller compatible data type to a larger one. Since no data is lost, C# performs the conversion automatically. | How It Works | Example
[S15] Explicit Conversions  — The Risky Path | Implicit casting is an automatic conversion from a smaller compatible data type to a larger one. Since no data is lost, C# performs the conversion automatically. | How It Works | Example
[S16] Implicit Conversions | Explicit Conversions | Conversions
[S17] Convert Class — Converting Between Base Types | The | Convert | class converts between base data types — | string | , | int | , | double | , | bool | , etc. It's especially useful when the source is an | object | or a | string | that needs to become a number. | Common Methods
[S18] Parse() vs TryParse() | Both | Parse() | and | TryParse() | convert a | string | to a number — but they handle failure very differently. | Parse() | throws an exception on bad input, while | TryParse() | returns | false | and gives you a default value. Pick the right one for your use case. | Common Methods | Aspect | Parse() | TryParse() | On failure | Throws an exception | Returns | false | Syntax | Cleaner one-liner | Needs | out | variable | Exception in normal flow | Yes — slow on bad input | No — fast even on bad input | Safety for user input | ⚠ | Less safe | ✅ | Safer choice | Null input | Throws | ArgumentNullException | Returns | false
[S19] ToString() Method — Converting to Strings | ToString() | converts a value to its | string representation | . Every .NET type inherits it from | object | , and many types override it to provide meaningful output. With a | format specifier | argument you can also control how the value is displayed — decimal places, currency symbols, percentages, and more. | Common Format Specifiers | Format | Input | Output | Use For | "0.00" | 1234.5 | "1234.50" | Fixed decimal places | "N0" | 1234567 | "1,234,567" | Thousand separators | "C" | 99.99 | "$99.99" | Currency | "X" | 255 | "FF" | Hexadecimal | "P" | 0.25 | "25.00 %" | Percentage | "F2" | 3.14159 | "3.14" | Fixed-point (2 decimals)
[S20] Boxing & Unboxing — Crossing the Type Divide | Boxing converts a value type (e.g. int) into an object by storing it on the heap. Unboxing extracts the value type back out of the object. It's how value types and reference types coexist — but it comes with a performance cost. | Boxing( | Implicit | ) | Unb | oxing( | Explicit | ) | Value → Object | Object → Value | Boxing and Unboxing
[S21] Thank You | See You Next Session

This means built-in types (like int and string) and custom classes all have the same basic functionality. Two Approaches Method ToString() Equals() What It Does Returns a string representation of the object Determines whether two objects are equal Returns a hash code (integer) used GetHashCode() in hash-based collections Returns the type of the current GetType() object at runtime .NET Track Default Behaviour Returns the fully qualified type name. Useless for debugging. Compares references (memory addresses). Types like string and int override to compare values. Based on the reference address. Different instances return different values, even if they contain identical data. Returns Namespace. TypeName. Used for retrieving type information at runtime (reflection). Override Strategy Always override for meaningful output. Override when value equality matters. Must pair with GetHashCode. Must override if Equals is overridden. Use consistent fields. Cannot override — sealed by the CLR."}]

ASP.Net Course  
C# Assignment 
Declare string title = "clean code";. Call title.ToUpper() and store it in a new variable upperTitle. Print 
both title and upperTitle to show that title did not change. 
Declare two separate string variables, both set to the literal "Clean Code". Use ReferenceEquals() 
to check if they point to the same object in memory. 
 
Create a StringBuilder, Append() the text "Book List", then Append() " - Updated" onto the same 
object. Print the final result. 
 
Using the StringBuilder from the question above, use Replace() to change "Book List" into "Library". 
Print the result. 
 
Given string title = "Clean Code"; and int pages = 464;, build the sentence "Book: Clean Code, 
Pages: 464" using the + operator. 
 
Build the same sentence as above, but using string interpolation ($"..."). 
 
Build the same sentence again, but using string.Format(). 
 
Given int pages = 464;, write an if / else statement that prints "Long Book" if pages is greater than 
300, otherwise prints "Short Book". 
 
Given int pages = 464; and bool isAvailable = true;, print "You can borrow this book" only if pages is 
greater than 300 and isAvailable is true. Use the && operator. 
 
Given string title = "Refactoring";, write a switch statement that prints "Great choice!" if the title is 
"Clean Code", "Nice pick!" if it's "Refactoring", and "Never heard of it" for anything else. 
 
Given int pages = 464;, use the ternary operator to store "Long Book" or "Short Book" into a 
variable sizeLabel (same rule as question 8: long if pages > 300). 
 
Given string[] books = { "Clean Code", "The Pragmatic Programmer", "Refactoring" };, use a for loop 
to print each book with its position number, like 1. Clean Code. 
 
1
[P02] Using the same books array, use a while loop to print every book title. 
 
Write a do-while loop that prints "Checking book..." exactly 3 times. 
 
Using the same books array, use a foreach loop to print every book title. 
 
Using the same books array, loop through it and print each title, but stop completely (break) once 
you reach "Refactoring". 
 
Using the same books array, print every title except "The Pragmatic Programmer" (skip it with 
continue, don't stop the loop). 
 
Write a method PrintFirstBook() that prints the first book in the books array. If the array is empty, 
use return to exit the method early instead of printing anything.

[S03] Control statements change the flow of execution: they decide what runs, when it runs, and how often. | Control Statements in C#
[S04] Conditional Statements | 1.1 if Statement | statement evaluates a condition and executes the associated block of code if the condition is true. | 1.2 else Statement | The else statement is used to provide an alternative block of code when the if condition is false.
[S05] Conditional Statements | 1.3 else if Statement | The else if statement allows for multiple conditions to be checked sequentially. | 1.4 switch Statement | The switch statement is used to select one of many code blocks to be executed based on the value of a variable.
[S06] Conditional Statements | A | switch | only needs to take one step | if | falls through 3 separate if cases
[S07] Loop | Statements | 2.1 for Loop | The for loop is used when the number of iterations is known beforehand. | 2.2 while Loop | The while loop executes as long as the specified condition is true. The condition is evaluated before each iteration
[S08] Loop Statements | 2.3 do-while Loop | The do-while loop is similar to the while loop, but the condition is evaluated after the loop's body, meaning the block of code will always execute at least once. | 2.4 foreach Loop | The foreach loop is used to iterate over collections such as arrays, lists, or other enumerable types.
[S09] for vs foreach | Aspect | for | foreach | Performance | ✅ Faster | ⚠️ Slightly slower | Collection Modification | ✅ Can modify | ❌ Cannot modify | Access To Index | ✅ Has access | ❌ No access | Readability | ⚠️ More code | ✅ Cleaner | while vs do-while | Aspect | while | do-while | Condition Check | Before the loop starts | After the loop runs | Execution | May not execute if false initially | Always executes at least once | Use Case | Execute only if condition is true at start | Must run at least once regardless | Loop Statements | Medium
[S10] Jump | Statements | 3.1 break Statement | Is used to exit from a loop or a switch statement. | 3.2 continue Statement | Is used to skip the current iteration of a loop and continue with the next iteration.
[S11] Jump Statements | 3.3 return Statement | Is used to exit from a method and optionally return a value. | 3.4 goto Statement | Is used to jump to a specific label within the code. It is generally not recommended due to its make code difficult to understand.
[S12] String in C# | string | Is a Built in Class [Reference Data Type] and represented as a sequence of characters. | They are | immutable | [once a string object is created, its value cannot be changed] | Any operation that modifies a string actually creates a new string object, leaving the original string unchanged. | Internally is an object that stores a sequence of UTF-16 char values. Each char occupies 2 bytes of memory.
[S13] String in C# | String immutability in C#
[S14] String in C# | String Interning in C# | C# stores identical string literals in a special memory area called the | String Intern Pool | .Instead of creating multiple copies of the same text, C# reuses one shared string object.This saves memory and can improve performance.
[S15] StringBuilder in C# | StringBuilder is a mutable class that lets you change text without creating a new string object each time. | It is a | mutable string | [if an object of stringbuilder is created, its value can be changed]
[S16] StringBuilder in C#
[S17] StringBuilder vs String
[S18] String Formatting in C# | String formatting is how you build readable text output by inserting values into a string. C# supports multiple styles: concatenation, interpolation, composite formatting, and formatting helpers. | Common Approaches | + | Concatenation (simple, but not ideal for many parts) | $"..." | interpolation (most readable, C# 6.0+) | string.Format | (older, still useful for localization) | Console.WriteLine | with placeholders
[S19] String Formatting in C#

C# Assignment  
Create a one-dimensional array double[] prices with the values 25.5, 40.0, 33.75. Print 
the second price (index 1). 
  
Create a 2x2 multidimensional array int[,] shelfCopies where shelf 0 has 3, 5 copies and 
shelf 1 has 1, 4 copies. Print the number of copies on shelf 1, slot 0. 
  
Write a method called PrintWelcomeMessage that takes no parameters and prints

Session 04 (Nullable Types - Null Operators - Arrays - User Defined Functions - Functions Parameters)
[S01] C# - Basics | Session 04
[S02] Session Agenda | 01 | Nullable Types | 02 | Null Operators | 03 | Arrays | 05 | Functions Parameters | 04 | User Defined Functions
[S03] Nullable Value Types | Nullable value types allow a value type to store | null | . | Nullable<T> | represents any struct type that holds all values of its underlying type | T | plus an additional | null | value. Use | int? | as shorthand for | Nullable<int> | . | 📌 | Introduced in C# 2.0 (2005) | Key Properties | Property | Description | Example | .HasValue | true | if the instance holds a real value | score.HasValue | → | false | .Value | Gets the underlying value. Throws | InvalidOperationException | if null! | score.Value | → | 💥 | crash! | .GetValueOrDefault() | Returns value or 0 if null — never throws | score.GetValueOrDefault() | → | 0 | .GetValueOrDefault(T) | Returns value or your custom fallback | score.GetValueOrDefault(5) | → | 5
[S04] Nullable Reference Types | Nullable Reference Types (NRT) | help prevent NullReferenceException by making nullability | explicit | in your code. The compiler warns you about potential null issues at build time — before your app even runs. | A variable of type | T | and a variable of type | T? | are the same .NET type. | 📌 Introduced in C# 8.0 (2019) | Non-nullable vs Nullable | Annotation | Meaning | Example | string | Must not be null (compiler expects assignment) | string name = "Ahmed"; | string? | Can be null, must be handled safely | string? nickname = null;
[S05] Null-Conditional Operator ?. | The null-conditional operator | ( | ?. | and | ?[] | ) safely accesses members and elements | only if the target is not null | . If it is null, the whole expression evaluates to | null | instead of throwing a | NullReferenceException | . | 📌 | Introduced in C# 6.0 (2015) | The Two Operators | Operator | Use | Example | ?. | Member access (properties, methods) | user?.Name | ?[] | Index access (arrays, lists) | names?[0] | Employee.Department.Name | if Employee is Null     => Throw Exception | if Department is Null => Throw Exception | if Name is Null           => Return Null | Employee?.Department?.Name | if Employee is Null => Stop Propagating | if Department is Null => Stop Propagating | No Exception Will be Thrown
[S06] Null-Coalescing Operators ?? ??= | Null-coalescing operators provide a | fallback value | when something is | null | . | ?? | returns the right side if the left is null. | ??= | assigns the right side only if the left is null — a concise way to set defaults. | 📌 | ?? in C# 2.0 (2005) | ??= in C# 8.0 (2019) | The Two Operators | Operator | What it does | Example | Result | ?? | Returns right if left is | null | name ?? "Guest" | "Guest" | if name is null | ??= | Assigns right only if left is | null | name ??= "Admin" | name becomes | "Admin" | only if it was null
[S07] Null-Forgiving Operator ! | The | null-forgiving operator | ( | ! | ) tells the compiler: "I know this value is not null." It | suppresses nullable warnings | at compile time. Use it when you have a strong guarantee that a value cannot be null, but the compiler can't prove it. | 📌 | Introduced in C# 8.0 (2019) | What It Does (and Doesn't Do) | Aspect | ✅ | Yes | ❌ | No | Compile time | Suppresses warnings | — | Runtime | — | Zero protection! | Still throws NRE if actually null | IL code generated | Identical to without | ! | No runtime check added
[S08] Arrays in C# | An array is a collection of elements of the same type, stored next to each other in memory. | Think of it like a row of lockers — each locker has a number (index) and holds one item. | Key Characteristics | Fixed Size | — once array is created, you can't change it during runtime (unless you create a new array) | Same Data Type | — all elements in an array must be of the same type (all ints, all strings) | Zero-Based Indexing | — the first element is always at index | [0] | , not | [1] | Fast access | — jump directly to any item by its index in O(1) time
[S09] Types of Arrays
[S10] User-Defined Functions (Methods) | A Method is a named code block that contains a series of statements. A program executes those statements by calling the method and specifying any required arguments.
[S11] Function Syntax
[S12] Function Parameters | Parameters are variables declared in the method signature that receive values from the caller. They allow methods to accept input and behave dynamically. | Type | Syntax | Behavior | Value (default) | (int x) | Copies the value. Changes inside don't affect the original. | ref | (ref int x) | Passes the reference. Changes affect the original variable. | out | (out int x) | Like ref, but the method | must | assign a value before exiting. | Optional | (int x = 10) | Caller can omit the argument; uses the default value. | params | (params int [ ] nums) | Accepts a variable number of arguments. | Common Parameter Types
[S13] Passing By Value — Value Type
[S14] Passing By Value — Reference Type
[S15] Passing By ref — Value Type
[S16] Passing By ref — Reference Type
[S17] Passing Reference Types | Point of Comparison | Passing By Value | Passing By ref | Mechanism | Passes a | copy of the reference | to the object. Both variables point to the same heap object. | Passes the | original reference | itself (alias). The parameter is literally the same variable with a different name. | Modifying | Members | ✅ Affects | the original object — both point to the same data in the heap. | ✅ Affects | the original object — same behavior. | Reassigning | the Variable | ❌ Won't affect | the original reference outside the method. The copy is reassigned, not the original. | ✅ Will affect | the original reference outside the method. You're reassigning the actual variable. | Modifying | the Reference | Method has a copy of the reference — | cannot modify the reference itself | (can't make it point elsewhere). | Method has the actual reference — | can modify the reference itself | (can make it point to a completely new object).
[S18] out Parameters | out | parameters allow a function to return multiple values. The variable does not need to be initialized before passing — the method must assign it before exiting.
[S19] Value vs ref vs out | POC | Passing by Value | Passing by ref | Passing by out | Initialization | Must be initialized before passing | Must be initialized before passing | Does | not | need to be initialized before passing | Value | Modification | ❌ | Changes inside method do | not | affect the original value (for value types) | ✅ | Changes inside method | affect | the original value | Method | must assign | a value to the parameter before returning | Limitation | Read value only — safe but limited | Read first, then Write [Optional modification] | Write first [Mandatory], then Read. Cannot read before writing inside the method.
[S20] Optional Parameters | Optional parameters have a default value. If no argument is passed, the default is used. This makes your methods more flexible and easier to call.
[S21] Named Parameters | Named parameters let you pass arguments by name, so you can change the order and skip optional parameters you don't want to set. This makes code more readable, especially with many parameters.
[S22] params Keyword (Variable-Length Parameters) | The | params | keyword allows a method to accept a variable number of arguments. It compiles them into an array automatically, so you don't need to create one manually.
[S23] Thank You | See You Next Session

C#  
ASP.Net Course  
C# Assignment  
Add a private string password = "secret"; field to a Book class. Try to print it from Main 
(outside the class). What happens, and why? 
 
Add an internal int copiesInStock = 5; field to Book. Print it from Main. Does it compile? 
Why? 
 
Add a public string Title; field to Book. Set it and print it from Main. 
 
Declare an enum Genre { Fiction, NonFiction, Science }. Add a Genre property to Book, 
assign it Genre.Science, and print it. 
 
Using the Genre enum above, print the underlying int value of 
Genre.Fiction, Genre.NonFiction, and Genre.Science by casting each to int. 
 
Given int genreNumber = 1;, cast it into a Genre value and print the result. 
 
Given Genre genre = Genre.Fiction;, convert it into a string using ToString() and print it. 
 
Given string genreText = "Science";, convert it into a Genre value using Enum.Parse() and 
print the result. 
 
Given string genreText = "Mystery"; (not a valid Genre value), use Enum.TryParse() to 
attempt the conversion. Print "Unknown genre" if it fails.

Task: Gym Management System 
Scenario
You are required to develop a simple Gym Management System using a Console Application.
The receptionist should be able to register a new gym member by entering the member’s information.
The application should validate all entered data, calculate the membership price automatically based on the selected membership type, and finally display the complete member information.
Requirements
1. Create Member Type
Create a type named Member that contains the following fields:
Id
Name
Age
Gender
MembershipType
MembershipPrice
 2. Read Member Information
The application should ask the user to enter the following information:
Member ID
Member Name
Member Age
Member Gender
Membership Type
The application must validate each input before moving to the next one.
3. Input Validation
Member ID
The entered ID must:
Be a valid integer.
Be greater than 0.
If the entered value is invalid, ask the user to enter it again.
Member Name
The entered name must:
Not null
If the entered value is invalid, ask the user to enter it again.
Member Age
The entered age must:
Be a valid integer.
Be between 16 and 50.
If the entered value is invalid, ask the user to enter it again.
Member Gender
Display the following menu:
Choose Gender:
1. Male
2. Female
The application should:
Accept only valid choices.
Membership Type
Display the following menu:
Choose Membership Type:
1. Standard
2. Premium
The application should:
Accept only valid choices.
Store the selected membership type.
Calculate the membership price automatically.
Membership prices:
Membership Type
Price
Standard
500
Premium
700
Note: The user should not enter the membership price manually.
4. Display Member Information
After successfully entering all member information:
Display the member details in a well-formatted output.

[S01] C# - Basics | Session 05
[S02] 01 | Class Library | 02 | Access Modifiers | 03 | User Defined Data Types | 04 | Enum | Session Agenda
[S03] Class Library | A | Class Library | is a separate project that contains reusable classes, but | has no Main method | and | cannot run on its own | . It compiles into a | .dll | file (Dynamic Link Library).
[S04] Access | Modifiers | Access modifiers | are keywords that control | who can access | your types (classes, structs) and their members (fields, methods, properties). | These modifiers determine where the members or types can be accessed inside the code
[S05] User Defined Data types | User-defined data types | allow developers to create custom types that represent real-world entities instead of relying only on primitive types like | int | , | string | , or | bool | . | Why Do We Need Custom Types?
[S06] User Defined Data types
[S07] User Defined Data types
[S08] Namespace | A namespace is a container that organizes related types (classes, structs, enums, interfaces) and prevents naming conflicts. Think of it as a folder for your code.
[S09] Class | A | class | is a blueprint that defines the | structure | and | behavior | of objects — it groups related data (fields) and actions (methods) together. Classes are | reference types | stored on the heap.
[S10] Struct | A | struct | is a lightweight | value type | that holds related data together — ideal for small, simple objects like coordinates, colors, or dates. Structs live on the stack (when not boxed), making them faster for short-lived data.
[S11] Interface | An | interface | defines a | contract | — a set of methods, properties, and events that a class or struct | must | implement. It says "what" to do, not "how" to do it. Interfaces enable polymorphism and loose coupling.
[S12] Enum | An | enum | (enumeration) is a value type that defines a set of | named constants | . It makes code more readable and self-documenting by replacing magic numbers with meaningful names.
[S13] Enum
[S14] Session Task | Documentation link
[S15] Thank You | See You Next Session

C# OOP Assignment 
 
OOP 01 - Smart Delivery Management System 
Part 01 : Theoretical Questions 
Question 1 
Consider the following code: 
 
 
a) What happens when a DeliveryAddress variable is copied into another variable and the copy is modified? 
b) What happens when a Customer variable is copied into another variable and one variable modifies the object? 
 
Question 2 
Consider the following class: 
 
 
a) Identify at least three problems with this design from an encapsulation perspective. 
b) How can private fields and public properties improve this design?
[P02] OOP 
ASP.Net Course 
Page 2 
 \ 
 
 
Part 02 : Practical 
Smart Delivery Management System 
User Story: You are building a simple Smart Delivery Management System for a delivery company. The system man-
ages shipment data, delivery addresses, prices, and shipment searching. Build it as a Console Application that reads data 
from the user and prints shipment information. 
What you need to build : 
1. Create a DeliveryAddress struct with: 
• City of type string. 
• Street of type string. 
• BuildingNumber of type int. 
 
• A constructor that initializes all fields. 
• A GetFullAddress() method that returns the complete address as one string. 
Create one DeliveryAddress value, copy it into a second variable, modify the copy, and print both values to prove that 
the original did not change. 
 
2. Create a Shipment class with: 
• TrackingCode. 
• Description. 
• Weight. 
• DeliveryFee. 
• Destination of type DeliveryAddress. 
Apply proper encapsulation using private fields and public properties with the following rules: 
• TrackingCode cannot be null, empty, or whitespace. 
• Description cannot be null, empty, or whitespace. 
• Weight must be greater than 0. 
• DeliveryFee must be greater than 0. 
• If an invalid value is assigned, keep the previous valid value.
[P03] OOP 
ASP.Net Course 
Page 3 
 \ 
 
Add the following properties: 
• TrackingCode: read-only from outside the class. 
• Description: read/write property with validation. 
• Weight: read/write property with validation. 
• DeliveryFee: public getter and private setter. 
• Destination: public read/write property. 
• EstimatedCost: calculated property that returns DeliveryFee + (Weight * 5). 
The EstimatedCost value must be calculated when requested and must not be stored in a separate field. 
 
3. Add constructor overloading to Shipment: 
• The first constructor receives only trackingCode. 
• The first constructor uses default values: Description = "Unknown", Weight = 1, DeliveryFee = 50, and a default 
destination. 
• The second constructor receives trackingCode, description, weight, deliveryFee, and destination. 
• Each constructor must initialize the object with valid data. 
 
4. Add the following methods to Shipment: 
• UpdateDeliveryFee(decimal newFee): updates the fee only when newFee is greater than 0. 
• PrintShipment(): prints all shipment information, including the estimated cost. 
5. Create a DeliveryCenter class: 
• The DeliveryCenter class should store up to 10 shipments using a private Shipment array. 
• Add an integer indexer this[int index] to get or set a shipment by position. 
• If the integer index is invalid, the getter returns null and the setter does nothing. 
• Add a string indexer this[string trackingCode] that returns the first shipment with the matching tracking code. 
• If no matching shipment is found, the string indexer returns null. 
• Add bool AddShipment(Shipment shipment), which adds the shipment to the first empty position and returns true. 
• Return false when the center is full.
[P04] OOP 
ASP.Net Course 
Page 4 
 \ 
 
6. In Main, build a Console Application that does the following: 
a) Create a DeliveryCenter object. 
b) Ask the user to enter data for three shipments. 
c) Create each Shipment and add it to the DeliveryCenter. 
d) Print the three shipments using the integer indexer. 
e) Ask the user to enter a tracking code. 
f) Search for the shipment using the string indexer. 
g) Print the shipment when found, or print "Shipment not found." 
h) Demonstrate the DeliveryAddress struct copy behavior.

C# OOP Assignment
OOP 02 – Smart Delivery Management System
Part 01 : Theoretical Questions
Question 1
Answer the following questions:
a) What is the difference between a class and a struct?
b) Why are classes more suitable than structs for large applications?
Question 2
Consider the following code:
a) Which class is the parent class?
b) Which class is the child class?
c) What members are inherited by ExpressShipment?
d) Why is inheritance better than duplicating the same code in multiple classes?
Part 02 : Practical
Smart Delivery Management System
User Story
In Assignment 01, you built a simple Smart Delivery Management System using structs.
Now that you have learned Classes, Inheritance, Constructor Chaining, Access Modifiers, and Class Relationships, you will refactor your project to support multiple shipment types while keeping the existing functionality.
Before You Start
Important Note
In Assignment 01, the following types were implemented as structs:
Shipment
DeliveryCenter
Before starting this assignment:
Convert Shipment into a class.
Convert DeliveryCenter into a class.
Keep DeliveryAddress as a struct, since it represents a value object.
Do not remove any functionality implemented in Assignment 01.
What You Need to Build
1. Shipment Class
Reuse your Shipment class from Assignment 01.
The class should still contain the following properties:
Property
Type
TrackingCode
string
Description
string
Weight
decimal
DeliveryFee
decimal
Destination
DeliveryAddress
Keep all validation rules from Assignment 01.
The class should also keep:
Constructor Overloading
EstimatedCost property
UpdateDeliveryFee()
PrintShipment()
2. Create Three Shipment Types
StandardShipment
Create a class named StandardShipment that inherits from Shipment.
This class does not contain any additional properties.
Create a constructor that initializes all inherited members using constructor chaining.
ExpressShipment
Create a class named ExpressShipment that inherits from Shipment.
Add the following property:
Property
Type
ExtraFee
decimal
Requirements:
ExtraFee must be greater than or equal to 0.
Override the EstimatedCost property to include the extra fee.
Formula:
DeliveryFee + (Weight × 5) + ExtraFee
Create a constructor that initializes all inherited members and ExtraFee.
InternationalShipment
Create a class named InternationalShipment that inherits from Shipment.
Add the following properties:
Property
Type
DestinationCountry
string
CustomsFee
decimal
Requirements:
DestinationCountry cannot be null, empty, or whitespace.
CustomsFee must be greater than or equal to 0.
Override the EstimatedCost property to include the customs fee.
Formula:
DeliveryFee + (Weight × 5) + CustomsFee
Create a constructor that initializes all inherited members and the new properties.
3. DeliveryCenter Class
Extend your DeliveryCenter class.
The class should contain:
Member             
Type
CenterName
string
Shipments
Shipment[]
Requirements:
The center can store up to 20 shipments.
The Shipment array must be private.
Keep the indexers from Assignment 01.
Keep the AddShipment() method from Assignment 01.
Add the following methods:
RemoveShipment
Searches for a shipment using its tracking code.
If found:
Remove the shipment.
Return true.
Otherwise:
Return false.
PrintAllShipments
void PrintAllShipments()
Print all stored shipments.
4. Demonstrate Class Relationships
Your project must demonstrate the following relationships.
Inheritance
Shipment
├── StandardShipment
├── ExpressShipment
└── InternationalShipment
5. In Main
Build a Console Application that performs the following:
Create a DeliveryCenter.
Read the center name from the user.
Create one StandardShipment.
Create one ExpressShipment.
Create one InternationalShipment.
Read all shipment data from the user.
Add the shipments to the delivery center.
Print all shipments.
Search for a shipment using the existing tracking code indexer.
Remove one shipment using its tracking code.
Print the remaining shipments.
