ASSIGNMENT 03
Smart Delivery Management System
Polymorphism · Binding · Class Relationships · Sealed Classes & Methods
Builds on Assignment 02 — keep all existing functionality
Part 01 — Theoretical Questions
Q1  Overloading, Overriding, and Binding
a)  What is the difference between Method Overloading and Method Overriding?
b)  What is the difference between Static Binding and Dynamic Binding?
Q2  Sealed Classes and Methods
a)  What is the purpose of the sealed keyword when applied to a class?
b)  What is the difference between a sealed class and a sealed method?
c)  Can a sealed method be overridden? Why?
Part 02 — Practical
Continue from your Assignment 02 project. Nothing that already works should be removed — you are extending behavior, not replacing it.
1  Update the Shipment Class
Keep every member from Assignment 02, then make two members polymorphic:
Member
Change
EstimatedCost
Convert to a virtual property so each derived class can calculate its own cost.
PrintShipment()
Convert to a virtual method. Every child class will override it.
 
Method Overloading — add two versions of the weight-update method:
#
Behavior
1
Updates the shipment weight.
2
Updates the shipment weight after adding the extra packing weight.
2  Constructor Chaining
Every derived class calls the base Shipment constructor with base(...) instead of repeating its initialization code.
Derived Class
Must chain to
StandardShipment
base(...) → Shipment
ExpressShipment
base(...) → Shipment
InternationalShipment
base(...) → Shipment
Figure 1 — Class hierarchy: inheritance, and where the sealed class/method sit.
3  Override EstimatedCost
Class
Formula
StandardShipment
uses the inherited calculation, unmodified
ExpressShipment
DeliveryFee + (Weight × 5) + ExtraFee
InternationalShipment
DeliveryFee + (Weight × 5) + CustomsFee
4  Override PrintShipment()
Every derived class overrides PrintShipment(). Base fields are inherited; each row below is additional to the base set.

5  Class Relationships
Aggregation — create a Driver class (DriverId, FullName, PhoneNumber), then add a Driver property to DeliveryCenter. The driver must be able to exist independently of the delivery center.
Composition — every Shipment owns exactly one DeliveryAddress. It cannot outlive its shipment.
Figure 2 — Aggregation (Driver) vs. Composition (DeliveryAddress).
6  Update DeliveryCenter
Keep: the Shipment array, AddShipment(), RemoveShipment(), and both indexers — all reused from Assignment 02.
Modify PrintAllShipments() to loop through the array and simply call shipment.PrintShipment(); — no manual type-checking. That single call resolving to a different method per object is dynamic binding.
Figure 3 — Dynamic binding: one call, resolved per object at runtime.
7  Create DeliveryHelper
A static class with one method: void PrintShipmentDetails(Shipment shipment). It calls shipment.PrintShipment(); — whichever override matches the object's real type runs automatically.
8  Sealed Class
Create CompletedShipment, inheriting from Shipment, and mark the class sealed.
9  Sealed Method
In InternationalShipment, add a virtual GenerateCustomsReport(). In PriorityInternationalShipment (inherits from InternationalShipment), override it and mark that override sealed.
10  Main() Checklist
☐  a. Create a Driver.
☐  b. Create a DeliveryCenter.
☐  c. Assign the Driver to the DeliveryCenter.
☐  d. Create one StandardShipment.
☐  e. Create one ExpressShipment.
☐  f. Create one InternationalShipment.
☐  g. Add all shipments to the DeliveryCenter.
☐  h. Print all shipments using PrintAllShipments().
☐  i. Call DeliveryHelper.PrintShipmentDetails() for each shipment.
☐  j. Demonstrate both versions of UpdateWeight().
☐  k. Build a Shipment[] holding mixed types and print all of them in a loop.
☐  l. Demonstrate the sealed class and sealed method (comments or code).

[@01:30|t=90] Binding ROUTE Is the Process by which the runtime or compiler decides which method implementation to execute for a given method call 1. Early Binding (Static Binding) Resolved at compile time by the compiler. Faster — the target address is fixed before the program runs. The reference type decides. Occurs with: • Method Overloading • Method Hiding (new) • Non-virtual methods Static methods Overload resolution happens here too: the compiler picks which Add ( ) to call from the declared argument types, long before the program runs. .NET Track 2. Late Binding (Dynamic Binding) Resolved at run time by the CIR. Slightly slower — the lookup happens on every call. The actual Object in memory decides. Occurs with: • Method Overriding (virtuat / override) • Abstract methods • Interface methods This is What makes polymorphism work: one reference can run many different Speak ( ) bodies — the CLR looks up the right one on every call. Smart Delivery Management System
Abstraction · Abstract Classes · Interfaces · Interface Polymorphism
Builds on Assignment 03 — keep all existing functionality
Part 01 — Theoretical Questions
Q1  Abstraction
a)  What is Abstraction in Object-Oriented Programming?
b)  Why is abstraction considered one of the four pillars of OOP?
Q2  Abstract Classes vs. Interfaces
a)  What is the difference between an Abstract Class and an Interface?
b)  When would you choose an Interface instead of an Abstract Class?
c)  Can a class inherit from multiple abstract classes? Can it implement multiple interfaces?
Part 02 — Practical
The delivery company is growing, and many new shipment types will be added in the future. Continue from your Assignment 03 project — nothing that already works should be removed.

7  Update DeliveryCenter
Reuse the existing DeliveryCenter. Add void PrintTrackingStatuses() — it loops through all shipments and prints their tracking status using the ITrackable interface.

[S01] OOP | Session 04
[S02] Session Agenda | 01 | Abstraction | 02 | Interface | 03 | Interface Advanced Topics | 04 | Abstract Class
[S03] Abstraction In OOP
[S04] WHAT IS ABSTRACTION? Abstraction is the process of hiding the implementation details and showing only the essential features of an object to the user. Focus on WHAT Hide the HOW
BENEFITS Reduces complexity Improves maintainability Enhances security (hides sensitive details) Promotes flexibility and reusability
[S05] HOW IS ABSTRACTION ACHIEVED IN
1. Abstract Class Provides a blueprint with abstract and non-abstract members. public abstract class Shape public abstract double Area(); public void Display() // no body Console. WriteLine("This is a shape");
2. Interface Provides a contract with only method signatures (no implementation). public interface IDrawab1e void Draw(); // no body public class Circle . IDrawab1e public void Draw() Console . WriteLine( "Drawing Circle") ;
[S06] EXAMPLE
public abstract class Animal public abstract void Sound(); public class Dog : Animal public override void Sound() Console . WriteLine( "Bark " public class Cat : Animal public override void Sound() Console . WriteLine( "Meow" ) // Abstraction
Animal (abstract) + Sound() Dog + Sound() Cat + Sound()
// Usage Animal al Animal a2 al. Sound(); a2. Sound(); new Dog(); new Cat(); // Output: // Output: // Only Bark Neow ' Sound ' is known from Animal
We know that Animal has Sound(), but the actual implementation is provided by Dog and Cat.
[S07] WHEN TO USE ABSTRACTION?
When you want to provide a common structure for related classes.
When you want to hide complex implementation details.
When you expect future changes and want to keep code flexible.
When multiple classes should have the same behavior.
[S08] KEY POINTS You cannot create an object of an abstract class. You must inherit from an abstract class and implement its abstract members. Interfaces can be implemented by classes (multiple interfaces can be implemented). Abstraction helps in designing loosely coupled systems. Implementation details are hidden. Only essential features are shown.
[S09] Interface
[S10] WHAT IS AN INTERFACE?
IShape + DrawO + Area() : double + Perimeter() : double It defines a contract. Classes that implement the interface must provide the implementation. Circle Rectangle
An interface is a reference type that can contain only method, property, event, indexer and constant definitions.
[S11] SYNTAX interface I InterfaceName // methods (no body) returnType MethodName(parameters) ; // properties type PropertyName { get; set; } // events event EventHand1er EventName; // indexers returnType this [type index] { get; // constants type ConstantName = value; set;
Key Rules Members are public by default (cannot use private, protected, or intemal). Methods have no body. Fields are not allowed (only constants). A class or struct implements an interface using : llnterface.
[S12] EXAMPLE
// 1. Interface definition public interface IShape void Draw(); double Area();
// 2. Class implementing the interface public class Circle : IShape private double radius; public Circle(double radius) this. radius = radius; public void Draw() Console . a Circle"); public double Area() return Math. PI * radius * radius;
[S13] IMPLEMENTING AN INTERFACE A class or struct uses the interface members by providing their own implementation. A class can implement multiple interfaces. Interface members must be implemented explicitly or implicitly (by matching name and signature).
IMoveble + Move() Car + Move() + Runo IRunnable + Run()
[S14] WHEN TO USE INTERFACE? O When you want to define a common behavior for unrelated classes. When you want to achieve loose coupling. When you want to support multiple inheritance of type. When you are building a plugin-based or scalable system.
[S15] INTERFACE POLYMORPHISM
Interface polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common interface.
How it works We use an interface reference to point to objects of any class that implements that interface. The actual method called at runtime is determined by the object, not the reference (dynamic binding).
CreditCardPayment Pay() IPayment Pay(decimal amount) PayPalPayment Pay() CashPayment Pay()
[S16] Example
public interface IPayment void Pay (decimal amount) ;
public class CreditCardPaym€nt IPayment public void Pay (decimal amount) Console . { amount} using Credit Card") ; public class PayPalPayment IPayment public void Pay (decimal amount) Console . WriteLine(S "Paid {amount} public class CashPayment IPayment public void Pay (decimal amount) Console . WriteLine(S "Paid {amount) using PayPal" in Cash"
[S17] public class Program public static void ProcessPayment(IPayment payment, payment . Pay (amount) ; // Polymorphic call public static void Main() IPayment pl new CreditCardPayment() ; = new PayPalPayment(); IPayment p2 new Cashpayment() ; IPayment p3 ProcessPayment (pl, lee ) ; ProcessPayment(p2, 299) ; ProcessPayment(p3, 50) ; decimal amount)
Output Paid 100 using Credit Card Paid 200 using PayPal Paid 50 in Cash
Key Takeaway We can write methods that work with any implementation of an interface. This gives us flexibility and makes our code easy to extend.
Benefits Loose coupling Easier testing (mocking) Easy to add new implementations Follows SOLID principles (DIP)
[S18] MULTIPLE INTERFACE IMPLEMENTATION
A single class can implement more than one interface.
Syntax class ClassName Interfacel, Interface2, InterfaceN // Implement members of all interfaces
[S19] Example
public interface IPrintab1e void Print(); public interface ISaveab1e Console. WriteLine( "Document printed") ; void Save(); public class Document . IPrintab1e, ISaveab1e public void ublic void Print() Save() Console . WriteLine( "Document saved'
Diagram IPrintable + print ( ) ISaveable + Save() Document (implements both)
[S20] public class Program public static void Main() Document doc = new Document(); doc; IPrintab1e printer = ISaveab1e saver doc; printer . Print() ; saver . Save() ; // reference to IPrintab1e // reference to ISaveab1e // calls Document. Print() // calls Document. Save()
Output Document printed Document saved
Key Takeaway A class can implement multiple interfaces and provide implementations for all their members.

[S21] Interface Advanced Topics

ASSIGNMENT 05 
Smart Delivery Management System 
Object Copying · Shallow Copy · Deep Copy · Static Members · Extension Methods · Partial Classes & Methods 
Builds on Assignment 04 — keep all existing functionality 
Part 01 — Theoretical Questions 
Q1  Object Copying 
a) What happens when you assign one object variable to another object variable? 
b) Does assigning one object to another create a new object? Explain. 
c) What is the difference between copying an object and copying its reference? 
Q2  Shallow Copy vs Deep Copy 
a) What is a Shallow Copy? 
b) What is a Deep Copy? 
c) What happens to reference-type members when a Shallow Copy is created? 
d) What happens to reference-type members when a Deep Copy is created? 
e) Give one situation where Deep Copy would be safer than Shallow Copy. 
Q3  Static Members 
a) What is a static field, and how is it different from an instance field? 
b) What is a static method? Can a static method directly access instance members? 
c) What is a static constructor, and when is it executed? 
d) What is a static class? Can you create an object from a static class?
[P02] Q4  Extension Methods 
a) What is an Extension Method? 
b) What keyword must be used in the first parameter of an extension method? 
c) Where must an extension method be declared? 
d) Can an extension method access private members of the class it extends? 
Q5  Partial Classes and Partial Methods 
a) What is a Partial Class? 
b) Why would a developer split one class into multiple files? 
c) What is a Partial Method? 
d) What happens if a declared partial method has no implementation? 
Part 02 — Practical 
Continue from your Assignment 04 project. Nothing that already works should be removed — you are extending the existing 
system. 
1  Object Copying 
Add object-copying functionality to the Shipment class. 
• Create a method: Shipment CopyShipment(). 
• The method should create a copy of the current shipment. 
• Demonstrate the difference between assigning one object variable to another and creating an actual copy. 
Shipment shipment2 = shipment1; 
2  Shallow Copy 
• Create Shipment ShallowCopy(). 
• Use MemberwiseClone() to create the copy. 
• The original and copied Shipment objects must be different objects. 
• Their DeliveryAddress objects must still reference the same object. 
• Change the address through the copied shipment and demonstrate that the original shipment's address is also 
affected. 
3  Deep Copy 
• Create Shipment DeepCopy(). 
• The Deep Copy must create a new Shipment and a new DeliveryAddress. 
• Change the address of the copied shipment; the original address must remain unchanged. 
Demonstration

After changing copied address 
Cairo

Same DeliveryAddress object? 
False 
False
[P03] 4  Static Field 
• Add a static field to Shipment: TotalShipmentsCreated. 
• It should keep track of the total number of Shipment objects created. 
• Every time a shipment is created, increment the counter. 
• The value must be shared between all shipment objects. 
5  Static Constructor 
• Add a static constructor to Shipment. 
• Initialize the shipment counter and display a message indicating that static initialization has happened. 
• The static constructor must not be called manually. 
Shipment System Initialized 
6  Static Method 
• Add: static int GetTotalShipmentsCreated(). 
• Return the total number of shipment objects created. 
• Call the method without creating a Shipment object just to access the method. 
Total Shipments Created : 3 
7  Static Class 
• Create a static class named DeliveryUtilities. 
• Add static methods: PrintSeparator() and PrintSystemTitle(). 
• Use these methods throughout Main() instead of repeatedly writing the same separator/title code. 
==========================================​
Delivery Center​
========================================== 
8  Extension Methods 
• Create a static class named ShipmentExtensions. 
• Add string GetSummary(this Shipment shipment). 
• The summary must contain Tracking Code, Shipment Type, Weight, and Tracking Status. 
SH001 | Standard | 3 KG | In Transit 
• Add bool IsDelivered(this Shipment shipment). 
• Return true only when the tracking status is Delivered. 
shipment.GetSummary();​
shipment.IsDelivered();
[P04] 9  Partial Shipment Class 
• Convert the existing Shipment class into a partial class. 
• Split it into at least two files: Shipment.cs and Shipment.Tracking.cs. 
• Shipment.cs should contain the main properties, constructor, EstimatedCost, PrintShipment(), and other existing 
functionality. 
• Shipment.Tracking.cs should contain tracking-related members such as tracking status, GetTrackingStatus(), and 
UpdateTrackingStatus(). 
• The program must continue to work exactly as before. 
File 
Suggested Responsibility 
Shipment.cs 
Main shipment members, constructor, cost, printing, existing 
functionality 
Shipment.Tracking.cs 
Tracking status and tracking-related functionality 
10  Partial Method 
• Declare a partial method: partial void OnTrackingStatusChanged(string newStatus); 
• Call it from UpdateTrackingStatus(). 
• Implement the partial method in another part of the Shipment class. 
• Display a message when the tracking status changes. 
Tracking status changed to: Out For Delivery 
Demonstrate that the declaration and implementation belong to the same Shipment class even though they are in different files. 
11  Main() Checklist 
☐  Demonstrate reference assignment between two shipment variables. 
☐  Demonstrate that reference assignment does not create a new object. 
☐  Create a Shallow Copy using MemberwiseClone(). 
☐  Demonstrate that the shallow copy shares the same DeliveryAddress. 
☐  Create a Deep Copy. 
☐  Demonstrate that the deep copy has an independent DeliveryAddress. 
☐  Add and demonstrate the static shipment counter. 
☐  Demonstrate the static constructor. 
☐  Call GetTotalShipmentsCreated(). 
☐  Create and use DeliveryUtilities. 
☐  Create and use ShipmentExtensions. 
☐  Demonstrate GetSummary(). 
☐  Demonstrate IsDelivered(). 
☐  Split Shipment into partial class files. 
☐  Implement and demonstrate the partial method.

[S01] Session 05 C# | OOP
[S02] Session Agenda | 01 | Object Copying | 02 | Static | 03 | Extension Methods | 04 | Partial
[S03] Object Copying
[S04] -O- KEY CONCEPT In C#, copying an object can mean different things: • • Value types actual values are copied. Reference types -i only the reference is copied (shallow copy). To copy all fields of a reference type, use shallow copy or deep copy.
[S05] VALUE TYPE COPY Value types are copied by value. int a = 10 int b // copy Console. WriteLine(a) ; Console . WriteLine (b) ; // 10 // 20 a b Stack (Value Types) 10 20 Actual value is copied.
REFERENCE ASSIGNMENT (SHALLOW COPY) Only the reference is copied. Person pl = new Person { Name = "Ahmed" // copy reference Person p2 = pl; p2 . Name = "Omar" ; Console. WriteLine(pI. Name); // Omar Stack Heap Person Object Name: "Omar" Both refer to the same object.
[S06] SHALLOW COPY
WHAT IS SHALLOW COPY? A shallow copy creates a new object and copies all value-type fields. For reference-type fields, only the references (links) are copied — both objects point to the same nested objects.

[S28] Partial
[S29] A partial class allows you to split the definition of a class into multiple files. All parts are combined by the compiler into a single class.
// File 1: Student-Core.cs public partial class Student public int ld { get; set; public string Name { get; // File 2: Student. Extra.cs set; public partial public void class Student Display( ) Console . WriteLine ($ " {ld} {Name} " ) ;
[S30] How it works • All parts with the same class name and namespace are combined by the compiler. • The resulting class behaves as if it was written in a single file. • Members from all parts can access each other.
O Why it exists To organize large classes across multiple files. To separate auto-generated code from custom code. To allow different team members or tools to extend a class without modifying the original file. To improve maintainability and readability.
[S31] EXAMPLE
File 1: Product.cs (written by you) public partial class Product public int ld { get; set; } public string Name { get; set; } public decimal Price { get; set; } public decimal Get TotalPrice(int quantity) return Price * quantity;

[S33] Rules • All parts must use the 'partial' keyword. • All parts must be in the same namespace. • All parts must have the same accessibility (e.g., all public). • All parts must be compiled together in the same assembly.

[@00:45|t=45] Generic Constraints Constraints allow you to specify which types can be used as type arguments for a generic type or method. They enable you to: • Access members of the constrained type safely. • Enforce capabilities (e.g., must be a class, struct, etc.). • Prevent invalid type arguments at compile time. Online Store Order Processing 
 
You just got hired as a junior developer at "ShopMaster", a 
growing online store. Your manager gives you a list of features 
to build for the store's backend system. The system needs to 
handle products, orders, notifications, and reports. "We need 
this system to be flexible. Tomorrow we might add new 
product categories, new discount rules, new notification 
channels, new report formats... so don't hardcode anything. I 
want to be able to plug in new behavior without changing 
existing code — making the system easy to extend without 
modification."

Task 01 : Smart Product Search 
 
Manager: "Customers search in all kinds of ways - by category, by price, by name, 
by stock... and the list keeps growing. I need ONE search method that works for 
any filter, now and in the future, without being modified”.​
​
What You Need To Do: Write a single method called SearchProducts that accepts 
two parameters:  
1. The product list (List<Product>)  
2. A delegate representing the filter condition (Func<Product , bool>)  
 
The method should return a List containing only the products that satisfy the 
condition. Then, call this method four times with different lambda expressions to 
perform the following searches:  
1. All Electronics products  
2. Products cheaper than $50  
3. Products that are in stock (Stock > 0)  
4. Clothing products under $100 
 
Expected Output:  
3

Task 03 : Custom Report Generator 
 
Manager: "We need different reports from the same data - a quick summary, 
a detailed breakdown, a low-stock alert. Build one reporting engine where 
the caller controls the format. Use the built-in delegates this time." 
 
 
3.1  Print Reports  
Write a method called PrintReport that accepts the product list and an 
Action. The method loops through all products and calls the action on each 
one. The caller decides what to print by passing a lambda.  
Scenario 1  Short Report: Print each product as Name - $Price  
Scenario 2  Detailed Report: Print each product as [Category] Name | Price: 
$X | Stock: Y

Func.  
The method returns a List by applying the function to each product.  
Scenario 3 Summary List: Transform each product into a string like "Laptop 
($1200)". Print all results.  
Scenario 4 Price Label: Transform each product into "Expensive!" if Price > 
$100, or "Affordable" otherwise. Print each as Name: Label.

for each in the format: [LOW STOCK] Name: only X left!

6

[S21] Anonymous Methods
[S22] An anonymous method is a block of code that has no name. • It can be assigned to a delegate. Useful when the method is short and used only once. Helps in writing concise and readable code.
Key Point Anonymous methods are less commonly used today because lambda expressions (=>) are more concise and preferred.
WHAT IS AN ANONYMOUS METHOD?
SYNTAX
delegate (parameters) // statements
Example An anonymous method that matches the delegate Action<int, int>: delegate (int x, int y) Console. WriteLine(x + y);
[S23] Using Anonymous Methods
[S24] WHEN TO USE? • Use anonymous methods when you are working with older code or APIs that expect delegates. • Prefer lambda expressions for new code for better readability.
IMPORTANT NOTES • • • Anonymous methods can be converted to a delegate type. They are ideal for short, one-time use logic. They can access variables from their parent scope (closure). Lambdas are syntactic sugar over anonymous methods.
[S25] Lambda Expression
[S26] WHAT IS A LAMBDA EXPRESSION?
A to lambda expression is a short, inline way write an anonymous method. It has no name. It can be used to create delegates or expression trees. It is more concise and readable than anonymous methods.
Key Point Lambda expressions (2>) are the preferred way of writing anonymous functions in modern C#.
Lambda Syntax y; (parameters) (parameters) expression ; ( statements; // one expression // multiple statements

Exercise 1: Student Grade Manager
Create a program that manages student grades using One Of Collections
Create a Collection with these grades: 85, 92, 78, 95, 88, 70, 100, 65
Print the collection, Count, first and last grade
Sort the grades ascending, then print
Get the first grade above 90
Get all grades below 75 (failing grades)
Remove all failing grades (below 75)
Check if any grade equals 100
Create a List<string> where each grade becomes "Grade: X"
Exercise 2: Leaderboard
Create a leaderboard that automatically sorts players by score.
Add: 500="Ahmed", 200="Sara", 800="Ali", 350="Mona"
Print all entries (they should be sorted by score automatically)
Access the first key and first value 
Check if score 500 exists
Safely get the player with score 999
Remove the player with score 200 and print the updated list
Exercise 3: Phone Book
Build a phone book application.
Create a Collection  with 4 contacts (name → phone number)
Add a new contact using [] syntax (add or update)
Try adding a duplicate using .Add() — catch the exception and print the error
Try adding a duplicate using .TryAdd() — print whether it succeeded
Search for a contact that doesn’t exist
Get a contact with a fallback of "Not Found"
Print all Keys on one line, then all Values on another line
Exercise 4: Unique Email Validator
Use Collection to manage unique email addresses.
Create a HashSet<string> with a case-insensitive comparer: new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
Add these emails: "ahmed@test.com", "AHMED@test.com", "sara@test.com", "Sara@Test.Com"
Print Count — how many are actually stored? Explain why.
Create two sets: Set A = {1,2,3,4,5} and Set B = {4,5,6,7,8}
Print the result of: UnionWith, IntersectWith, ExceptWith
Use IsSubsetOf to check if {1,2} is a subset of Set A

[S10] Why Async Programming ?
[S11] Think of it like... Instead of standing in line and waiting for your coffee, you place the order, sit at a table, and do other things until it's ready.
Asynchronous programming allows your program to start a long-running operation and continue doing other work instead of waiting (blocking) for that operation to finish.
[S12] Asynchronous (Non-Blocking) The thread starts the operation and continues working. Start operation Benefits Operation runs in the background Continue working Operation completes (later) Thread remains free to do other work. Better responsiveness (Ul stays responsive). Higher throughput and better performance. More efficient use of threads. Scales better to handle more concurrent operations.
Synchronous (Blocking) The thread waits for the operation to complete. Start Waiting (blocked) Continue work Done Thread is idle (blocked) during the wait time. Problems X X X X Thread is blocked and cannot do anything else. Poor responsiveness (Ul freezes). Wastes thread resources. Doesn't scale well with many users.

[@05:15|t=315] The Blocking Problem 1) What is Blocking? STOP A blocking operation makes the current thread wait until the operation finishes. During this time, the thread cannot do anything else. Examples: • Reading a file • Calling a slow API • Waiting for a database 2) In a Single-Threaded Application If the main thread calls a slow (blocking) operation, it cannot process anything else until that operation completes. Demo.sql
04 Database\Khaled Ahmed\Session 08\Demo\Demo.sql
Khaled Ahmed
Session 08
USE Hospital;
GO
--=========================================================
-- TRIGGERS
--=========================================================
--=========================================================
-- 1. AFTER INSERT
--=========================================================
-- Log every new patient.
Create table PatientAudit
(
AuditId int primary key Identity(1,1),
PatientId int,
ActionType nvarchar(20),
ActionDate DateTime

)

Go
Create or alter trigger Trg_Patients_AfterInsert         -- Clean Code
on Patients
After Insert
as
Insert into PatientAudit
Select Id,'Insert',GETDATE()
from inserted

go

Insert into Patients(Id,Name,DOB,WardId)
values(303,'Amr Mohsen','1997-06-08',1)  

Select *
from PatientAudit


Drop table if exists PatientAudit


--=========================================================
-- 2. AFTER UPDATE
--=========================================================
-- Log old and new salary.

Create table ConsultantSalaryAudit
(
AuditId int primary key identity (1,1),
ConsultantId int,  
OldSalary decimal (18,0),  --deleted
NewSalary decimal(18,0),  --inserted
ActionDate Datetime
)

go
Create or alter trigger Trg_Consultant_AfterUpdate
on Consultants
after Update
as
--Update (Salary) => if not return
--If Name or DOB Changed => don't audit any transactions

if Not Update(Salary)
     Return;
Insert into ConsultantSalaryAudit
Select D.Id,D.Salary,I.Salary,GETDATE()
from deleted D
join inserted I
on D.Id=I.Id
where I.Salary <> D.Salary

go


Update Consultants
set Salary=Salary
where Id=303


Drop table if exists ConsultantSalaryAudit
--=========================================================
-- 3. AFTER DELETE
--=========================================================
Create table DeletedPatients
(
PatientId Int,
PatientName nvarchar(100),
DOB Date,
WardId Int,
DeletedDate DateTime
)

go
Create or alter trigger Trg_Patients_AfterDelete
on Patients
After Delete
as

Insert into DeletedPatients
Select Id,Name,DOB,WardId,GETDATE()
from deleted

go




-- Keep a copy of deleted patients.


Delete from Patients
WHERE Id in (301,302,303)



--=========================================================
-- 4. INSTEAD OF INSERT
--=========================================================
-- Block inserts: the trigger runs instead of the INSERT.

go
Create or alter trigger Trg_Patients_InsteadOfInsert
on Patients
Instead of Insert
as

Print 'Inserting inside Patient Not Allowed'

go


Insert into Patients (Id,Name,DOB,WardId)
values(301,'Blocked Patient','1990-01-01',1) 


--(1 row affected)  => search



--=========================================================
-- 5. INSTEAD OF UPDATE
--=========================================================
-- Reject salary cuts, otherwise do the update ourselves.
go
Create or alter trigger trg_Consultant_NoSalaryCut
On Consultants
Instead of Update
as
begin

If Exists (select 1  from Inserted I Join deleted D on I.Id=D.Id
                      where I.Salary<D.Salary  )

        BEGIN
          RAISERROR('Salary Cannot be reduced',16,1);
           Return;
        End;

        Update C
        Set C.Salary =I.Salary
        From Consultants C 
        Join Inserted I
        on C.Id=I.Id


END
go



Update Consultants
Set Salary =Salary+10000
where Id=303



Drop trigger [trg_Consultant_NoSalaryCut]

enable trigger  [Trg_Patients_InsteadOfInsert] on Patients

--=========================================================
-- 6. INSTEAD OF DELETE
--=========================================================
-- Block deletes.
go
Create or alter trigger trg_Patients_BlockDelete
on Patients
Instead of Delete
as
Raiserror('Patient Cannot be deleted',16,1);

go


Delete
from Patients
where Id=300


--=========================================================
-- INDEXES
--=========================================================
-- Example 1: Filtering by Id
-- ============================================
-- The Id column has a Clustered Index.
-- Since the query filters using the indexed column (Id),
-- SQL Server can directly navigate through the index
-- to find the required row instead of scanning all rows.
-- This results in an Index Seek.

Select *
from Patients
where Id=201


-- ============================================
-- Example 2: Filtering by Name
-- ============================================
-- The Name column does NOT have an index.
-- Therefore, SQL Server cannot use an index to directly
-- locate the rows where Name = 'Ahmed'.
-- It needs to scan the available index/data to find matching rows.
-- The execution plan may show an Index Scan if a suitable
-- nonclustered/clustered index is being scanned.

Select *
from Patients
where Name ='Ahmed'


-- ============================================
-- Example 3: Creating a Table Without Any Index
-- ============================================
-- This table has no Primary Key and no indexes.
-- Therefore, it is stored as a Heap.
-- A Heap is a table that does not have a Clustered Index.
Create table PatientsHeap(
Id int,
Name varchar(50)
)



-- ============================================
--  Filtering a Heap Table
-- ============================================
-- The PatientsHeap table has no indexes.
-- SQL Server has no index structure that it can use
-- to directly locate Id = 1.
-- Therefore, SQL Server must scan the entire table
-- row by row to find the matching record.
-- This appears in the execution plan as a Table Scan.


select *
from PatientsHeap
where Id =1


--=========================================================
-- 1. CLUSTERED INDEX
--=========================================================
-- Create Employees Table

Create table Employees
(
Id int primary key,
Name varchar(50),
Salary decimal(18,2),
age int
)
-- ============================================
-- A Primary Key is created on the Id column.
-- In SQL Server, a Primary Key is created as a
-- Clustered Index by default
-- The Id column will have a Clustered Index.



-- ============================================
-- Filter by Id
-- ============================================
-- Id has a Clustered Index.
-- SQL Server can use the index to directly navigate
-- to the row where Id = 10.
-- Therefore, the execution plan can use an Index Seek.

Select *
from Employees
where Id=10


-- ============================================
-- Filter by Name
-- ============================================
-- Name does NOT have a separate index.
-- SQL Server cannot directly navigate to the rows
-- based on the Name column.
-- Therefore, SQL Server needs to scan the existing
-- Clustered Index to find Name = 'Ahmed'.
-- This appear as a Clustered Index Scan.

Select *
from Employees
where Name='Khaled'



-- ============================================
-- Create Another Clustered Index
-- ============================================
-- A table can have only ONE Clustered Index.
-- The Employees table already has a Clustered Index
-- created for the Primary Key (Id).
-- Therefore, SQL Server cannot create another
-- Clustered Index on the Name column.
-- The statement will fail.


GO

Create Clustered Index IX_Employees_Name
on Employees (Name)


-- ============================================
-- Remove the Existing Clustered Index
-- ============================================
-- The existing Clustered Index belongs to the
-- Primary Key constraint.
-- We must remove the Primary Key constraint first
-- before creating another Clustered Index.
Alter table Employees
Drop Constraint[PK__Employee__3214EC072FCED98E]



-- ============================================
-- Create Clustered Index on Name
-- ============================================
-- The previous Clustered Index has been removed.
-- The table no longer has a Clustered Index.
-- Now we can create a Clustered Index on Name.
-- The operation succeeds because a table can have
-- only one Clustered Index, and currently there is none.
Create Clustered Index IX_Employees_Name
on Employees (Name)



drop Index if exists IX_Employees_Name
on Employees
GO


-- ============================================
-- Filter by Name
-- ============================================
-- Name now has a Clustered Index.
-- SQL Server can use this index to directly navigate
-- to the rows where Name = 'Ahmed'.
-- Therefore, the execution plan can use an Index Seek.

Select *
from Employees
where Name='Khaled'



-- ============================================
-- Filter by Salary
-- ============================================
-- Salary does NOT have an index.
-- The only index available is the Clustered Index on Name.
-- Since the query filters by Salary, SQL Server
-- cannot directly seek using the Name index.
-- Therefore, it may need to scan the Clustered Index
-- to find Salary = 5000.
-- This can appear as a Clustered Index Scan.

Select *
from Employees
where Salary=5000


--=========================================================
-- 2. NON-CLUSTERED INDEX
--========================================================= 

-- Re-Create Table Employees
-- Table Employee Has Clustered index on Id ONLY 
Create table Employees
(
Id int primary key,
Name varchar(50),
Salary decimal(18,2),
age int
)

-- Filter With Name 
-- Index Scan 

Select*
from Employees
where Name='Hamada'


-- Add Non Clustered index on Name 

Create nonclustered Index X_Employees_Name
On Employees(Name)


-- Filter With Name And Select Id and Name
-- Index Seek 
Select Id,Name
from Employees
where Name ='Khaled'


-- Filter With Name And Select Id , Name And Salary 
Select Id,Name,Salary
from Employees
where Name ='Khaled'



drop Index if exists X_Employees_Name
on Employees

-- Add Non Clustered index on Name Include Salary 
Create nonclustered Index X_Employees_Name
On Employees(Name)
include (Salary)


-- Filter With Name And Select Id , Name And Salary 
--index seek
Select Id,Name,Salary
from Employees
where Name ='Khaled'


-- Filter With Salary And Select Id , Name And Salary 
Select Id,Name,Salary
from Employees
where Salary=5000


--=========================================================
-- 3. UNIQUE INDEX
--=========================================================
-- Example : Unique Employees Names
-----------------------------------------------------------
-- Create a unique index to prevent duplicate
-- Employees names.

GO

Create Unique Index UX_Employees_Name
on Employees(Name)

-- Success
Insert into Employees(Id,Name,Salary)
values(301,'Khaled Ahmed',3000)


-- Fail
Insert into Employees(Id,Name,Salary)
values(302,'Khaled Ahmed',3000)

Hotel Reservation Management System 
 
A luxury hotel chain wants to design a database system to handle its 
reservations, guests, rooms, and payments efficiently The chain operates 
several hotels:  
●​ Each identified by a unique hotel ID, name, star rating, address, city, and contact 
number. 
●​ Each hotel has a manager responsible for operations, and every manager is also 
recorded in the system as a staff member. 
Each hotel contains multiple rooms: 
●​ Every room has a room number unique within that hotel, along with details such as 
room type (single, double, suite), capacity, daily rate, and availability status. 
●​ Some rooms may offer additional amenities like sea view, balcony, or kitchen, which 
should also be stored. 
 
Guests are the central focus of the system: 
●​ Each guest has a unique guest ID, full name, date of birth, contact details, nationality, 
and ID/passport number. 
●​ A guest can make multiple reservations, and some reservations can include more 
than one guest (such as families or business groups). 
A reservation is made for one or more rooms in a specific hotel: 
●​ It includes details such as reservation ID, check-in date, check-out date, booking date, 
number of adults and children, total price, and reservation status (e.g., confirmed, 
checked-in, canceled, completed). 
●​ Because guests may share a reservation, the relationship between guests and 
reservations must support multiple guests per booking. 
Each reservation can have one or more payments associated with it: 
●​ Payments record payment ID, date, amount, method (credit card, cash, online), and 
confirmation number. 
●​ Sometimes, a single reservation may be paid in multiple installments, while one 
payment may cover multiple reservations if handled by travel agencies. 
 
1
[P02] The hotel also employs several staff members: 
●​ Each identified by a staff ID. For each staff member, the system should record full 
name, position (e.g., receptionist, cleaner, manager), salary, and the hotel they work 
at. 
●​ Staff can be assigned to assist with multiple reservations — for example, a 
receptionist handles check-in/check-out, and a room service staff member may serve 
multiple guests. 
 
Additionally, guests may request services during their stay, such as laundry, 
spa, or transportation 
●​ Each service request should record a service ID, service name, request date, charge, 
and staff member who provided it 
●​ Since one reservation can have many service requests, and staff members can fulfill 
requests for many reservations, this relationship must be carefully modeled. 
 
 
 
2

ASP.Net Course
 
​
​
​
​
​
​
            
 
 
Online Retail Store Management System 
An online retail company wants to build a database system to manage its 
products, customers, orders, and deliveries.The store sells thousands of 
products across different categories, and each product must be properly 
tracked from listing to delivery: 
●​ Each product has a unique product ID, name, description, unit price, stock quantity, 
and date added. Every product belongs to a category, such as Electronics, Clothing, or 
Home Appliances. 
●​ Each category has a unique category ID, name, and description. 
●​ Some products may belong to subcategories, which are also stored in the same table, 
allowing a category to have multiple subcategories (e.g., “Laptops” under 
“Electronics”). 
The system records information about suppliers who provide the products: 
●​ Each supplier has a supplier ID, name, contact number, email, address, and country. 
●​ A supplier can supply multiple products, and a product may come from more than 
one supplier — so their relationship must support multiple associations. 
 
Customers are the core users of the store: 
●​ Each customer has a customer ID, full name, email, phone number, shipping address, 
and registration date. 
●​ A customer can place multiple orders, and each order contains one or more 
products. 
●​ An order is identified by an order ID and includes details such as order date, total 
amount, status (e.g., pending, shipped, delivered, canceled), and payment method. 
●​ Each order belongs to one customer but can contain many order items — each 
representing a product, its quantity, and the unit price at the time of purchase. 
After an order is placed, the system generates a shipment record to track 
delivery : 
●​ A shipment has a shipment ID, shipment date, delivery date, carrier name, tracking 
number, and current status.  
●​ Each order can have one or more shipments (for example, when items are sent in 
separate packages). 
 
1
[P02] The store also maintains payment information. : 
●​ Each payment has a payment ID, payment date, amount, method (credit card, wallet, 
bank transfer), and status. 
●​ Payments are linked to orders, and sometimes a single payment may cover multiple 
orders, such as when a customer preloads store credit. 
 
To manage inventory, the system keeps stock transactions that record 
whenever a product’s quantity changes due to new stock arrivals or customer 
purchases: 
●​ Each transaction includes a transaction ID, product ID, transaction date, quantity 
change, type (in or out), and reference (such as supplier or order ID). 
Finally, the store offers reviews where customers can rate and comment on 
products they purchased. 
●​ Each review includes a review ID, rating, comment, date, and references both the 
product and the customer who wrote it. 
 
2

Route Main
Session 01
[S01] Session 0 | 1 | - ERD
[S02] Session Agenda | 01 | Database Design | 02 | ERD | 03 | ERD Components | 04 | Entity | 05 | Attributes | 06 | Keys | 07 | Relationships | 08 | Relationship Cardinality | 09 | Relationship Participation | 10 | Weak Entity (Deep Dive)
[S03] Database Design
[S04] Purpose A well-designed database helps to: Reduce data redundancy Improve data consistency Ensure data integrity Support efficient storage and retrieval Make the system scalable and maintainable Meet business and user requirements
O Definition Database design is the process of creating a blueprint (structure) for a database that describes: What data to store How the data is organized How the data relates to each other What rules and constraints apply How to ensure data integrity, security, and efficiency
[S05] O Key Activities Database design involves: Analyzing requirements Identifying entities and relationships Defining attributes and keys Applying rules and constraints Normalizing data Designing the schema (structure) Entities Attributes Relationships
O Types of Database Design Database design is typically done in two main levels: • Conceptual Design High-level design using ERD to model the business requirements. STUDENT • Logical Design ENROLLS COURSE Convert the conceptual model into a logical schema (tables, keys, relationships). STUDENT PK StudentlD Name Email ENROLLMENT PK,FKI StudentlD PK,FK2 CourselD Grade COURSE PK CourselD CourseName
[S06] Database Design Process
[S07] Design Principles Data Integrity No Redundancy Simplicity Flexibility Efficiency Security • Ensure accuracy and consistency of data. • Avoid storing the same data multiple times. Keep the design as simple as possible. Allow changes to meet future requirements. Optimize performance for storage and retrieval. Protect data from unauthorized access and loss.
[S08] Why Good Database Design Matters ?
[S09] ERD
[S10] Key Components Entity A real-world object or concept Attribute A property or characteristic of an entity Relationship Association between entities
Why ERD? Helps in designing a better database Improves communication between team members Acts as a blueprint for database development Helps in identifying redundant or missing data Ensures data integrity and consistency
o What is ERD? An Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD) is a blueprint or a visual model that shows: The entities in a system The attributes of each entity The relationships between entities In Short ERD helps us understand what data we need to store and how the data is related.
[S11] Example ERD CustomerlD CustomerName CUSTOMER Email Phone Address OrderlD ProductlD Quantity UnitPrice PLACES ORDER ORDER_ITEM FOR ORDER CONTAINS PRODUCT OrderlD OrderDate TotalAmount ProductlD ProductName UnitPrice Stock
[S12] ERD Components
[S13] Attribute An attribute describes the properties or characteristics of an entity. Representation Ellipse Example CustomerName Email OrderDate
Entity An entity is a real-world object or concept that has an independent existence. Representation Rectangle Example CUSTOMER Customer, Product, Order, Employee, etc.
[S14] Keys Keys are used to uniquely identify records in an entity and define relationships. Note: Representation PK Primary Key Foreign Key Example PK: CustomerlD OrderlD (in Order table) PK = Primary Key FK = Foreign Key
Relationship A relationship defines how entities are associated with each other. Representation Diamond Example PLACES ORDER Places Order, Contains, Works For, etc.
[S15] Summary Table Component Entity Attribute Relationship Key Shape PK/ FK Purpose Represents a real-world object or concept Describes the properties of an entity Shows how entities are related Uniquely identifies records and links entities Example Customer, Product, Order CustomerName, Email, OrderDate Places Order, Contains CustomerlD (PK), OrderlD (FK)
[S16] Entity
[S17] How Entities are Represented in ERD Entities are represented using rectangles and named using singular nouns. ENTITY_NAME (Rectangle)
What is an Entity? An entity is a real-world object or concept that has independent existence and is distinguishable from other objects. Examples: Customer Product Order Employee
[S18] Types of Entities
[S19] Attributes
[S20] O How Attributes are Represented in ERD Attributes are represented using ovals and connected to their entity with a line. Attribute 1 Attribute 3 Attribute 2 ENTITY Attribute 4
O What is an Attribute? An attribute is a piece of data that describes an entity. It provides details about the entity and helps to store information. Examples CustomerName Email OrderDate Phone
[S21] Types Of Attributes
[S22] O Complex Attribute An attribute that is composed of both composite and multi-valued parts. Example PreviousAddresses (multiple addresses with details) Street CUSTOMER Address City ZipCode
O Derived Attribute An attribute whose value can be calculated from other attributes. Example Age (from DateOfBirth) EMPLOYEE Age (Derived)
[S23] Keys
[S24] How Keys are Shown in ERD Key attributes are underlined. Composite keys have multiple underlined attributes. Single Attribute Key EmployeelD Composite Key OrderlD ProductlD
O What is a Key? A key is an attribute or a set of attributes that uniquely identifies each instance of an entity. Examples: ID Number Email ABC - 1234 License Plate
[S25] Types Of Keys
[S26] O Super Key A set of one or more attributes that uniquely identifies an entity. It may contain extra attributes. Example: {EmployeelD}, (Email), (EmployeelD, Email}, {EmployeelD, Phone) EMPLOYEE EmployeelD Super Keys
O Foreign Key An attribute (or set of attributes) in one entity that refers to the primary (or candidate) key of another entity. Example: ORDER_lTEM.OrderlD references ORDER.OrderlD ORDER OrderiD ORDER_TEM OrderlD ProductlD Foreign Key
O Composite Key A key that consists of two or more attributes. Example: {OrderlD, ProductID} ORDER_ITEM OrdedD ProducdD Composite Key
[S27] Relationships
[S28] How Relationships are Shown in ERD Relationships are represented using diamonds and connected to the participating entities with lines. ENTITY A RELATIONSHIP ENTITY B
O What is a Relationship? A relationship is an association between two or more entities. It represents how entities are related to each other in the real world. Example: STUDENT IN COURSE A student enrolls in a course.
[S29] Types Of Relationships
[S30] N-ary Relationship (for more than 3 entities) A relationship among more than three entities. Example: COURSE STUDENT PARTICIPATES IN INSTRUCTOR
Ternary Relationship (N-ary for 3 entities) A relationship among three entities simultaneously. Example: SUPPLIER SUPPLIES ProductNarne Project(O SupplierfO ProÉctNune
[S31] Relationship Cardinality
[S32] How Cardinality is Shown in ERD Cardinality is shown near the ends of the relationship lines using 1, N, and M notation. 1 ENTIW A Notation 1 RELATIONSHIP ENTITY B Meaning Exactly one Many Many (No upper limit)
O What is Cardinality? Cardinality specifies how many instances of one entity can be related to how many instances of another entity. It helps define the constraints of a relationship in the real world. Example: ENROLLS STUDENT IN COURSE A student can enroll in many courses. A course can have many students.
[S33] 1 CUSTOMER PLACES 1 PRODUCT INCLUDES ORDER 1 CONTAINS ORDER_ITEM
[S34] Types Of Cardinality
[S35] Ternary (M-ary for 3 entities) A relationship among three entities simultaneously. Example: PRODUCT SUPPLIER SUPPLIER SUPPLIES PRODUCT PROJECT PROJECT
Recursive (1 :N) An entity is related to another instance of the same entity. Example: EMPLOYEE 1 MANAGES Parent -+ Child 1 Child Parent
[S36] Relationship Participation
[S37] O How Participation is Showm in ERD Participation is indicated by the style of the line connecting an entity to a relationship. Notation Meaning Total Participation Every instance of the entity must participate in the relationship. Partial Participation An instance of the entity may or may not participate in the relationship.
O What is Participation? Participation specifies whether an entity must participate in a relationship or whether it is optional. It shows the dependency of an entity on a relationship. Example: ENROLLS STUDENT IN COURSE Does every student enroll in a course? Does every course have at least one student?
[S38] ProductlD ProductName PRODUCT UnitPrice Stod( INCLUDES Quantity ORDER_ITEM UnitPrice A PRODUCT may or may not appear in any ORDER_ITEM (Partial Participation). Every ORDER_ITEM must be for some PRODUCT (Total Participation).
Example in ERD CustomedD CustomerName Email Phone CUSTOMER PLACES ORDER OrderlD OrderDate TotalAmount Every CUSTOMER must place at least one ORDER (Total Participation). An ORDER belongs to one CUSTOMER (Partial Participation).
[S39] Types Of Participation
[S40] Partial Participation (Optional Participation) An instance of the entity may or may not participate in the relationship. It is shown by a single line between the entity and the relationship. Example: SuppfiedD SupplierName SUPPLIER SUPPLIES PRODUCT ProductiD ProductName UnitPrice A SUPPLIER may supply zero or more PRODUCTS. (Partial Participation of SUPPLIER in SUPPLIES)
[S41] Weak Entity ( | Deep Dive | )
[S42] O What is a Weak Entity? A weak entity cannot be uniquely identified by its own attributes. It depends on a strong (owner) entity for identification through an identifying relationship. It has a partial key (discriminator) that, combined with the owner's key, forms a full key. Example: EMPLOYEE DEPENDENT EPENDENT A DEPENDENT cannot exist without an EMPLOYEE.
How Weak Entities are Shown in ERD Weak entity is shown with a double rectangle. Example: EMPLOYEE DEPENDEBIT A DEPENDENT cannot exist without an EMPLOYEE. .NET Track
[@01:15|t=75] O What is a Weak Entity? A weak entity cannot be uniquely identified by its own attributes. It depends on a strong (owner) entity for identification through an identifying relationship. It has a partial key (discriminator) that, combined with the owner's key, forms ROUTE How Weak Entities are Shown in ERD • Weak entity is shown with a double rectangle. • Identifying relationship is shown with a double diamond. • Total participation of the weak entity in the identifying relationship (double line). Weak entity has a partial key (discriminator) shown with a dashed underline. Notation a full key. Example: EMPLOYEE DEPENDEBIT Meaning Weak Entity Identifying Relationship Total Participation Partial Key (Discriminator) A DEPENDENT cannot exist without an EMPLOYEE. .NET Track
[@01:40|t=100] Example in ERD EmpName EMPLOYEE Department HireDato ROUTE DepName BirthDate DEPENDENT Gender Relationship The DEPENDENT entity is weak because it cannot be uniquely identified by DepName alone. It is identified by the combination of EmplD (from EMPLOYEE) and DepName. .NET Track

[S03] Relational Database
[S04] O What is a Relational Database? A relational database stores data in tables (relations) made up of rows (records) and columns (attributes). It is based on the relational model proposed by E. F. Codd. Data is linked between tables using relationships. Example Table: STUDENT StudentlD 101 102 103 Name Ali Omar Sara DepartmentlD 10 20 10 (Attribute) Row (Record)
[S05] Relational Model Structure In the relational model, data is organized into tables, and relationships are established between them using keys.
DEPARTMENT DepartmentID (PK) DepartmentName 10 20 30 Computer Science Information Systems Business 1 N StudentlD (PIO 101 102 103 104 STUDENT StudentName Ali Omar Sara Mona DepartmentlD (FK) 10 20 10 30
PK (Primary Key): A column (or set of columns) that uniquely identifies each row in a table. FK (Foreign Key): A column that references the primary key of another table. Relationship: Links data between tables using keys.
[S06] Key Characteristics Data in Tables Data is stored in tables (relations) made up of rows and columns. Unique Identification Each table has a primary key that uniquely identifies its rows. Relationships Tables are related to each other using foreign keys. Data Integrity Constraints and rules ensure accuracy and consistency of data. Set-Based Operations Data can be retrieved and manipulated using SOL, a set-based language.
[S07] O Key Terms Relation (Table) Tuple (Row) Attribute (Column) Domain Primary Key Foreign Key Relationship Degree of Relation Cardinality A collection of related data organized in rows and columns. A single record in a table. A field that contains a specific type of data. The set of valid values for an attribute. A column (or set of columns) that uniquely identifies each row. A column that references the primary key of another table. An association between two tables. The number of attributes (columns) in a relation. The number of rows (records) in a relation.
[S08] O Benefits of Relational Databases
Data Integrity and Accuracy
Powerful Querying and Reporting
Reduced Redundancy
Better Scalability
O Standardization (SOL)
Multiple User Access
[S09] Mapping Rules - Simple Entity
[S10] A simple entity is an entity that: • Does not have any weak entities. • Exists independently. Mapping Rule Create a relation (table) for the entity. Include all its attributes as columns.
Example EmpName Email EmplD EMPLOYEE Phone HireDate

An attribute that can be divided into smaller sub-attributes.

An attribute whose value can be derived from other attribute(s).

[S16] O Multivalued Attribute
An attribute that can have multiple values for one entity.
ERD Example Name StudentlD STUDENT PhoneNo
Mapping Rule • • Create a separate table for the multivalued attribute. Include the primary key of the main entity. The multivalued attribute becomes a column in this new table.

An attribute that combines composite and multivalued characteristics.
Mapping Rule Create a separate table for the complex attribute. Include the primary key of the main entity as a foreign key in the new table. [S19] Key Design Decisions
[S20] Choose Primary Keys
• Select an attribute (or combination of attributes) that uniquely identifies each row. Use surrogate keys (e.g., ID) when natural keys are complex or likely to change. Keep primary keys short, stable, and not null.
Example Name STUDENT BinhDotq Email

[S21] Choose Foreign Keys
Create foreign keys to enforce relationships between tables. Reference the primary key (or candidate key) of the parent table. Use meaningful names for foreign keys.
Example DEPARTMENT DoptlD (PK) 10 20 30 DeptNamo HR Financo EmplD (PK) 1 2 3 EMPLOYEE EmpNamo Ali Omar Sara Dopt]D (FIO 10 20 10
EMPLOYEE.DeptID is a foreign key referencing DEPARTMENT.DeptlD.
[S22] Name Tables and Columns Consistently
• Use meaningful, descriptive names. Use singular nouns for table names. Use consistent naming conventions (e.g., PascalCase or snake_case). Avoid reserved words and abbreviations.
Example e Good Names Employee Department Course EnrollDate TotalAmount e e O Avoid Emp DeptTbl Crs AmtTot Consistent naming improves readability and maintainability.
[S23] Plan for Scalability and Performance
• Identify frequently queried columns and add indexes. • Avoid unnecessary indexes. • Consider partitioning for very large tables. • Design with future growth in mind.
Index Example Table EMPLOYEE ORDER ORDER Column(s) DeptlD OrderDate CustomerlD, OrderDate Index Type Nonclustered Index Nonclustered Index Composite Index Purpose Speed up searches by department Speed up date range queries Speed up customer order history

-- DDL
-------
-- 1) Create Database

Create Database CityLibrary

Use CityLibrary
--------------------------------
-- 2) Create Tables :-
-----------------------
Create Table Librarian(
	Id int Primary Key, -- Not Null , Unique
	FullName Varchar(50) Not Null, -- Requried
	Salary Decimal(8,2),
	PhoneNumber Varchar(MAX),
	HireDate Date
)

Create Table Branches
(
	Id int Primary Key Identity,
	BranchName Varchar(50) Not Null,
	Address Varchar(100),
	PhoneNumber Varchar(MAX),
	OpeningHours int,
	ManagerId int UNIQUE References Librarian(Id) -- Foreign Key
)

Create Table Members
(
	MembershipId int Primary Key,
	FullName Varchar(50) NOT NULL,
	DateOfBirth DATE,
	Email Varchar(MAX),
	PhoneNumber Varchar(MAX),
	MembershipDate Date
)

Create Table Books
(
	ISBN Varchar(20) Primary Key,
	PubYear int,
	Title Varchar(MAX),
	Edition Varchar(MAX),
	BookCategory Varchar(MaX)
)

Create Table Authors
(
	Id int Primary Key,
	FullName Varchar(max) NOT NULL,
	Nationality Varchar(max),
	DateOfBirth Date
)


Create Table BookAuthors
(
	BookISBN Varchar(20),
	AuthorId int,
	Primary Key (BookISBN , AuthorId),
	CONSTRAINT FK_BA_Book Foreign Key (BookISBN) References Books(ISBN),
	CONSTRAINT FK_BA_Authors Foreign Key (AuthorId) References Authors(Id),
)

Create Table BookCopies
(
	CopyId int Primary Key,
	Condition Varchar(100),
	Status Varchar(50),
	BranchId int References Branches(Id),
	BookISBN Varchar(20) References Books(ISBN)
)

-- Missing Columns [Return Date , Due Date]
Create Table BorrowTransactions
(
	TransactionId int Primary Key Identity,
	BorrowDate Date,
	BookCopyId int References BookCopies(CopyId),
	MemberId int References Members(MembershipId)
)

-- Missing Constraint FK
Create Table Fines
(
	Id int Primary Key,
	Amount Decimal(10,2),
	IssueDate Date,
	PaymentStatus Varchar(20),
	BorrowTransId int Unique
)

-- Alter

-- Alter To Add Columns
Alter Table BorrowTransactions
Add ReturnDate int

Alter Table BorrowTransactions
Add DueDate int
--=====================================================
-- Alter To Add Constraint

Alter Table Fines
Add Constraint FK_F_BorrowTransaction
Foreign Key (BorrowTransId) References BorrowTransactions(TransactionId)
--=====================================================

-- Add Default Value 'Available' To Column Status in Table BookCopies
Alter Table BookCopies
Add Constraint DEF_Status
Default ('Available') FOR Status

-- Check Constraint

Alter Table BookCopies
Add Constraint CH_Status
Check (Status IN ('Available' , 'Borrowed' , 'Damaged' , 'Booked'))
------------------------------------------------------------------------

Alter Table Fines
Add Constraint UQ_Ay7aga
Unique (Amount)

Alter Table Fines
DROP Constraint UQ_Ay7aga

Alter Table Books
Add TempColumn int

Alter Table Books
Drop Column TempColumn

Create Table Test
(
id int primary key
)

Drop Table Test

--==================================
-- Scheams :-

-- dbo -> Database Owner => Default Schema
GO
Create Schema Managment
GO

Alter Schema Managment Transfer Branches
Alter Schema Managment Transfer Librarian

-- To Create Table in Speific Schema
Create Table Managment.LibManagment

[S35] 3. Examples e Create a table CREATE TABLE Employees ( Employee1D INT PRIMARY KEY, FirstName NVARCHAR(50) , Salary Alter a table ALTER TABLE Employees ADD Email NVARCHAR(IOØ) ; e Drop a table DROP TABLE Employees; Truncate a table TRUNCATE TABLE Employees; Rename a table ' Employees', 'Staff' ; EXEC sp_rename
[S36] 4. Key Points DDL changes the structure, not the data. Some DDL commands (e.g., DROP) cannot be rolled back. Always be careful when using DROP and TRUNCATE. DDL is usually auto-committed by the database.
[S37] Schema
[S38] 1. Definition A schema is a named collection of database objects such as tables, views, indexes, procedures, functions, and more. Examples of Objects in a Schema Tables o Indexes Views Others Procedures foo Functions
2. Schema vs Database Feature Level Purpose Can have multiple? Default Scope Database Top-level container Stores schemas and other settings A server can have multiple databases One system database (e.g., master) Isolates data between applications Schema Sub-container inside a database Organizes database objects A database can have multiple schemas Usually one default schema (e.g., dbo in SQL Server) Organizes objects within the same database
[S39] 3. Example In SQL Server, the default schema is dbo. You can create your own schemas to organize objects. Create a new schema CREATE SCHEMA Sales; Create a table in the Sales schema CREATE TABLE Sales. Customers ( Customer ID INT PRIMARY KEY, CustomerName NVARCHAR(IOØ) Query the table using schema name SELECT * FROM Sales. Customers;
[S40] 4. Why Use Schemas? Better organization of database objects. Avoids name conflicts between objects. Improves security by assigning permissions at the schema level. Helps in managing large applications with many objects.
5. Visual Example Database CompanyDB Schema: dbo (default) Tables Vtews Schema: Sales Tables Views Schema: HR Tables Vtews Procedures Procedures Procedures fix) Functions fix) Functions fix) Functions
[S41] Default Schema & Ownership
1. What is a Default Schema? The default schema is the schema that is used when a user creates an object without specifying a schema name. User Schema: dbo (default) Table View Procedure If no schema is specified, objects are created in the user's default schema.
2. How It Works Every user has a default schema. When you create an object without specifying a schema, it goes to your default schema. By default, the default schema for a new user is dbo. You can change a user's default schema to another schema if needed.
[S42] 3. Examples Example 1: Create a table without specifying schema CREATE TABLE Customers ( customer-ID INT PRIMARY KEY, CustomerName NVARCHAR(IØØ) If your default schema is dbo , the table is created as: dbo.Customers Example 2: Create a table in a specific schema CREATE TABLE Sales.orders ( OrderlD INT PRIMARY KEY The table is created in Sales schema.
[S43] 4. What is Ownership? The owner is the user who creates an object. The owner has full control over the object. Schema: dbo User Table (Ahmed) View Owner: Ahmed Procedure The owner can modify, delete, and manage permissions for the objects.
5. Check Default Schema & Ownership Check your default schema: SELECT Check the schema owner: SELECT SCHEMA_NAME(schema_id) AS SchemaName, USER_NAME(principa1_id) AS SchemaOwner FROM sys. schemas; Check object owner: SELECT AS SchemaName, OBJECT_NAME(object_id) AS ObjectName, AS Owner-Name FROM sys . objects;
[S44] Managing Schemas
1 Create a Schema Creates a new schema in the database. CREATE SCHEMA Sales; New schema Sales created.
2 View Schemas List all schemas in the database. SELECT name FROM sys. schemas ORDER BY name; name dbo Sales Finance
3 Modify a Schema Change the owner of a schema. ALTER AUTHORIZATION ON SCHEMA: . • Sales TO SomeUser; Owner: OldUser Owner: SomelJser You can change ownership but cannot rename a schema directly.
[S45] 4 Delete a Schema Removes a schema and all objects inside it. DROP SCHEMA Sales; 1 Make sure the schema is empty or use CASCADE to remove all objects inside. To remove with all objects: DROP SCHEMA Sates CASCADE;
5 Check Schema Owner Find the owner of a schema. SELECT AS SchemaName , AS OwnerName FROM sys.schemas HERE name = ' Sales' ; SchemaName Sales OwnerName SomeUser
[S46] 7 Transfer Objects to Another Schema Move objects from one schema to another. ALTER SCHEMA Sales TRANSFER dbo.Customers; ALTER SCHEMA Sales TRANSFER dbo.Orders; Schema: dbo Customers Orders Schema: Sales Customers Orders
6 Set Default Schema for a User Set the default schema for a user. ALTER USER SomeUser WITH DEFAULT_SCHEMA = Sales; Default Schema: Sales SomeUser
[S47] Thank You | See You Next Session

[@00:45|t=45] Data Types ROUTE A data type defines what kind of value can be stored in a database column and how that value is stored and handled. Categories of Data Types SOL Server data types are grouped into the following categories: Choosing the Right Data Type 123 abc .NET Track Exact Numeric Store whole numbers without decimal points. String (Character) Store text and character data. Boolean Store true/false values. Other / Special Include uniqueidentifier, xrnl, 3.14 ooo 1010 0101 Approximate Numeric Store numbers with decimal points (floating point). Date and Time Store date, time, or date and time values. Store binary data such as images, files, Or unique values. Guideline Store only what you need Consider performance. Ensure data integrity. Save Storage space. Think about future. table, cursor, sql_variant. etc. Recommendation Choose the smallest data type that fits your data. Smaller data types use less memory. improve performance. Use correct data type to avoid invalid data. Avoid using larger types than necessary. If data may grow. choose a type that can handle it. Talking: Route Academy

-- =====================================================
-- DML OPERATIONS - CITY LIBRARY DATABASE
-- =====================================================
Use LibrarySystemG03
-- =====================================================
-- 1. INSERT OPERATIONS
-- =====================================================
-- Single Row Insert
--==================================================
-- Insert New record Into table Members 

Insert Into Library.Members
Values ('Hossam Mostafa' , '2000-01-01' , 'hossam@gmail.com' , '123' , '2026-09-20')

-- Insert New Record Into Table Books

Insert Into Library.Books
Values ('123-4' , '2020' , 'Sql Server' , '3rd Edition' , 'Programming')


-- Multiple Rows Insert
--==================================================

-- Insert Some Authors into Table Authors
Insert Into Library.Authors
Values ('Ahmed Ali' , 'Egyptian' , '1950-01-01'),
	   ('Mai Gamal' , 'Syrian' , NULL),
	   ('Mohamed Kamal' , 'Lebanon' , NULL),
	   ('Esraa Sami' , 'Egyptian' , NULL)

-- Assign Book To Authors

Insert Into Library.BookAuthors
Values ('123-4' , 1)


-- Using Column List
--==================================================
-- Insert New record Into table Members 

Insert Into Library.Members(FullName)
Values ('Gamal Ahmed'),
       ('Ola Sayed'),
	   ('Ali Adel')

Insert Into Library.Members(Phone , FullName)
Values ('1234' , 'Aya Ali')
`

-- =====================================================
-- 2. UPDATE OPERATIONS
-- =====================================================
-- Simple Update - Single Record
-- Update Member Email
Update Library.Members
Set Email = 'gamal@gmail.com'
Where MembershipId = 2


-- Update with Multiple Columns
-- Update PhoneNumber and Opening Hours For CairoBranch

Insert Into Managment.Branches
Values ('CairoBranch' , 'Cairo-Egypt' , '1500' , 8 , 1)

Update Managment.Branches
Set PhoneNumber = '1515' , OpeningHours = 12
--Where Id = 1
Where Name = 'CairoBranch'

-- Update with Calculation

-- Increase the salary of all Librarians whose salary is less than 10,000 by 10%

Update Managment.Librarians
Set Salary += Salary * 0.1
Where Salary < 10000


-- Conditional Update with CASE

-- Update BorrowTransactions status based on ReturnDate
-- Late , Ontime
Update Library.Transactions
Set Status = CASE
	When ReturnDate > DueDate Then 'Late'
	When ReturnDate < DueDate Then 'Ontime'
	Else 'Ontime'
END

-- =====================================================
-- 3. DELETE OPERATIONS
-- =====================================================

-- Simple Delete - Single Record

-- Delete Author With Id 3
Delete From Library.Authors
Where Id = 3


-- Delete with Condition
-- Delete BorrowTransactions With Status Late
Delete From Library.Transactions
Where Status = 'Late'

-- Delete All Records

Delete From Library.Members

-- =============================================
-- Foreign key RELATIONSHIP RULES
-- =============================================

-- =============================================
-- RULE 1: cascade DELETE
-- When parent is deleted, automatically delete all child records
-- =============================================

-- Delete No Action [Default]
Delete From Library.Authors
Where Id = 1


-- Cascade => Delete Parent => Child Delete
Delete From Library.Books
Where ISBN = '123-5'

Alter Table Library.BookCopies
Drop Constraint [FK__BookCopie__BookI__5812160E]

Alter Table Library.BookCopies
Add Constraint FK_BC_Books
Foreign Key (BookISBN) References Library.Books(ISBN)
ON Delete Cascade

-- cascade Update - BookCopies Follows Book
Alter Table Library.BookCopies
Drop Constraint FK_BC_Books

Alter Table Library.BookCopies
Add Constraint FK_BC_Books
Foreign Key (BookISBN) References Library.Books(ISBN)
ON Update Cascade
ON Delete Cascade

Update Library.Books
SET ISBN = '456-1'
Where ISBN = '987-1'
-- =============================================
-- RULE 2: set NULL
-- When parent is deleted/updated, set foreign keyto NULL in child
-- Requires the foreign keycolumn to be NULLABLE
-- =============================================
Alter Table Library.BookCopies
Drop Constraint FK_BC_Books

Alter Table Library.BookCopies
Add Constraint FK_BC_Books
Foreign Key (BookISBN) References Library.Books(ISBN)
ON Update SET NULL
ON Delete SET NULL

Update Library.Books
Set ISBN = '1-2-3'
Where ISBN = '456-1'

Delete From Library.Books
Where ISBN = '1-2-3'
 
-- =============================================
-- RULE 3: set default
-- When parent is deleted/updated, set foreign keyto its default value
-- Requires a default constraint on the foreign keycolumn
-- =============================================
Alter Table Library.BookCopies
Drop Constraint FK_BC_Books

Alter Table Library.BookCopies
Add Constraint FK_BC_BooksISBN
Foreign Key (BookISBN) References Library.Books(ISBN)
ON Update SET DEFAULT
ON Delete SET DEFAULT

Alter Table Library.BookCopies
Add Constraint DEF_VLU Default ('0000') FOR BookISBN

Delete From Library.Books
Where ISBN = '12-345'


Update Library.Books
Set ISBN = '12-345'
Where ISBN = '12-34'


 
-- =============================================
-- RULE 4: no action (default behavior)
-- Prevent deletion/update if child records exist
-- =============================================
-- =============================================
-- Data Query Language - SELECT
-- ============================================
Use Hospital

-- BASIC SELECT - All Columns
-- ============================================

-- Select all columns from Patients table

Select *
From Patients

-- ============================================
-- SELECT Specific Columns
-- ============================================

-- Select nurse name and address
Select Name , Address
From Nurses

-- ============================================
-- WHERE Clause - Single Condition
-- ============================================

-- Find patients in a specific ward
Select * 
From Patients
Where WardId = 1

-- Find patients born after a specific date
-- 2010-01-01

Select Name , DOB
From Patients
Where DOB > '2010-01-01'


-- ============================================
-- WHERE Clause - Multiple Conditions
-- ============================================

-- Find patients in a specific ward born after a specific date

Select Name , DOB , WardId
From Patients
Where WardId = 3 AND DOB > '2000-01-01'

-- Find patients born within a specific date range

Select Name , DOB
From Patients
--Where DOB >= '2000-01-01' ANd DOB <= '2005-01-01'
Where DOB BETWEEN '2000-01-01' AND '2005-01-01'

-- Find nurses serving in more than ward

Select Name , ServesInWardId
From Nurses
Where ServesInWardId IN (1 , 3)

-- Find nurses who are not serving in specific wards

Select Name , ServesInWardId
From Nurses
Where ServesInWardId is null

-- Find nurses who are not supervising any ward

Select Name , SupervisedWardId
From Nurses
Where SupervisedWardId is null


-- Find nurses who are supervising a ward

Select Name , SupervisedWardId
From Nurses
Where SupervisedWardId is not null

-- Find nurses serving in ward 1 or 2 and supervising a ward

Select Name , SupervisedWardId , ServesInWardId
From Nurses
Where ServesInWardId IN (1,2) and SupervisedWardId IS NOT NULL

-- ============================================
-- DISTINCT -> Remove Duplication
-- ============================================
-- Find distinct patient names

Select DISTINCT Name From Patients

-- ============================================
-- ORDER BY
-- ============================================

-- Find patients sorted by name in ascending order

Select Name
From Patients
Order By Name -- By Default Sorting in Ascending Order [A - Z]

-- Find patients sorted by date of birth in descending order

Select Name , DOB
From Patients
Order By DOB DESC -- Sorting in Descending Order


-- Find nurses serving in wards sorted by ward

Select Number , Name , ServesInWardId
From Nurses
Where ServesInWardId IS NOT NULL
Order By ServesInWardId

-- ============================================
-- STRING FUNCTIONS
-- ============================================

-- LEN: Returns the length of a string
-- Return Patient Name And Their Length

Select Name , LEN(Name)
From Patients


-- SUBSTRING: Extracts part of a string
-- Return First 3 Characters In Patient Name
-- Ahmed -> 

Select Name , SUBSTRING(Name , 1 , 3)
From Patients

-- ==============================================
-- Built-In Functions
-- ==============================================
-- ============================================
-- DATE & TIME FUNCTIONS
-- ============================================

-- GETDATE: Returns current date/time
-- Return Patient Name, Date Of Birth And Current Date

Select Name , DOB , GETDATE() AS CurrentDate
From Patients


-- DATEDIFF: Difference between two dates
-- Return Patient Name And Their Age In Years

Select Name , DATEDIFF(YEAR , DOB , GETDATE()) as Age
From Patients

-- ============================================
-- CONVERSION FUNCTIONS
-- ============================================

-- CAST: Converts a value to another data type
-- Convert Patient ID To String

Select Name , CAST(Id AS VARCHAR(20)) PatientAsString
From Patients


-- CONVERT: Converts a value and supports formatting
-- Convert Patient Date Of Birth To MM/DD/YYYY

Select Name , CONVERT(VARCHAR , DOB , 101) AS FormattedDate
From Patients

-- ============================================
-- AGGREGATE FUNCTIONS
-- ============================================

-- SUM: Total of numeric values
-- Return Total Salaries for Consultants

Select SUM(Salary) TotalSalaries
From Consultants

-- COUNT: Number of rows/items
-- Return Total Patients

Select COUNT(*)
From Patients

-- COUNT: Count non-null values
-- Return Total Patients With A Ward



-- AVG: Average value
-- Return Average Salary

Select AVG(Salary) AvergaeSalaries
From Consultants

-- MIN: Smallest value, MAX: Largest value
-- Return Minimum And Maximum Salary

Select MIN(Salary) AS MinSalary , MAX(Salary) MaxSalary
From Consultants


-- COUNT_BIG: Count for very large datasets

Select COUNT_BIG(*)
From Patients


-- ============================================
-- NULL FUNCTIONS
-- ============================================

-- COALESCE: Returns first non-null value
-- Return Supervised Ward, Serving Ward Or Default Text

Select Name , COALESCE(SupervisedWardId , ServesInWardId , 0)
From Nurses

-- ISNULL: Replaces NULL with a value
-- Return Supervised Ward Or Zero

Select Name , ISNULL(SupervisedWardId , 0)
From Nurses

-- ============================================
-- TOP - Limit number of rows returned
-- ============================================

-- Get top 3 consultants by salary

Select TOP 3 Name , Salary
From Consultants
Order By Salary DESC

-- Select Half Data Of Consultants Table

Select TOP(50) PERCENT Id , Name , Salary
From Consultants
Order By Id

-- ============================================
-- TOP WITH TIES - Include rows with same value as last row
-- ============================================

-- Get top 3 consultants by salary, including ties
-- If multiple consultants have the same salary as the 3rd consultant, include them all

Select TOP 3 WITH TIES Name , Salary
From Consultants
Order By Salary DESC
