[S03] Data Manipulation Language
[S04] 2. Common DML Commands Command INSERT UPDATE DELETE MERGE Purpose Adds new rows into a table Modifies existing data in a table Deletes rows from a table Performs insert, update, or delete in a single statement
1. What is DML? DML statements are used to manipulate data stored in tables. They do not change the structure of the database.
[S05] Delete data DELETE FROM Employees WHERE Employee1D = 1
Update data UPDATE Employees SET Salary = 65000 WHERE Employee1D = 1
Insert data INSERT INTO Employees VALUES ('Ahmed' , 'Ali' (FirstName, LastName , Salary)
3. Examples
[S06] What happened? O O O O ld = 1 Updated (salary changed from 5000 to 5500) Not in source, so no change Exists with same data, so no change Inserted (new employee)
Target Table After MERGE ld 2 3 4 Name Ahmed Sara Ali Mona Department Finance Salary 5500 6000 7000 6500
MERGE INTO Employees AS target USING Employees _ Staging AS source ON target . ld = source. ld WHEN MATCHED AND (target. Salary source. Salary) THEN target. Salary = source. Salary UPDATE SET WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET THEN INSERT (ld, Name, Department, Salary) (source. ld, source. Name, source . Department, VALUES source . Salary) ;
Source Table: Employees_Staging Name Ahmed Ali Mona ld 3 4 Department Finance Salary 5500 7000 6500
Target Table: Employees ld Name Ahmed 1 2 Sara Ali 3 Department Finance Salary 5000 6000 7000
Simple Example for MERGE
[S07] 4. DML vs DDL (Quick Comparison) Feature Purpose Affects Examples Commit DML Manipulates data Data in tables INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE Transaction-based (can be rolled back) DDL Defines structure Database objects (tables, views, etc.) CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE Auto-commit (in most cases)
[S08] 0 Insert a new Manager into the Managers table, providing only FullName and Email. Create a new table called ArchivedCustomers, then insert all customers born before 1990 using INSERT ...SELECT. Delete all transactions where the Amount greater than 50,000.
SQL Practice Tasks
[S09] Referential Integrity Rules
[S10] 2 Update Rule You cannot update the primary key value in the parent table if it is referenced by records in the child table. Departments (Parent) Employees (Child) Name Departmentld ld 2 3 Name IT Finance ld 2 3 Ahmed Sara Ali 1 2 3 Departmentld (Foreign Key)
Insert Rule You cannot insert a record in the child table with a foreign key value that does not exist in the parent table. Departments (Parent) Employees (Child) Name Departmentld ld 2 3 Name Finance ld I 2 3 Ahmed Sara Ali 2 3 Departmentld (Foreign Key)
[S11] 4 No Orphan Records Every foreign key value in the child table must match an existing primary key value in the parent table. This prevents orphan records (child records without a valid parent). Employees (Child) Name Departmentld ld 1 2 3 Ahmed Sara Ali 1 2 99 Not allowed Departmentld = 99 does not exist in the Departments table.
3 Delete Rule You cannot delete a record from the parent table if it is referenced by records in the child table (unless a delete action like CASCADE or SET NULL is defined). Departments (Parent) Employees (Child) Name Departmentld ld 2 3 Name Finance ld I 2 3 Ahmed Sara Ali 1 2 3 Departmentld (Foreign Key)
[S12] 5 Defined Actions (Optional) You can define what happens to child records when a parent record is updated or deleted: Action NO ACTION (default) CASCADE SET NULL SET DEFAULT On Delete Restrict Delete Set FK to NULL Set to default value On Update Restrict Update Set FK to NULL Set to default value Description Prevent the operation if child records exist. Automatically delete or update child records. Set the foreign key in child records to NULL. Set the foreign key to its default value.
[S13] Data Query Language
[S14] 2. Basic SELECT Syntax SELECT columnl, column2, FROM table name [WHERE condition] [ORDER BY column ASC DESC] ;
3. Simple Examples o All columns from a table SELECT * FROM Employees; Specific columns SELECT FirstName, FROM Employees; e With a condition LastName , Salary SELECT * FROM Employees WHERE DepartmentID = 10
1. What is DQL? DQL (Data Query Language) is used to query and retrieve data from one or more tables.
[S15] 6. Key Points DQL does not change data. Safe to use (read-only). Returns data in a result set. Supports filtering, sorting, and grouping.
5. Result Set DOL returns the data in a result set (virtual table). Example: EmployeelD FirstName 1 2 3 4 Ahmed Sara Omar Mona LastName Ali Hassan Khaled Ibrahim Salary 60000 55000 48000 52000

[S17] 2 Types of Functions SQL Server provides several types of functions: O Built-in (System) Functions Provided by SQL Server (e.g., string, date, math). Scalar-valued Functions Return a single value. O Table-valued Functions Return a table (inline or multi-statement). O User-defined Functions Created by users for specific needs.
1 What is a Function? A function is a reusable block of code that accepts input (parameters), performs a specific task, and returns a single value (or a table in the case of table-valued functions). dbo. FunctionName ( parameters ) ; SELECT

-- ============================================
-- JOINs 
-- ============================================

-- ============================================
-- INNER JOIN - Two Tables
-- ============================================
-- Display every patient together with the ward Name they belong to.

-- Microsoft Syntax
Select P.Name , W.Name 
From Patients P INNER JOIN Wards W
ON P.WardId = W.Id
Where P.WardId IS not Null --(Conditions)

-- ANSI Syntax
Select P.Name , W.Name 
From Patients P , Wards W
Where P.WardId = W.Id AND P.WardId IS NOT NULL


-- Display every drug administration together with
-- the details of the drug that was administered.

Select DA.PatientId , DA.NurseId , D.Code AS DrugCode , DA.DATE , DA.Time
From DrugAdministrations DA INNER JOIN Drugs D
ON DA.DrugCode = D.Code



-- ============================================
-- LEFT OUTER JOIN
-- ============================================
-- Display every patient and the ward they belong to,
-- including patients who are not assigned to any ward.

-- Patients

Select P.Name , W.Name
From Patients P LEFT JOIN Wards W
ON P.WardId = W.Id


-- Display every ward and the patients assigned to it,
-- including wards that currently have no patients.

Select P.Name , W.Name
From Wards W Left Join Patients P
ON W.Id = P.WardId

-- ============================================
-- RIGHT OUTER JOIN
-- ============================================
-- Display every ward and the patients assigned to it,
-- including wards that currently have no patients.

Select P.Name , W.Name
From Patients P Right Join Wards W
ON W.Id = P.WardId

-- ============================================
-- FULL OUTER JOIN
-- ============================================
-- Display all patients and all wards,
-- including patients without a ward and wards without patients.

Select P.Name , W.Name
From Patients P FULL Join Wards W
ON W.Id = P.WardId


-- Display all consultants and nurses,
-- including consultants without nurses and nurses without consultants.

Select C.Name AS Doctor , N.Name AS NurseName
From Consultants C Full Join Nurses N
ON C.Id = N.Number

-- Display all consultants and their patient assignments,
-- including consultants without assignments and assignments without consultants.

Select C.Name AS Doctor , PCA.ConsultantId , PCA.PatientId
From Consultants C FULL Join PatientConsultantAssignments PCA
ON PCA.ConsultantId = C.Id



-- ============================================
-- SELF JOIN
-- ============================================

-- Display each nurse together with their manager,
-- returning only nurses who have a manager. [Inner Join]

Select N.Name AS NurseName , NM.Name NurseManager
From Nurses N Join Nurses NM
ON N.ManagerId = NM.Number


-- Display every nurse together with their manager,
-- including nurses who do not have a manager.

Select N.Name AS NurseName , NM.Name NurseManager
From Nurses N Left Join Nurses NM
ON N.ManagerId = NM.Number

-- ============================================
-- CROSS JOIN
-- ============================================

-- Generate every possible combination of patients and consultants.

Select P.Name PatientName , C.Name DoctorName
From Patients P Cross Join Consultants C

-- Generate every possible combination of wards and consultants.

Select W.Name WardName , C.Name DoctorName
From Wards W Cross Join Consultants C
-- ============================================
-- MULTIPLE JOINS - Three or More Tables
-- ============================================

-- Display each patient together with their ward
-- and the consultant who examined them.

Select P.Name PatientName , W.Name WardName , PE.ConsultantId , C.Name
From Patients P 
INNER JOIN Wards W
ON W.Id = P.WardId
INNER Join PatientExaminations PE
ON P.Id = PE.PatientId
INNER Join Consultants C
ON PE.ConsultantId = C.Id


Select P.Name PatientName , W.Name WardName , PE.ConsultantId , C.Name
From Patients P , Wards W , Consultants C , PatientExaminations PE
Where W.Id = P.WardId AND P.Id = PE.PatientId AND PE.ConsultantId = C.Id

-- Display each patient together with the drugs
-- that were administered to them.

-- Patients , Drugs DrugAdminst

Select P.Name , D.Dosage , DA.DATE , DA.Time
From Patients P INNER Join DrugAdministrations DA
ON DA.PatientId = P.Id
INNER Join Drugs D
ON DA.DrugCode = D.Code

-- Display each patient together with the nurse who administered
-- the drug and the details of the administered drug.
-- PAtient , Nurse , Drugs , DrugAdmin

Select P.Name , N.Name NurseName , D.Dosage , DA.DATE , DA.Time
From Patients P INNER Join DrugAdministrations DA
ON DA.PatientId = P.Id
INNER JOIN Nurses N 
ON DA.NurseId = N.Number
INNER Join Drugs D
ON DA.DrugCode = D.Code



-- Display each patient's ward, the nurse who administered the drug,
-- and the details of the administered drug.

Select P.Name , W.Name WardName ,N.Name NurseName , D.Dosage , DA.DATE , DA.Time
From Patients P 
Inner Join Wards W
ON P.WardId = W.Id
Inner Join DrugAdministrations DA
ON DA.PatientId = P.Id
Inner Join Nurses N
ON DA.NurseId = N.Number
Inner Join Drugs D
ON DA.DrugCode = D.Code

Select P.Name , W.Name WardName ,N.Name NurseName , D.Dosage , DA.DATE , DA.Time
From Patients P , Nurses N , Wards W , DrugAdministrations DA , Drugs D
Where P.WardId = W.Id 
	  AND DA.PatientId = P.Id
	  AND DA.NurseId = N.Number
	  AND DA.DrugCode = D.Code

-- ============================================
-- RANKING FUNCTIONS
-- ============================================

-- ============================================
-- ROW_NUMBER()
-- ============================================

-- Assign a unique sequential number to every consultant
-- based on their salary, starting with the highest salary.

Select Name , Salary , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (Order By Salary DESC) RowNumber
From Consultants


-- Assign a unique sequential number to every consultant
-- based on their salary, starting with the lowest salary.

Select Name , Salary , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (Order By Salary) RowNumber
From Consultants

-- Assign a unique sequential number to every consultant
-- based on salary, with the consultant's name used
-- to determine the order when salaries are equal.

Select Name , Salary , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (Order By Salary DESC , Name ASC) RowNumber
From Consultants

-- ============================================
-- DENSE_RANK()
-- ============================================

-- Assign a dense rank to consultants based on salary,
-- giving consultants with the same salary the same rank.

Select Name , Salary , DENSE_RANK() OVER (Order By Salary DESC) DenseRank
From Consultants


-- Rank consultants from the highest salary to the lowest salary
-- without leaving gaps between ranking numbers.

Select Name , Salary , DENSE_RANK() OVER (Order By Salary DESC) DenseRank
From Consultants

-- Display the salary rank of each consultant
-- and sort the result by salary rank.

Select Name , Salary , DENSE_RANK() OVER (Order By Salary DESC) DenseRank
From Consultants
Order By DenseRank

-- ============================================
-- RANK()
-- ============================================

-- Rank consultants based on their salary,
-- giving consultants with the same salary the same rank.

Select Name , Salary , RANK() OVER (Order By Salary DESC) Rank
From Consultants

-- Rank consultants based on their salary


Select Name , Salary , RANK() OVER (Order By Salary DESC) as SalaryRank
From Consultants
Order By Salary DESC
-- Rank consultants from the lowest salary to the highest salary.

Select Name , Salary , RANK() OVER (Order By Salary) as SalaryRank
From Consultants


-- ============================================
-- RANK() vs DENSE_RANK()
-- ============================================

-- Compare RANK() and DENSE_RANK() for consultant salaries
-- to see how they handle consultants with equal salaries.

Select Name , Salary , ROW_NUMBER () Over (Order By Salary DESC) RowNum , 
					   DENSE_RANK() Over (Order By Salary DESC) DenRank ,
					   RANK() Over (Order By Salary DESC) Rank
From Consultants 


-- ============================================
-- NTILE()
-- ============================================
-- Divide consultants into 2 salary groups,
-- with the highest-paid consultants placed in the first group.

Select Name , Salary , NTILE(2) Over (Order By Salary DESC) SalaryGroup
From Consultants


-- Divide consultants into 3 approximately equal groups
-- based on their salary.

Select Name , Salary , NTILE(3) Over (Order By Salary DESC) SalaryGroup
From Consultants

-- Divide consultants into 4 approximately equal salary groups
-- and display the highest-paid group first.


Select Name , Salary , NTILE(4) Over (Order By Salary DESC) SalaryGroup
From Consultants
Order By SalaryGroup , Salary DESC


-- ============================================
-- PARTITION BY
-- ============================================
-- Rank nurses by salary separately within each ward.
-- The ranking starts again from 1 for every ward.

Select N.Number , N.Name , W.Name WardName , N.Salary , RANK() Over (Partition By N.ServesInWardId Order By Salary DESC) Rank
From Nurses N INNER JOIN Wards W
ON N.ServesInWardId = W.Id


-- Assign a unique row number to nurses based on salary
-- within each ward.


Select N.Number , N.Name , W.Name WardName , N.Salary , ROW_NUMBER() Over (Partition By N.ServesInWardId Order By Salary DESC) Rank
From Nurses N INNER JOIN Wards W
ON N.ServesInWardId = W.Id




-- Rank nurses by salary within each ward using DENSE_RANK(),
-- so equal salaries receive the same rank without gaps.

Select N.Number , N.Name , W.Name WardName , N.Salary , DENSE_RANK() Over (Partition By N.ServesInWardId Order By Salary DESC) Rank
From Nurses N INNER JOIN Wards W
ON N.ServesInWardId = W.Id

-- ============================================
-- PARTITION BY + NTILE()
-- ============================================
-- Divide the nurses in each ward into 2 salary groups 
-- The grouping starts again for every ward.

Select N.Name , W.Name WardName , N.Salary ,
       NTILE(2) OVER (Partition By N.ServesInWardId Order By Salary DESC)
From Nurses N , Wards W
Where N.ServesInWardId = W.Id


-- Divide the nurses in each ward into 3 approximately equal salary groups.

Select N.Name , W.Name WardName , N.Salary ,
       NTILE(3) OVER (Partition By N.ServesInWardId Order By Salary DESC)
From Nurses N , Wards W
Where N.ServesInWardId = W.Id

[@00:45|t=45] I What are Ranking Functions? Ranking functions assign a rank, row number, or bucket number to each row in a result set based on a specified order. They are window functions, used with the OVER() clause. They do not collapse, group, or aggregate rows (unlike GROUP BY). They are useful for ordered analysis, such as finding top records, handling ties, and pagination scenarios. .NET Track 2 Example Data Employees Employeeld 2 3 4 5 6 EmployeeName Ali Sara Omar Mona Hany Laila Department ROUTE Salary 12000 15000 15000 10000 12000 12000

[@03:00|t=180] 1 What is DENSE_RANK() assigns a rank to each row within a result set based on the specified ORDER BY clause. Key points: • Rows with the same value get the same rank. The next rank is the next consecutive integer (no gaps). The ranking starts from I. The order of rows is determined by the ORDER BY clause. If the order is not unique, the order of rows with the same rank is nondeterministic (can vary between executions). .NET Track 2 Sample Data Employees Employeeld 1 2 3 4 5 6 EmployeeName Ali Sara Omar Mona Hany Laila Department IT IT IT ROUTE Salary 12000 15000 15000 10000 12000 12000

Key points: n is the number of buckets. The bucket numbers start from I. The rows are distributed as evenly as possible. If the number of rows is not perfectly divisible by n, the first buckets get one extra row. The order of rows is determined by the ORDER BY clause inside OVERO. .NET Track ROUTE

Session 06
Question 1 — Count Patients per Ward
Display the number of patients assigned to each ward.
Question 2 — Calculate the Average Consultant Salary
Display the average salary of all consultants.
Question 3 — Display Salary Statistics for Consultants
Display the minimum, maximum, average, and total consultant salaries.
Question 4 — Count Patients by Ward
Display the ward ID and number of patients in each ward, sorted from highest to lowest.
Question 5 — Medication Quantity per Patient
Display the total medication quantity administered to each patient.
Question 6 — Medication Administrations per Patient
Display each patient ID together with the number of medication administrations they received.
Question 7 — Patients per Ward with Ward Names
Display every ward together with the number of patients assigned to it, including wards with no patients.
Question 8 — Average Nurse Salary per Ward
Display each ward together with the average salary of nurses serving in that ward.
Question 9 — Wards with More Than 3 Patients
Display wards that have more than 3 patients.
Question 10 — Patients with More Than 5 Medication Administrations
Display patients who received medication more than 5 times.
Question 11 — Consultants Above Average Salary
Display consultants whose salary is greater than the average consultant salary.
Question 12 — Nurses Above Average Salary
Display nurses whose salary is greater than the average nurse salary.
Question 13 — Patients in the Largest Ward
Display patients who belong to the ward containing the largest number of patients.
Question 14 — Consultants with the Maximum Salary
Display the consultant or consultants who have the highest salary.
Question 15 — Patients Who Received Medication
Display patients who have at least one medication administration.
Question 16 — Patients Who Never Received Medication
Display patients who have never received any medication.
Question 17 — Count Medication Administrations per Patient
Display every patient together with the number of medication administrations they received.
Question 18 — Total Medication Quantity per Patient
Display every patient together with the total medication quantity administered to them.
Question 19 — Derived Table for Consultant Salaries
Create a derived table containing the average consultant salary, then display consultants whose salary is above that average.
Question 20 — Patients with Above-Average Medication Quantity
Display patients whose total medication quantity is greater than the average total medication quantity across patients who received medication.
Question 21 — Create a Patient Backup
Create a new table containing all patients.
Question 22 — Create a Basic Patient Information Table
Create a new table containing only patient ID, name, and date of birth.
Question 23 — Create a Consultant Salary Report
Create a new table containing consultant ID, name, and salary.
Question 24 — Create a Patient-Ward Report
Create a new table containing each patient together with the ward they belong to.
Question 25 — Create a Patient-Consultant Report
Create a new table containing patients and their assigned consultants.
Question 26 — Create a High-Salary Consultant Table
Create a new table containing consultants whose salary is greater than 50000.
Question 27 — Create a Young Patients Table
Create a new table containing patients born after January 1, 2000.
Question 28 — Create a High-Salary Nurse Report
Create a new table containing nurses earning more than 30000 together with the ward they serve in.
Question 29 — Create a Ward Patient Summary
Create a new table containing each ward and its patient count.
Question 30 — Create a Patient Medication Summary
Create a new table containing each patient and their total medication quantity.
Question 31 — Calculate Patient Age
Create a scalar function that receives a date of birth and returns the patient's age.
Question 32 — Calculate Annual Salary
Create a scalar function that receives a monthly salary and returns the annual salary.
Question 33 — Calculate Medication Cost
Create a scalar function that receives quantity and unit price and returns the total medication cost.
Question 34 — Get Patients by Ward
Create an inline table-valued function that receives a ward ID and returns all patients in that ward.
Question 35 — Get Consultants by Minimum Salary
Create an inline table-valued function that receives a minimum salary and returns consultants whose salary is greater than or equal to it.
Question 36 — Get Patients with Their Ward
Create an inline table-valued function that receives a ward ID and returns patients together with their ward name.
Question 37 — Get Patients Above a Specific Age
Create a multi-statement table-valued function that receives a minimum age and returns patients who are at least that age.
Question 38 — Get Patient Medication Summary
Create a multi-statement table-valued function that receives a patient ID and returns the total medication quantity and number of medication administrations.
Question 39 — Classify Consultant Salaries
Create a multi-statement table-valued function that receives a minimum salary and returns consultants with a salary classification.
Question 40 — Patient Medication Statistics
Display each patient together with their number of medication administrations, total medication quantity, and average medication quantity.
Question 41 — Above-Average Wards
Display wards whose patient count is greater than the average patient count across all wards.
Question 42 — Create a High-Activity Patient Report
Create a new table containing patients who received medication more than 5 times.
Question 43 — Create a Consultant Salary Report Using a Scalar Function
Create a new table containing each consultant's name, monthly salary, and annual salary.
Question 44 — Use an Inline TVF with a Filter
Using GetConsultantsByMinimumSalary, display consultants whose salary is at least 50000 and whose name starts with A.
Question 45 — Use a Multi-Statement TVF
Using GetPatientsWithAge, display patients who are at least 30 years old and order them from oldest to youngest.
Question 46 — Final Hospital Patient Summary
Display patient ID, patient name, ward name, patient age, number of medication administrations, and total medication quantity. Use the existing tables and CalculatePatientAge.

[@01:30|t=90] User-Defined Function O What is a User-Defined Function? A UDF is a reusable block of T-SQL code that returns a value or a table. You can define input parameters and perform calculations or queries. Helps in modularizing code and improving maintainability. can be used in SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, ORDER BY, etc. Functions can return a single value (scalar) or a table (table- valued). .NET Track Types of User-Defined Functions Scalar Function Returns a single value (e.g., number, string, date). Can be used wherever an expression is allowed. Inline Table-Valued Function Returns a table (single SELECT statement). Generally better performance. Multi-Statement Table-Valued Function Returns a table (multiple statements with table variable). More flexible but may have lower performance. ROUTE Talking: Route Academy

Question 1 — Display All Patients

Question 3 — Display Patients with Their Wards 
Create a stored procedure that displays every patient together with the ward they belong to. 
 
Question 4 — Get Patient by ID 
Create a stored procedure that receives a patient ID and returns that patient. 
Question 5 — Get Consultants by Minimum Salary 
Create a stored procedure that receives a minimum salary and returns consultants whose 
salary is greater than or equal to it. 
Question 6 — Get Patients by Ward 
Create a stored procedure that receives a ward ID and returns all patients assigned to that 
ward. 
 
Question 7 — Return Patient Count 
Create a stored procedure that returns the total number of patients through an OUTPUT 
parameter. 
Question 8 — Return Average Consultant Salary 
Create a stored procedure that returns the average consultant salary through an OUTPUT 
parameter. 
1
[P02] Question 9 — Return Patient Medication Quantity 
Create a stored procedure that receives a patient ID and returns the total medication 
quantity through an OUTPUT parameter. 
 
Question 10 — Increase a Salary 
Create a stored procedure that receives a salary as an input-output parameter and 
increases it by a supplied percentage. 
Question 11 — Increase Medication Quantity 
Create a stored procedure that receives a quantity as input-output and adds an additional 
quantity to it. 
Question 12 — Convert Monthly Salary to Annual Salary 
Create a stored procedure that receives a monthly salary as input-output and replaces it 
with the annual salary. 
 
Question 13 — Insert Patient with Error Handling 
Create a stored procedure that inserts a patient and handles errors using TRY-CATCH. 
Question 14 — Update Consultant with Error Handling 
Create a stored procedure that updates a consultant's salary and handles errors. 
Question 15 — Delete Patient with Error Handling 
Create a stored procedure that deletes a patient and handles errors using TRY-CATCH. 
 
Question 16 — Add a New Patient 
Create a stored procedure that inserts a new patient. 
Question 17 — Add a New Consultant 
Create a stored procedure that inserts a new consultant. 
Question 18 — Record a Medication Administration 
Create a stored procedure that inserts a new medication administration.

[P03] Question 19 — Update Patient Information 
Create a stored procedure that updates a patient's name, date of birth, and ward. 
Question 20 — Update Consultant Salary 
Create a stored procedure that changes a consultant's salary. 
Question 21 — Increase Nurse Salary 
Create a stored procedure that increases a nurse's salary by a percentage. 
Question 22 — Delete a Patient

Question 23 — Delete a Consultant

Question 24 — Delete a Medication Administration

Question 25 — Store All Patients Returned by a

Create a table and use INSERT INTO ... EXEC to store the result of GetAllPatients. 
Question 26 — Store High-Salary Consultants 
Create a table and use INSERT INTO ... EXEC to store consultants earning at least 50000. 
Question 27 — Store Patients from a Specific Ward 
Create a table and use INSERT INTO ... EXEC to store patients returned from

Question 28 — Create a Patient Audit Table 
Create a table that can store patient insert, update, and delete operations.

[P04] Question 29 — Create an AFTER INSERT Trigger 
Create an AFTER INSERT trigger that records every newly inserted patient in PatientAudit. 
 
Question 30 — Audit Consultant Salary Changes 
Create an audit table and an AFTER UPDATE trigger that stores the old and new 
consultant salary. 
Question 31 — Audit Patient Ward Changes 
Create a trigger that records the old and new ward whenever a patient's ward changes. 
 
Question 32 — Archive Deleted Patients 
Create a table for deleted patients and an AFTER DELETE trigger that stores deleted 
patient information. 
Question 33 — Audit Deleted Consultants 
Create an AFTER DELETE trigger that stores deleted consultant information. 
 
Question 34 — Compare Old and New Consultant Salary 
Create an AFTER UPDATE trigger that displays the old and new salary of the consultant. 
Question 35 — Compare Old and New Patient Ward 
Create an AFTER UPDATE trigger that displays the patient's old ward and new ward. 
Question 36 — Handle Multiple Inserted Rows 
Create an AFTER INSERT trigger that records every patient inserted by a single statement. 
Then insert three patients in one statement. 
 
Question 37 — Prevent Patients Without a Ward 
Create an INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger that prevents inserting a patient when WardId is 
NULL.

[P05] Question 38 — Validate Patient Date of Birth 
Create an INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger that prevents patients whose date of birth is in the 
future. 
 
Question 39 — Prevent Consultant Salary Reduction 
Create an INSTEAD OF UPDATE trigger that prevents reducing a consultant's salary. 
Question 40 — Control Patient Updates 
Create an INSTEAD OF UPDATE trigger that allows patient information to be updated 
without changing the patient ID. 
 
Question 41 — Prevent Patient Deletion 
Create an INSTEAD OF DELETE trigger that prevents patients from being deleted directly. 
Question 42 — Archive Before Delete 
Create an INSTEAD OF DELETE trigger that first stores the deleted patient in 
DeletedPatients, then deletes the patient from Patients. 
 
Question 43 — Add Patient with Audit Trigger 
Create a stored procedure that adds a patient and an AFTER INSERT trigger that records 
the new patient in PatientAudit. Then execute the procedure. 
Question 44 — Update Consultant with Salary Audit 
Create a stored procedure to update a consultant salary and an AFTER UPDATE trigger to 
record the old and new salary. 
Question 45 — Delete Patient and Archive the Record 
Create a stored procedure that deletes a patient and a trigger that automatically archives 
the deleted patient. 
Question 46 — Stored Procedure with TRY-CATCH and 
Transaction 
Create a stored procedure that updates a patient's ward and inserts a medication 
administration for the same patient. Use TRY-CATCH and a transaction, rolling back

Question 47 — Patient Modification Audit System 
Build a complete audit system for Patients. Record INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE 
operations with patient ID, operation type, and operation date. 
Question 48 — Stored Procedure Returning Multiple 
Statistics 
Create a stored procedure that returns total patients, total consultants, average consultant 
salary, and total medication quantity. 
Question 49 — Stored Procedure with OUTPUT and 
TRY-CATCH 
Create a stored procedure that receives a patient ID and returns total medication quantity 
through an OUTPUT parameter. Handle errors using TRY-CATCH. 
Question 50 — Final Hospital Patient Summary 
Create a stored procedure that receives a patient ID and returns patient information, ward 
name, number of medication administrations, and total medication quantity. Use 
TRY-CATCH.

	From Patients

   --------------------------------------------------------- */

-- Return patients together with their ward information.

Create Or Alter Function dbo.GetPatientWithWardInfo(@WardId int)
Returns Table
AS
Return
(
	Select P.Id PatientId , P.Name PatientName , W.Id WardId , W.Name WardName
	From Patients P Join Wards W
	ON P.WardId = W.Id
	Where W.Id = 1
)

-- Display patients together with their ward

Select * From dbo.GetPatientWithWardInfo(1)

/* =========================================================

/* ---------------------------------------------------------

   --------------------------------------------------------- */

-- Return the total medication quantity
-- administered to each patient.

Create Or Alter Function dbo.GetPatientMedicationSummary(@PatientId INT)
Returns @table Table
(
	PatientId INT ,
	TotalQuantity INT ,
	CountOfDA INT
)
AS
Begin
	INSERT INTO @table
	Select PatientId , SUM(Quantity) , COUNT(*)
	From DrugAdministrations
	Where PatientId = @PatientId
	Group By PatientId

	RETURN
End


-- Display the medication summary for patient number 1.

Select *
From dbo.GetPatientMedicationSummary(202)

--   Example 3: Get Consultant Salary Classification
-- Return consultants together with a salary classification.
Create Or Alter Function dbo.ConsultantSalaryGroups(@MinSalary Decimal(18,0))
Returns @Result Table
(
	ConsultantId Int,
	DoctorName nvarchar(100),
	Salary Decimal(18,0),
	SalaryCategory NVARCHAR(50)
)
As 
Begin
	INSERT INTO @Result
	Select Id , 
		   Name , 
		   Salary , 
		   CASE 
				When Salary > 20000 Then 'High Salary'
				When Salary < 20000 Then 'Low Salary'
				Else 'Medium Salary'
		   END
	From Consultants
	Where Salary >= @MinSalary
	Return
End



-- Display consultants earning at least 15000
-- together with their salary classification.

Select * From dbo.ConsultantSalaryGroups(15000)

--=========================================================
-- 2. INPUT PARAMETERS
--=========================================================
-- Example 1: 
-- Create a stored procedure that filters consultants by an
-- optional salary range (minimum and/or maximum).
-- A NULL parameter means "no limit".
-- Call it with: only a minimum, a range, and no parameters.

-- Parameters with "= NULL" are optional: the caller can skip them.
Create or Alter Procedure dbo.GetConsultantBySalary
						  @MinSalary Decimal(18,0) = NULL, -- Optional Parameters 
						  @MaxSalary Decimal(18,0) = NULL  -- Optional Parameters
AS
Begin
	Select Id , Name , Salary
	From Consultants
	Where (@MinSalary IS NULL OR Salary >= @MinSalary)
	AND   (@MaxSalary IS NULL OR Salary <= @MaxSalary)
	Order By Salary DESC
End

-- Only a minimum: consultants earning at least 20000.

Exec dbo.GetConsultantBySalary @MinSalary = 20000 

-- A range: consultants earning between 20000 and 23000.

Exec dbo.GetConsultantBySalary 20000 , 23000

-- No parameters: both filters are skipped, all consultants return.

Exec dbo.GetConsultantBySalary


--=========================================================
-- Example 2: 
-- Create a stored procedure that joins Patients with Wards,
-- then filters by patient name and/or ward name using LIKE.
-- Call it with: name starts with 'A', ward contains 'Care',
-- and both filters together.

-- 
-- '%' matches any text; '_' matches one character.
-- Defaults = '%' mean "match everything" if a parameter is skipped.

Create or Alter Procedure dbo.SearchForPatientAndWards 
						  @PatientName Nvarchar(100) = '%', -- A
						  @WardName nvarchar(100) = '%'
AS
Begin
	Select P.Id PatId , P.Name PatName , W.Name WardName
	From Patients P Join Wards W
	ON P.WardId = W.Id
	Where P.Name LIKE @PatientName AND W.Name LIKE @WardName
	Order By W.Name , P.Name
End

-- Patients whose name starts with 'A'.

Execute dbo.SearchForPatientAndWards @PatientName = 'A%'

-- Patients in wards whose name contains 'Care' (e.g. Intensive Care Unit).

Exec dbo.SearchForPatientAndWards @PatientName = 'A%' , @WardName = '%Care%'

--=========================================================
-- Create a stored procedure that receives a consultant ID(INPUT) and
-- returns his name, salary, and number of assigned patients
-- through OUTPUT parameters.

Create Or Alter Procedure dbo.GetDoctorInfo
						  @Id INT,
						  @ConsultantName NVARCHAR(100) OUTPUT,
						  @ConsultantSalary Decimal(18,0) OUTPUT,
						  @PatientCount INT OUTPUT
AS
Begin
	Select @ConsultantName = C.Name , 
		   @ConsultantSalary = C.Salary ,
		   @PatientCount = COUNT(PCA.PatientId)
	From Consultants C Left Join PatientConsultantAssignments PCA
	ON PCA.ConsultantId = C.Id
	Where C.Id = @Id
	Group By C.Name , C.Salary
End

						  @Salary Decimal(18,2) OUTPUT, -- 5000
						  @Percentage Decimal(10,2)
AS
Begin -- 11000    10000    +  10000    *     = 1000 =      11000
	SET @Salary = @Salary + (@Salary * @Percentage / 100)

-- 6. TRY-CATCH
--=========================================================
-- Create a stored procedure that validates the data, inserts a  patient while handling errors, and returns the new patient Id.
-- Patients.Id is not IDENTITY, so calculate the next Id manually.


-- Ward 99 does not exist -> THROW -> CATCH.
-- The INSERT is skipped and the error details are displayed.



--=========================================================
-- 7. INSERT Based On EXEC
--=========================================================
-- Example 1 : Save  Store Consultants Above a Salary

Exec dbo.GetConsultantBySalary @MinSalary = 20000


-- Create a table to store high-salary consultants.
Create Table ConsultantWithHigeshtSalaries
(
	Id int,
	Name NVARCHAR(100),
	Salary Decimal(18,0)
)


-- Execute the stored procedure and insert
INSERT INTO ConsultantWithHigeshtSalaries
Exec dbo.GetConsultantBySalary @MinSalary = 20000



-- Display the stored consultant results.
Select * From ConsultantWithHigeshtSalaries

--=========================================================
-- 1. AFTER INSERT
--=========================================================
-- Log every new patient.


--=========================================================
-- 2. AFTER UPDATE
--=========================================================
-- Log old and new salary.



   -- UPDATE(Column) -> TRUE if the column appears in the SET clause.
    -- If only the Name was updated, exit early.
  

--=========================================================
-- 3. AFTER DELETE
--=========================================================

-- Keep a copy of deleted patients.


--=========================================================
-- 4. INSTEAD OF INSERT
--=========================================================
-- Block inserts: the trigger runs instead of the INSERT.


--=========================================================
-- 5. INSTEAD OF UPDATE
--=========================================================
-- Reject salary cuts, otherwise do the update ourselves.


--=========================================================
-- 6. INSTEAD OF DELETE
--=========================================================
-- Block deletes.

[@00:00|t=0] Multi-Statement Table-Valued Function O Concept A Multi-Statement Table-Valued Function returns a table of rows and columns. It is created using the CREATE FUNCTION statement with RETURNS @table TABLE. It can contain multiple T-SQL statements (IF-ELSE, and INSERT / UPDATE on the table variable). It can accept input parameters. It allows complex logic compared to Inline TVE Used in the FROM clause like a table, and can be joined with other tables. In SELECT or WHERE only inside a subquery. Generally has lower performance than Inline TVF because results are stored in a table variable. .NET Track ROUTE

[@00:45|t=45] Stored Procedure ROUTE A Stored Procedure is a named set of T-SQL statements saved inside the database. You write it once and run it any time with EXEC. SYNTAX CREATE PROCEDURE dbo. @Param1 DataType, @Param2 DataType AS BEGIN ProcedureName = DefaultValue optional - T -SQL statements END; Parentheses around the parameters are optional, and PROC is a short form of PROCEDURE. .NET Track KEY POINTS Can accept input and output parameters. Can return result sets, output values and a return code. Can contain logic: variables, IF, TRY...CATCH, INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE. Run it with EXEC (or EXECUTE), as many times as you need. Compiled on its first execution. The execution plan is then cached and reused. Stored in the Plan Cache (Procedure Cache) — a part of SQL Server's memory (RAM), not on disk. It's cleared on server restart.

[@08:15|t=495] Why Use Stored Procedures? COMMON USE CASES Keep business logic in one place. Reuse the same code from many applications. Control access: give users permission to EXECUTE the procedure instead of direct access to the tables. Run INSERT 1 UPDATE 1 DELETE with validation. ROUTE it it ADVANTAGES Performance: the execution plan is cached and reused. Less network traffic: one EXEC instead of many statements. Security: permissions on the procedure, and parameters help prevent SQL injection. Easier maintenance: change the procedure, not every application. Error handling with TRY...CATCH. Execute Statements 5. Build Results ROUTE 6. Send Results to Client O Client sends EXEC The client (application, SSMS, sends an EXEC statement with the procedure name and the parameter values. EXEC dbo. GetEmpIoyeesByDepartment @DeptID = I .NET Track SQL Server Parses & Validates Checks the syntax of the EXEC Statement. e The procedure body was already syntax-checked at CREATE time. Checks that the procedure exists. Checks the parameters: names, data types, and that every required parameter is passed. Checks that the user has EXECUTE permission. If any check fails, an error is returned and nothing runs.

-- Stored Procedure :-
--=========================================================
-- 5. MODIFYING DATA
--=========================================================
-- 5.1 INSERT

Create or Alter Procedure dbo.AddPatient
		  @Id INT , @Name NVARCHAR(100) , @DOB Date , @WardId INT
AS
	INSERT INTO Patients (Id , Name , DOB , WardId)
	Values(@Id , @Name , @DOB , @WardId)


Execute dbo.AddPatient @Id = 401 , @Name = 'Hossam Mostafa' , 
					   @DOB = '2000-01-01' , @WardId = 2

-- 5.2 UPDATE

-- Create a stored procedure for a partial update: only the
-- parameters that are sent get changed. Report whether the
-- patient was found.
-- ISNULL(@Param, Column) -> if @Param is NULL, keep the current value.

Create or Alter Procedure dbo.UpdatePatient
					@PatientId INT , 
					@Name NVARCHAR(100) = NULL , 
					@DOB Date = NULL, 
					@WardId INT = NULL
AS
Begin
	Update Patients
	SET Name = ISNULL(@Name , Name),
		DOB = ISNULL(@DOB , DOB), 
		WardId = ISNULL(@WardId , WardId)
	Where Id = @PatientId

	IF @@ROWCOUNT = 0
		Print 'No Patient Found With This Id'
	ELSE
		Print 'Patient Updated Successfully'
End

Exec dbo.UpdatePatient @PatientId = 401 , @Name = 'Mohamed Mostafa'

-- 5.3 DELETE

Create or Alter Procedure dbo.RemovePatient @PatientId INT
AS
	Delete From Patients
	Where Id = @PatientId

Exec dbo.RemovePatient 401

-- TRIGGERS
--=========================================================
--=========================================================
-- 1. AFTER INSERT
--=========================================================
-- Log every new patient.

Create Table PatientDataAudit
(
	AuditId INT Identity(1,1) Primary Key,
	PatientId INT,
	ActionType NVARCHAR(50),
	ActionDate DateTime
)

Create or Alter Trigger TRG_PatientAfterInsert
ON Patients
After Insert
AS
	-- Body
	INSERT INTO PatientDataAudit
	Select Id , 'Insert' , GETDATE()
	From inserted


Insert Into Patients (Id , Name , DOB , WardId)
Values (402 , 'Hossam Mostafa' , '2000-01-01' , 1)
--=========================================================
-- 2. AFTER UPDATE
--=========================================================
-- Log old and new salary.

Create Table ConsultantsSalaryAudit
(
	AuditId INT Identity(1,1) Primary Key,
	ConsultantId INT,
	OldSalary DECIMAL(18,0),
	NewSalary DECIMAL(18,0),
	ActionDate DateTime
)

Create or Alter Trigger TRG_ConsultantAfterUpdate
ON Consultants
AFTER Update
AS
-- If Name ONly Updated , Exist Trigger
	IF NOT UPDATE(Salary)
		RETURN;
	INSERT INTO ConsultantsSalaryAudit(ConsultantId , OldSalary , NewSalary , ActionDate)
	Select D.Id , D.Salary , I.Salary , GETDATE()
	From deleted D Join inserted I
	ON D.Id = I.Id

Update Consultants 
SET Salary = 40000
Where Id = 301

Select * From ConsultantsSalaryAudit

-- 3. AFTER DELETE
--=========================================================
Create Table DeletedPatients
(
	PatientId INT,
	PatientName NVARCHAR(100),
	DOB Date,
	WardId INT,
	DeletedDate DATETIME
)
-- Keep a copy of deleted patients.
Create or Alter Trigger TRG_PatientAfterDelete
ON Patients
AFTER Delete
AS

	Select Id , Name , DOB , WardId , GETDATE()
	From deleted

Delete From Patients Where Id = 402

Create or Alter Trigger TRG_BlockInsertIntoPatient
ON Patients
INSTEAD OF INSERT

	Print 'You Cannot Insert To This Table !'


Insert Into Patients (Id , Name , DOB , WardId)

Drop Trigger TRG_BlockInsertIntoPatient

--=========================================================
-- 5. INSTEAD OF UPDATE
--=========================================================
-- Reject salary cuts, otherwise do the update ourselves.

Create or Alter Trigger TRG_ConsNoSalaryCut
ON Consultants
INSTEAD OF UPDATE
AS
Begin
	-- 2000 < 5000
	IF Exists(Select 1
			  From deleted D Join inserted I ON D.Id = I.Id
			  Where I.Salary < D.Salary)
	Begin
		RAISERROR('Salary Cannot Be Cutted !' , 16 , 1)
		RETURN;
	END

	Update C SET C.Salary = I.Salary
	From Consultants C JOIN inserted I
	ON C.Id = I.Id
End


Update Consultants SET Salary = 10000 Where Id = 301
Update Consultants SET Salary = 50000 Where Id = 301

Drop Trigger TRG_ConsNoSalaryCut

INSTEAD OF DELETE

	RAISERROR('Cannot Delete From This Table' , 16 , 1)

Delete From Patients Where Id = 201


--=========================================================
-- INDEXES
--=========================================================
-- Example 1: Filtering by Id
-- ============================================
-- The Id column has a Clustered Index.
-- Since the query filters using the indexed column (Id),
-- SQL Server can directly navigate through the index
-- to find the required row instead of scanning all rows.
-- This results in an Index Seek.

Select *
From Patients
Where Id = 280
-- ============================================
-- Example 2: Filtering by Name
-- ============================================
-- The Name column does NOT have an index.
-- Therefore, SQL Server cannot use an index to directly
-- locate the rows where Name = 'Ahmed'.
-- It needs to scan the available index/data to find matching rows.
-- The execution plan may show an Index Scan if a suitable
-- nonclustered/clustered index is being scanned.

Select * 
From Patients
Where Name = 'Ahmed'



-- ============================================
-- Example 3: Creating a Table Without Any Index
-- ============================================
-- This table has no Primary Key and no indexes.
-- Therefore, it is stored as a Heap.
-- A Heap is a table that does not have a Clustered Index.

Create Table PatientsHeap
(
	Id INT,
	Name VARCHAR(50)
)

-- ============================================
--  Filtering a Heap Table
-- ============================================
-- The PatientsHeap table has no indexes.
-- SQL Server has no index structure that it can use
-- to directly locate Id = 1.
-- Therefore, SQL Server must scan the entire table
-- row by row to find the matching record.
-- This appears in the execution plan as a Table Scan.

Select *
From PatientsHeap
Where Id = 1
--=========================================================
-- 1. CLUSTERED INDEX
--=========================================================
-- Create Employees Table
-- ============================================
-- A Primary Key is created on the Id column.
-- In SQL Server, a Primary Key is created as a
-- Clustered Index by default
-- The Id column will have a Clustered Index.

Create Table Employees
(
	Id Int Primary Key, -- Unique , Clustered Index
	Name Varchar(50),
	Salary DECIMAL(18,0),
	Age INT
)

-- ============================================
-- Filter by Id
-- ============================================
-- Id has a Clustered Index.
-- SQL Server can use the index to directly navigate
-- to the row where Id = 10.
-- Therefore, the execution plan can use an Index Seek.

Select * From Employees Where Id = 3

-- ============================================
-- Filter by Name
-- ============================================
-- Name does NOT have a separate index.
-- SQL Server cannot directly navigate to the rows
-- based on the Name column.
-- Therefore, SQL Server needs to scan the existing
-- Clustered Index to find Name = 'Ahmed'.
-- This appear as a Clustered Index Scan.


-- ============================================
-- Create Another Clustered Index
-- ============================================
-- A table can have only ONE Clustered Index.
-- The Employees table already has a Clustered Index
-- created for the Primary Key (Id).
-- Therefore, SQL Server cannot create another
-- Clustered Index on the Name column.
-- The statement will fail.

Create CLUSTERED INDEX IX_Employees_Name
ON Employees(Name)

-- ============================================
-- Remove the Existing Clustered Index
-- ============================================
-- The existing Clustered Index belongs to the
-- Primary Key constraint.
-- We must remove the Primary Key constraint first
-- before creating another Clustered Index.

Alter Table Employees
Drop Constraint [PK__Employee__3214EC07B6E65991]

-- ============================================
-- Create Clustered Index on Name
-- ============================================
-- The previous Clustered Index has been removed.
-- The table no longer has a Clustered Index.
-- Now we can create a Clustered Index on Name.
-- The operation succeeds because a table can have
-- only one Clustered Index, and currently there is none.
Create CLUSTERED INDEX IX_Employees_Name
ON Employees(Name)


-- ============================================
-- Filter by Name
-- ============================================
-- Name now has a Clustered Index.
-- SQL Server can use this index to directly navigate
-- to the rows where Name = 'Ahmed'.
-- Therefore, the execution plan can use an Index Seek.

Select * From Employees Where Name = 'Sara'

-- ============================================
-- Filter by Salary
-- ============================================
-- Salary does NOT have an index.
-- The only index available is the Clustered Index on Name.
-- Since the query filters by Salary, SQL Server
-- cannot directly seek using the Name index.
-- Therefore, it may need to scan the Clustered Index
-- to find Salary = 5000.
-- This can appear as a Clustered Index Scan.
Select * From Employees Where Salary = 5000

--=========================================================
-- 2. NON-CLUSTERED INDEX
--========================================================= 

-- Re-Create Table Employees
-- Table Employee Has Clustered index on Id ONLY 

-- Filter With Name 
-- Index Scan 
Select Id , Name
From Employees
Where Name = 'Ahmed'

-- Add Non Clustered index on Name 

Create NONCLUSTERED INDEX IXN_Employees_Name
ON Employees(Name)

-- Filter With Name And Select Id and Name
-- Index Seek 
Select Id , Name
From Employees
Where Name = 'Ahmed'

-- Filter With Name And Select Id , Name And Salary 
-- Index Scan 

Select Id , Name , Salary
From Employees

-- Add Non Clustered index on Name Include Salary 

Create NONCLUSTERED INDEX IXN_Employees_Salary
ON Employees(Salary)


-- Filter With Name And Select Id , Name And Salary 
-- Index Seek 

Select Id , Name , Salary
From Employees
Where Name = 'Ahmed'

-- Filter With Salary And Select Id , Name And Salary

[@00:45|t=45] Triggers ROUTE A Trigger is a special kind of stored procedure that runs automatically when an event happens. You never call it with EXEC. CHARACTERISTICS Fires automatically on an event, e.g. INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. Cannot be executed manually. Fires once per statement, not once per row, so it must handle many rows. Runs inside the same transaction: an error in the trigger can roll back the change. Used for auditing, validation, and keeping related data in sync. .NET Track TYPES BY EVENT Type DML DDL Logon Type AFTER 1 FOR INSTEAD OF Fires on INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE CREATE, ALTER, DROP A user logs in DMI- TRIGGERS: WHEN DO THEY RUN? Runs After the statement succeeds Instead of the statement Defined on Table or view Database or server Server Defined on Tables only Tables or views FOR and AFTER are the same thing. Runs inside the same transaction: an error in the trigger can roll back the change. Used for auditing, validation, and keeping related data in sync. .NET Track TYPES BY EVENT Type DML DDL Logon Type AFTER 1 FOR INSTEAD OF Fires on INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE CREATE, ALTER, DROP A user logs in DML TRIGGERS: WHEN DO THEY RUN? Runs After the statement succeeds Instead of the statement Defined on Table or view Database or server Server Defined on Tables only Tables or views FOR and AFTER are the same thing. This session focuses on DML triggers. Talking: Route Academy

[@00:00|t=0] The inserted and deleted Tables What Are They? e inserted and deleted are virtual tables that exist only inside a DML trigger, while it runs. They have the same columns as the table the trigger is on. They hold only the affected rows, which can be many rows. e They are read-only: you can SELECT from them and JOIN them, but you cannot change them. .NET Track When Are They Filled? Operation INSERT DELETE UPDATE inserted New rows Empty New values (after update) ROUTE deleted Empty Deleted rows Old values (before update) An UPDATE is like a DELETE of the old row + an INSERT of the new row, so it fills both tables. Talking: Route Academy

[@12:00|t=720] Triggers — Important Notes BEST PRACTICES Write set-based code: JOIN with inserted / deleted . Never assume only one row changed. e Keep triggers short and fast: they run inside the user's transaction. e Don't return result sets (SELECT) from a trigger. Write to an audit table instead. UPDATE(Column) tells you if a column was in the SET list of the UPDATE. Triggers are "hidden" logic: document them so others know they exist. .NET Track ROUTE MANAGE TRIGGERS - turn a trigger off / on DISABLE TRIGGER ON Employees; ENABLE TRIGGER t ON Employees; - change or delete a trigger ALTER TRIGGER trg_Emptoyee_Audit_Insert DROP TRIGGER t In SSMS: Object Explorer — Tables Employees — Triggers. [@00:45|t=45] Index ROUTE An Index is a database object that helps SQL Server find rows quickly, like the index at the back of a book, instead of reading the whole table. WHY USE INDEXES? speeds up SELECT queries: filtering (WHERE), joining (JOIN) and sorting (ORDER BY). SQL Server reads fewer pages to answer the guery. Can enforce uniqueness (unique index). Kept up to date automatically on every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE. Without an index, SQL Server reads every row (table scan). USE Hospital;
GO

--============================================================
-- VIEWS
--============================================================
--============================================================
-- 1. SIMPLE VIEW
--============================================================
--------------------------------------------------------------
-- Example 1: Create a view to display basic patient information
--------------------------------------------------------------
-- A view is a virtual table based on a SELECT statement.
-- View Cannot Accept Any Parameters !

-- This view exposes only the columns we need from the Patients table.

Create Or Alter View VW_PatientBasicInfo
AS
	Select Id , Name , DOB , WardId
	From Patients


-- Retrieve data from the view just like querying a table.
Select Id , Name From VW_PatientBasicInfo
Select * From VW_PatientBasicInfo


--============================================================
-- VIEW DEFINITION / SOURCE CODE
--============================================================

-- sp_helptext displays the definition (source code) of the view.

Exec sp_helptext 'VW_PatientBasicInfo'

--============================================================
-- ENCRYPT THE VIEW DEFINITION
--============================================================
-- WITH ENCRYPTION hides the source code of the view.
-- After encryption, the view still works normally,
-- but its definition cannot be displayed using sp_helptext.

Create Or Alter View VW_PatientBasicInfoSecure
With Encryption
AS
	Select Id , Name , DOB , WardId
	From Patients


-- Try to retrieve the source code again.
Exec sp_helptext 'VW_PatientBasicInfoSecure'



-- Expected result:
-- The text for object 'vw_PatientBasicInformation' is encrypted.


--============================================================
-- Example 2: Create a view for patients assigned to a ward
--============================================================

-- This view displays only patients whose WardId is NOT NULL.
-- In other words, the patient must be assigned to a ward.

Create or Alter View VW_PatientsAssignedToWards
With Encryption
AS
	Select Id PatientId , Name PatientName , DOB , WardId
	From Patients
	Where WardId IS NOT NULL


-- Display the rows currently visible through the view.
Select * From VW_PatientsAssignedToWards

--============================================================
-- INSERT THROUGH A VIEW
--============================================================

-- A simple view can sometimes be modified directly.
-- Here, we insert a new patient through the view.

INSERT INTO VW_PatientsAssignedToWards (PatientId , PatientName , DOB)
Values (501 , 'Hossam MOstafa' , '2000-01-01')


Select * From VW_PatientsAssignedToWards

-- The INSERT succeeds because the view is updatable.
-- However, the new patient has WardId = NULL.
--
-- Therefore, the row is inserted into the base table (Patients),
-- but it does NOT appear in the view because the view contains:
--
--     WHERE WardId IS NOT NULL

-- Verify whether the new row appears in the view.


--============================================================
-- WITH CHECK OPTION
--============================================================
-- WITH CHECK OPTION prevents INSERT/UPDATE operations
-- through the view if the resulting row does not satisfy
-- the view's WHERE condition.


Create or Alter View VW_PatientsAssignedToWards
With Encryption
AS
	Select Id PatientId , Name PatientName , DOB , WardId
	From Patients
	Where WardId IS NOT NULL
	WITH CHECK OPTION

INSERT INTO VW_PatientsAssignedToWards (PatientId , PatientName , DOB , WardId)
Values (503 , 'Ali Ahmed' , '2000-01-01' , 2)

-- This INSERT will fail because WardId is NULL.
--
-- The new row would not satisfy:
--     WHERE WardId IS NOT NULL
--
-- WITH CHECK OPTION prevents this operation.


-- Expected result:
-- The attempted insert or update failed because the target view
-- specifies WITH CHECK OPTION and the resulting row does not
-- qualify for the view.


--============================================================
-- 2. COMPLEX VIEW
--============================================================
--------------------------------------------------------------
-- Example 1: Display every patient together with their ward name
--------------------------------------------------------------
-- This view combines data from two tables using INNER JOIN.
-- Patients contains the patient information.
-- Wards contains the ward information.
-- The result shows:    PatientId    PatientName     WardName

Create Or Alter View VW_PatientWithWards
With Encryption
AS
	Select P.Id PatientID , P.Name PatientName , W.Name WardName
	From Patients P Join Wards W
	ON P.WardId = W.Id



-- Display all patients together with their ward information.
-- A view can also be filtered like a normal table.
-- Here, display only patients assigned to Cardiology.
Select * From VW_PatientWithWards
Where WardName = 'Cardiology'


--============================================================
-- INSERT THROUGH A COMPLEX VIEW
--============================================================

-- A view based on a JOIN may still be updatable in some cases.
--
-- The INSERT below attempts to insert data through the view.
-- SQL Server may insert the data into the underlying table
-- if the view remains updatable.


Insert INTO VW_PatientWithWards (PatientID , PatientName)
Values (600 , 'Mohamed Ali')

--
-- However, DOB is NOT NULL in the Patients table.
-- Therefore, this INSERT fails because DOB is not provided.



-- Expected result:
-- Cannot insert the value NULL into column 'DOB'.


--------------------------------------------------------------
-- Example 2: Display the number of drugs administered to each patient
--------------------------------------------------------------
-- GROUP BY is used to create one row per patient. COUNT(PatientId) counts how many drug administration records  belong to each patient.

Create or Alter View VW_CountOfDAPatients
With Encryption
AS
	Select PatientId , COUNT(*) CountOfDA
	From DrugAdministrations
	Group By PatientId


-- Display the number of drug administrations for each patient.
Select * From VW_CountOfDAPatients




-- This view cannot be directly modified because it contains
-- GROUP BY and an aggregate function (COUNT).
--
-- Therefore, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations are not allowed
-- directly through this view.

-- VIEW PARTIAL Update

--============================================================
-- 3. INDEXED VIEW
--============================================================
--------------------------------------------------------------
-- Example 1: Create an indexed view for consultant information
--------------------------------------------------------------
-- An indexed view stores the result of the view physically
-- after creating an index on it.

--
-- SCHEMABINDING creates a dependency between the view
-- and the underlying table structure.
--
-- The referenced table must use two-part names:
--     dbo.Consultants
--     Id, Name, Salary


Create Or Alter View dbo.VW_IndexedConsultantsView
WITH SCHEMABINDING
AS
	Select Id , Name , Salary
	From dbo.Consultants
	Where Salary IS NOT NULL

Select * From dbo.VW_IndexedConsultantsView

--============================================================
-- CREATE THE FIRST INDEX
--============================================================

-- The first index on an indexed view MUST be
-- a UNIQUE CLUSTERED INDEX.
Create Unique Clustered Index IX_VW_IndexedConsultantsView
ON dbo.VW_IndexedConsultantsView(Id)

--
-- The unique clustered index physically materializes
-- the view's result.



-- The view can now be queried normally.
Select * From dbo.VW_IndexedConsultantsView
Where Id = 301


--============================================================
-- EXAMPLE 2: INDEXED VIEW WITH GROUP BY
--============================================================

-- COUNT_BIG() is required instead of COUNT()
-- when creating an indexed view that contains GROUP BY.

Create or Alter View dbo.VW_IndexedConsultantPatientsCount
With Schemabinding
AS
	Select ConsultantId , COUNT_BIG(*) PatientCount
	From dbo.PatientConsultantAssignments
	Group By ConsultantId

-- Create the required UNIQUE CLUSTERED INDEX. ConsultantId identifies each group in the view, so it is used as the unique key.

Create UNIQUE Clustered Index IX_PatientConsiltant
ON dbo.VW_IndexedConsultantPatientsCount(ConsultantId)

-- Display the indexed view.
Select ConsultantId , PatientCount
From dbo.VW_IndexedConsultantPatientsCount
Where ConsultantId = 305

--============================================================
-- ADDING A NONCLUSTERED INDEX TO AN INDEXED VIEW
--============================================================

-- After creating the required UNIQUE CLUSTERED INDEX,
-- we can create additional nonclustered indexes.
--
-- This can improve performance when searching or filtering
-- by other columns in the indexed view.

--------------------------------------------------------------
-- Example: Create an index on PatientCount
--------------------------------------------------------------
Create NonClustered Index IX_VW_IndexedConsultantPatientsCount_PatientCount
ON dbo.VW_IndexedConsultantPatientsCount(PatientCount)
--============================================================
-- DROPPING A VIEW
--============================================================

-- DROP VIEW permanently removes the view definition.
-- IF EXISTS prevents an error if the view does not exist.
Drop View IF Exists VW_CountOfDAPatients

--============================================================
-- TCL [TRANSACTION CONTROL LANGUAGE]
--============================================================

-- A transaction groups one or more statements into
-- a single unit of work.
--
-- COMMIT permanently saves the changes.
-- ROLLBACK cancels the changes made in the transaction.


--============================================================
-- COMMIT TRANSACTION
--============================================================

Begin Transaction
	Update Patients
	SET Name = 'Hossam Ahmed'
	Where Id = 201
COMMIT Transaction -- Save Changes

--============================================================
-- ROLLBACK TRANSACTION
--============================================================

Begin Transaction
	Update Patients
	SET Name = 'Test'
	Where Id = 201
	-- Cancel Any Change
	-- Patient Original Name Will Be Restored
ROLLBACK Transaction


--============================================================
-- TRANSACTION WITH SAVEPOINT AND TRY / CATCH
--============================================================
--------------------------------------------------------------
-- Example: Update multiple patients and use a SAVEPOINT
--------------------------------------------------------------
-- A SAVEPOINT allows us to rollback only part of a transaction.
--
-- In this example:
--
-- 1. Update Patient 201.
-- 2. Create a SAVEPOINT.
-- 3. Update Patient 208.
-- 4. Rollback to the SAVEPOINT.
-- 5. The update to Patient 208 is undone.
-- 6. The update to Patient 201 is kept.
-- 7. COMMIT saves the remaining changes.

Begin Try
Begin Transaction
-- 1. Update Patient 201.
	Update Patients
	Set WardId = 2
	Where Id = 201
-- 2. Create a SAVEPOINT.
	SAVE Transaction PatientOneUpdate
-- 3. Update Patient 208.
	Update Patients
	Set WardId = 3
	Where Id = 208
-- 4. Rollback to the SAVEPOINT.
	ROLLBACK Transaction PatientOneUpdate

	COMMIT Transaction
End Try
Begin Catch

	IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0
		ROLLBACK Transaction
	Select
		ERROR_NUMBER() as ErrorNumber,
		ERROR_MESSAGE() as ErrorMessage

End Catch

[@00:45|t=45] ACID Properties ROUTE ACID is four rules that every transaction follows. Together they keep the data correct, even when errors or crashes happen. Atomicity All or nothing. Every statement succeeds, or none of them is applied. A transfer never takes money without giving it. O .NET Track c Consistency Rules are always respected. Data moves from one valid state to another. A balance can never become negative. Isolation Transactions do not disturb each other while they run at the same time. Others do not see your unfinished changes. D Durability Committed data is never lost, even after a crash or power cut. After COMMIT the change survives a restart. Talking: Route Academy

[S76] Exercise #4 | LINQ · Mini Exercises | EXERCISE 4 OF | 8 | var | numbers = | new | [] { | 1 | , | 2 | , | 3 | }; | dynamic | d = numbers; | d[ | 0 | ] = | "Hello" | ; | Console | . | WriteLine | (numbers[ | 0 | ]); | ❓ What is the output? | 💥 | Runtime Error! | RuntimeBinderException | It | compiles | (dynamic skips checks), but at runtime the array is | int[] | — can't store strings!
[S77] Exercise #5 | LINQ · Mini Exercises | EXERCISE 5 OF | 8 | var | numbers = | new | List | < | int | > { | 1 | , | 2 | , | 3 | }; | var | query = numbers. | Where | (n => n > | 1 | ); | numbers. | Add | ( | 4 | ); | Console | . | WriteLine | ( | string | . | Join | ( | ", " | , query)); | ❓ What is the output? | ✅ Output: | 2, 3, 4 | Query is NOT executed when defined! | numbers.Add(4) | modifies the source. When | string.Join | iterates → query runs NOW with {1,2,3,4}.
[S78] Exercise # | 6 | LINQ · Mini Exercises | EXERCISE | 6 | OF | 8 | var | data = | new | List | < | List | < | int | >> { | new | List | < | int | > { | 1 | , | 2 | }, | new | List | < | int | > { | 3 | , | 4 | } | }; | var | result = data. | Select | (x => x); | Console | . | WriteLine | (result. | Count | ()); | ❓ What is the output? | ✅ Output: | 2 | (NOT 4!) | Select(x => x) | returns each inner list as-is → still 2 lists. Need | SelectMany | to flatten and get 4 items.
[S79] Exercise # | 7 | LINQ · Mini Exercises | EXERCISE | 7 | OF | 8 | var | items = | new | [] { | new | { Name = | " | A | " | , Value = | 2 | }, | new | { Name = | " | C | " | , Value = | 1 | }, | new | { Name = | " | B | " | , Value = | 3 | } | }; | var | result = items. | OrderBy | (x => x.Name). | OrderBy | (x => x.Value); | foreach | ( | var | r | in | result) | Console | . | Write | (r.Name + | " " | ); | ❓ What is the output? | ✅ Output: | C A B | (sorted by Value only!) | Second | OrderBy | replaces | the first! Items sorted by Value (1,2,3). To sort by Name THEN Value: | .OrderBy(x => x.Name).ThenBy(x => x.Value)
[S80] Exercise # | 8 | LINQ · Mini Exercises | EXERCISE | 8 | OF | 8 | var | numbers = | new | List | < | int | > { | 1 | , | 2 | , | 3 | , | 4 | , | 5 | }; | numbers. | Where | (n => n > | 3 | ); | Console | . | WriteLine | ( | string | . | Join | ( | ", " | , numbers)); | ❓ What is the output? | ✅ Output: | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 | (unchanged!) | Where() | returns a NEW sequence — it doesn't modify the original! The result was not stored anywhere. Fix: | var filtered = numbers.Where(n => n > 3).ToList();

product's name and price. 
 
2.​Get a list of only the product names from ProductList. Print 
each name. 
 
3.​Sort all products by UnitPrice (ascending). Print each 
product's name and price. 
 
4.​Get all products where UnitPrice is between 10 and 30​
 
5.​Get all products that are in stock (UnitsInStock > 0) and 
belong to the "Condiments" category. 
 
6.​Create a new anonymous type with three properties: 
●​Name → the product name 
●​Price → the unit price 
●​StockStatus → a string: "Available" if UnitsInStock > 0, 
otherwise "Out of Stock" 
●​Print the result.

original array.

1.​Get top 3 most expensive products 
2.​show page 2 of products, with page size = 5 
3.​Take products from the list as long as Their UnitPrice is less than 
$25 (list is ordered by price). 
4.​Check if ALL products in the "Seafood" category are in stock 
5.​Check if the ID list contains 9 
int[] ids = { 3, 9, 13, 18 }; 
6.​Group all products by Category and print each group  with its 
product count. 
7.​Group products by Category and project only product names  per 
group 
8.​Find all categories that have MORE THAN 3 products 
9.​Using QUERY SYNTAX, group customers by Country, and for  each 
group select { Country, Count, TotalOrderValue }. 
10.​ Calculate the total number of units in stock across all products 
11.​ Find the CHEAPEST and MOST EXPENSIVE product prices 
12.​ Get a distinct list of all product categories 
13.​ find product IDs that are in setA but NOT in setB 
int[] setA = { 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 };      
int[] setB = { 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 13 };

(case-insensitive). 
string[] list1 = { "Germany", "France", "UK", "Spain" }; 
string[] list2 = { "france", "SPAIN", "Italy" }; 
 
15.​ Build a Dictionary<int, Product> keyed by ProductID. Then 
retrieve and print the product with ID = 18.

19.​ Generate even numbers between 1 and 30. 
20.​ Concatenate the first 3 product names with the first  3 
customer company names into a single sequence.

a string "ProductName sold to CompanyName".

Session 01
CASE STUDY: BOOKSTOREYou are hired as a junior developer at "ReadMore Books", a small bookstore that 
needs a simple database system. The owner explains: "We need to track our book 
inventory - each book has a title, ISBN number, price, number of pages, the year 
it was published, and whether it's currently in stock. We also want to keep 
information about the authors we work with, including their first and last names, 
email addresses, a short biography, and their date of birth. Finally, we organize 
our books into different categories - each category has a name, description, and 
we need to know if the category is still active or not."
Requirements: 
1. Create a Console Application using Entity Framework Core
2. Use EF Core CONVENTIONS ONLY 
3. Use Sql Server as the database provider
4. Identify and create the necessary entities from the case study
5. Create an appropriate DbContext class
6. Demonstrate that the database is created correctly

[S01] SESSION 01 | EF Core | Entity Framework Core — Architecture & Setup | .NET Track
[S02] Session Agenda | EF Core · Session 01 | 01 | What is an ORM? | Object-Relational Mapping, the mapping concept, | table ⇄ class | 02 | EF Core | Architecture & query processing, DbContext, | Database First vs Code First, providers | 03 | Configuration & Migrations | Conventions, the migration lifecycle | & PMC commands | 04 | Data Annotations | [Key], [Required], [MaxLength], [Table], | [NotMapped] & more | 05 | Mini Exercises
[S03] SECTION 01 | What is an ORM? | Working with the database using objects — instead of raw SQL strings | 01
[S04] What is an ORM? | EF Core · What is an ORM? | ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) | lets you work with the database using | objects | . It maps | tables → C# classes | and | rows → objects | . | 1 | Without an ORM — raw SQL | var | sql = | "SELECT Id, Name, Email FROM Users WHERE Id = @id" | ; | using | var | cmd = | new | SqlCommand | (sql, connection); | cmd. | Parameters | . | AddWithValue | ( | "@id" | , userId); | using | var | reader = cmd. | ExecuteReader | (); | if | (reader. | Read | ()) | { | var | user = | new | User | { | Id | = reader. | GetInt32 | ( | 0 | ), | Name | = reader. | GetString | ( | 1 | ), | Email | = reader. | GetString | ( | 2 | ) | }; | } | ❌ SQL inside | strings | , manual mapping by | column index | — errors are found at runtime. | 2 | With EF Core — clean & type-safe | // One line — EF Core writes the SQL | var | user = | await | _context. | Users | . | FindAsync | (userId); | // Or with LINQ | var | user = | await | _context. | Users | . | Where | (u => u. | Id | == userId) | . | FirstOrDefaultAsync | (); | ✅ No SQL strings, no manual mapping — the compiler checks your query and EF Core builds the | User | object for you.

CASE STUDY: EventHub
EventHub is a platform that allows individuals and companies to organize, promote, and 
manage public and private events.
When a person or a company decides to host events through the platform, they first register 
as an organizer by providing their name and, if applicable, the name of the company they 
represent.
The platform assigns each organizer a verified status after completing an internal review 
process. Alongside their account, every organizer maintains a public-facing profile page 
where they can write a short biography, link to their personal or company website, and 
upload a logo.
This profile page is directly tied to the organizer’s account and cannot exist without it.
Once their account is set up, an organizer can publish events on the platform. Every event 
carries a title, a detailed description, a start date, an optional end date, and a maximum 
number of attendees allowed.
People who wish to attend events join the platform as attendees. Each attendee provides 
their full name, an email address, and a home address that includes a street, city, country, 
and postal code, used for correspondence purposes. The platform can issue an attendee a 
badge — a credential uniquely numbered per attendee, stamped with the date it was 
issued, and assigned a tier: either Standard or VIP.
A badge belongs to one attendee, and each attendee can have at most one badge.
Task:
Implement a full EF Core console app with all entity classes, a DbContext, and 
OnModelCreating fully configured.
Configure the relationships between the entities:
●
Organizer and OrganizerProfile: One-to-One.
●
Organizer and Event: One-to-Many.
●
Attendee and Badge: One-to-One.
Each entity must be configured using one technique only — do not mix techniques on 
the same entity.
Organizer and Attendee: use Data Annotations with these rules:
●
Maximum lengths: organizer name 100 and company name 150; attendee full name 150, 
email 200, street 150, city 100, country 100 and postal code 20.
1
[P02] ●
Required: the organizer name, and the attendee full name, email, street, city, country 
and postal code. The company name is optional.
●
The table of Organizer is named EventOrganizers.
●
The attendee postal code is stored in a column named ZipCode.
●
Attendee has a read-only FullAddress property (street, city, country and postal code 
in one text) that must NOT become a column.
OrganizerProfile, Event and Badge: use the Fluent API, either directly in 
OnModelCreating or in separate configuration classes. Use each of these two ways at 
least once.

Once their account is set up, an organizer can publish events on the platform. Every event 
carries a title, a detailed description, a start date, an optional end date, and a maximum 
number of attendees allowed.
People who wish to attend events join the platform as attendees. Each attendee provides 
their full name, an email address, and a home address that includes a street, city, country, 
and postal code, used for correspondence purposes. The platform can issue an attendee a 
badge — a credential uniquely numbered per attendee, stamped with the date it was 
issued, and assigned a tier: either Standard or VIP.
A badge belongs to one attendee, and each attendee can have at most one badge.
Task:
Implement a full EF Core console app with all entity classes, a DbContext, and 
OnModelCreating fully configured.
Configure the relationships between the entities:
●
Organizer and OrganizerProfile: One-to-One.
●
Organizer and Event: One-to-Many.
●
Attendee and Badge: One-to-One.
Each entity must be configured using one technique only — do not mix techniques on 
the same entity.
Organizer and Attendee: use Data Annotations with these rules:
●
Maximum lengths: organizer name 100 and company name 150; attendee full name 150, 
email 200, street 150, city 100, country 100 and postal code 20.

The entity class stays a clean | POCO | — no attributes, no EF Core references. | Method | Purpose | ToTable() | Table name | HasKey() | Primary key (incl. composite) | Property() | Pick a property to configure | IsRequired() | NOT NULL | HasMaxLength() | nvarchar(n) | HasColumnName() | Column name | HasColumnType() | Exact SQL type | HasDefaultValue() | Default value | HasDefaultValueSql() | Default from SQL, e.g. | GETDATE() | Ignore() | Not mapped

Move each entity's Fluent API into its own class with | IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> | . | 1  One class per entity | public | class | ProductConfiguration | : | IEntityTypeConfiguration | < | Product | > | { | public | void | Configure | ( | EntityTypeBuilder | < | Product | > builder) | { | builder. | ToTable | ( | "Products" | ); | builder. | HasKey | (p => p. | Id | ); | builder. | Property | (p => p. | Name | ) | . | IsRequired | () | . | HasMaxLength | ( | 100 | ); | builder. | HasOne | (p => p. | Category | ) | . | WithMany | (c => c. | Products | ) | . | HasForeignKey | (p => p. | CategoryId | ); | } | } | 2  Register in the DbContext | protected | override | void | OnModelCreating | ( | ModelBuilder | modelBuilder) | { | // one by one | modelBuilder. | ApplyConfiguration | ( | new | ProductConfiguration | ()); | // or ALL configuration classes in the assembly | modelBuilder. | ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly | ( | typeof | ( | AppDbContext | ). | Assembly | ); | } | 💡 | ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly | scans the project — add a new configuration class and it's picked up automatically.
